analysis.name: Jason Azoulay
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The other class has insane curves. They get half credit back on every q they get wrong while we just get cooked. How is this fair? Even exam 1, class avg in the other class was like 50ish while ours was 60 smth. yet they got at least half credit back while we got nothing.

Wasn't an amazing lecturer— sometimes it felt like he cared more about his lab than the class especially when he would bring it up super often but he was really nice and his TA is amazing and carries the class for sure. Super accessible out of class though, and has a ton of extra credit. Definitely not a bad person, just not the best at lecturing.

He prepares us well for tests with homeworks and practice tests, which are representative of the real tests. If you don't understand a concept, speak to him after class or in office hours, or speak to a TA. This can be a tough class, but the people that complain are the ones usually not showing up to class every time.

He was generally chill and has awesome TAs. Likes to read straight off the PowerPoint slides in lecture. Exams were very straightforward and what we were prepared for. Grading scheme sucks compared to other professors, so you might get screwed over compared to other available sections.

Absolute goat of organic chemistry. Very nice and always gives extensions or corrects prs points if it's not working. Tests are very fair and doable. Lectures do lack the level of detail we get tested on but honestly if you actually study you'll be ok. Great professor overall and he's very chill.

analysis.name: Cyrus Aidun
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Lectures are good time for sleeping. He compensates his incompetence in teaching by grading generously. Easy A.

Dr. Aidun is a decent pick for fluids. The class is hard and he goes over practice that is mostly applicable to the tests, but lectures can tend to get boring. With the proper focus, an A is very doable as the test grading is slightly on the gracious side. I took it in the spring and an A actually ended up being a 91+...

Can't ask questions during exam, only at beginning. No calculators. Explained concepts well in class with plenty of examples and grades generously. Curved the class down(??) Extra credit by computer project that adds 10 points onto final grade, nearly impossible to get all 10. Start early as soon as he releases, it takes more than a week to finish.

Dr. Aidun's lectures provided us with great notes even though lectures were not always the most engaging. Your grade is basically made up of just tests. I did well by putting the notes slides in my crib sheet, but I am not sure I actually learned the concepts. The cutoffs for A, B, etc. are decided at the end of the semester (they could go up!)

He's a really good professor! Class was a little boring but he makes up for that by being a REALLY generous grader. Extra credit offered. The final was optional. Exams based on textbook and homework. Accessible outside of class and really cares about you making a good grade. I would know I started the semester failing lol. Best option for Fluids!

analysis.name: Amanda Stockton
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Stockton is one of the best professors I have had! She is hardworking, cares about her students, and wants you to succeed. She is so passionate about the material that it makes you excited to learn. Although she is busy, she tries to make time to help her students and even does online office hours. Her lecture notes are fantastic! Recommend!!!!

Stockton is a kind and funny person and an alright lecturer. With the grade redemption opportunities on the test (half credit back on every question) it's hard to do poorly in this class. If you ever need extensions or help message and she is very helpful.

Very knowledgable, good slides. Makes analytical easy. Prone to moving class online with little notice. Offers corrections to earn 1/2 points back on missed exam questions. Will sit with you one-on-one for hours until you understand, will help you even on the weekend or at 8pm before exam. Very passionate, can go off on tangents. No real complaints

Not a bad professor: very knowledgeable, just frustrating sometimes with poor communication (cancelling class or moving it online last minute, unclear deadlines, last minute changes in homework, doesn't really respond to emails/Teams) and going on tangents getting super far behind in lecture. She does provide a lot of resources, it's an easy class.
Very nice professor who's very engaged with the material. TAs review sessions are also a saving grace for midterms

analysis.name: Akanksha Menon
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The professor was really engaging in lectures, but the tests are HARD. I took this Fall 2025 and got an A but for a grad level class, there were a lot of Bs and Cs in the final distribution. Expect to work hard but I enjoyed the learning experience overall and learned a lot.

Great professor that ACTUALLY listens to her students. She has decent lectures and slides (they help when supplemented with the textbook) and is very organized. The class keeps you busy with multiple assignments but so do other ME 3345 sections. I really don't get the other comments that speak ill of Dr. Menon. Don't hate the player hate the game.

Most of the heat transfer professors at Tech are terrible, Professor Menon is still difficult (it's a difficult class), but is an incredible professor. Her exams are extremely fair, homework isn't too intense, and lectures are very well made. Go to class and do all the practice she tells you, and it'll 100% pay off.
Just don't take her. Trust me. Your life will suck.

analysis.name: Arnold Schneider
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 47 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Did not care about his students - wrote chicken scratch notes for every lecture that were based off accounting text books. Talks way too fast and writes so quickly/poorly, that it is just better to read the textbooks. Exams are extremely difficult and practice problems were not representative of biomedical engineering applications. Avoid Avoid!!!

Class time purely goes over examples from the book - don't expect to go into lectures and actually learn anything, the expectation is that class time clarifies what you've already learned. 

In class he reflects his hand-writing on screen and its awfully scratchy - it's incredibly hard to read and follow along. 

Terribly downgrade from Deby

Mr. Schneider knows accounting very well and ask lots of questions during class to get class participation, but I could never participate unless I read the chapters before hand.  Its all about working problems.  The material isn't hard but its not an easy A.  He isn't very eager to answer questions and can often be condescending.

Lectures somehow go too fast and too slow at the same time. He handwrites notes in class. Its supposed to line up with the textbook (that he wrote himself) but he jumps around like crazy and doesn't even cover everything in the chapter. Reading the textbook is equally difficult. Nothing is clear and practice problems don't have answers. Avoid avoid

This professor wasn't as bad as the reviews made him out to be. He's ok. lectures are kinda boring but he gives extra credit. Your final grade is based on tests and homework, there aren't any projects or anything like that. You get a cheat sheet on the tests. He grades pretty easy and gives partial credit where he can.

analysis.name: Aibek Musaev
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 165 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: How can I begin to describe this class? Professor Musaev is hands-down one of the best professors I've ever laid my eyes on at Tech. I'm only 3 weeks into the course, but I've already learned so much about what I don't want to become in the future: a CS 2340 professor!

I honestly don't understand all the bad reviews. He is a nice professor and does a good job teaching concepts. Most students tend to just blame the professor whenever they struggle lol. Go to class, ask questions, and practice and you will be good. HWs are long and suck though.

Biggest troll I have encountered in my ed career. Copies slides from textbook & codes demos super fast. Instead of lecture read his slides, do slide practices & read textbook if stuck. TAs are amazing for HW help & explaining concepts. Start HW early. Teaches surface level of content to have time to ask riddles & gets mad if you know the answer.

Lectures weren't paced great - introductions to concepts went too slow and coding examples went too fast to retain anything. I personally struggled going in unfamiliar with java. Had coding homeworks due every week that would take a few hours. Exams were also weighted very heavily that focused a lot on theory over actual coding.

What professor you take doesn't really matter in this course (idk if there's even multiple options). This guy seems alright though. The course itself is a decent amount of busy work and lecture attendance is required, but otherwise its chill.

analysis.name: Anna Ivanova
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: You need to attend lectures or watch the recordings to understand content since the slides can't really stand alone. There's 2 open note exams and then weekly open note quizzes. The questions can be tricky-ish but if you attend and listen to lectures it's easy! We also had written assignments that are lengthy but easy. Really cool content though!

Anna is really knowledgeable with the course topics, but it can be hard to follow along in lecture sometimes due to either the content being confusing without enough prior knowledge or the disorganization and lack of clarity on the notes slides. Lecture recordings and everything being open notes makes it easy to do okay in the class, though.

LOTS of EC offered, if you do it easy to get an A. Open-internet tests but info is obscure and difficult to find online/slides. Best to transcribe lecture notes. Dr. Ivanova is extremely knowledgable but was unapproachable and unfriendly in office hours. I really liked the head TA Will. Fun, easy, but lengthy assignments make up majority of grade.

professor ivanova was great! she's a great lecturer, and the class is really interesting. there's only two exams (midterm and final), about 11 quizzes (you can drop one), and four assignments with extra credit opportunity. all the exams/quizzes are open note, so as long as you go to/watch lecture, you'll have a very easy time in this class!

Very interesting class, and Dr. Ivanova clearly knew a lot about it! While attendance isn't mandatory and everything is posted online, weekly quizzes mean you cannot get behind in the class. However, everything is open note so as long as you listen to the lectures and complete the assignments, I didn't find the assessments hard.

analysis.name: Antonio Cardentey
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Expect to participate 1-2 times each class, and make sure you're doing the weekly assignments and readings since those same topics will be brought up during lecture to be discussed. Really enjoyed the times I got to speak with native speakers around the world for 30 minutes, and learn more about their lives while also improving my Spanish.

Dr. Cardentey's sheer knowledge and clear passion for the subject matter were refreshing. You could tell throughout the course that he truly wanted his students to understand the nuances of the region through sci-fi, as it would improve us as students across all of our various majors. Truly recommend!

I took this course online, and it was great. Because there were no in-person lectures, we had to do 50-minute weekly Zoom conversations with small groups, but they were pretty low-stress. Dr. Cardentey gives great feedback and his class has helped me fine-tune my Spanish skills. He is also very caring and flexible. Definitely recommend!

Dr. Cardentey was extremely knowledgeable about all of the course material and was extremely interesting and enthusiastic in his lectures in class. This always made me excited to come to class and I feel like I learnt the most in the class, compared to the numerous other Spanish courses I've taken thus far at Georgia Tech.

prof cardentey is amazing! almost all assignments are collaborative, and i left the class feeling way more confident in my speaking skills. 10/10 would take this class again and would recommend to anyone taking spanish at tech!!

analysis.name: Abrahim Ladha
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 174 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: I think Ladha is a chill guy. However, it's pretty clear that the expectations of the course don't really align with the reality. I don't think the exams are fairly written and there should be, at the very least, an exam drop for this class (like other CS2050). The TAs need less power though; they practically run the course and not in a good way.

Take if you are 100% sure that you will attend all lectures + solve all homework + all practice problems + spend a lot of time trying to combine your knowledge from the lectures with the extremely difficult practice problems, and expect even more "creative", harder questions to appear on your exam. You need to practice as if this is your only class

Why is this called an intro class. Homeworks take min 6 hrs a week, TAs cant help much, it's too hard. Test reviews are so useless from TAs. If you get a C on 1 exam, no chance of an A.

He's a nice guy, content itself isn't even really that bad, but the class structure is absolutely abysmal. Save yourself the headache and transfer in the credit.

Ladha himself is a good lecturer and a good person. It's his TA's that make the class a nightmare. Just because they went through hell in their semester they think it's their turn to give us hell back. HW's took 6+ hrs per week and exams had singular questions worth 5+% of your COURSE GRADE. Absolutely do not take this class under any circumstances

This class actively regressed my knowledge of discrete mathematics and math as a whole. If God wished to give his strongest warriors a challenge, he would send students to CS2050 Office Hours to face the awful TAs for this class. Such students would emerge Navy SEALs.  Ladha is a terrible lecturer and teaches content that cater to few. Do not take.

analysis.name: Leonardo  Abbrescia
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I thought he is a pretty sold choice for multi, I think he did a good job with including a lot of visuals and simple explanations for concepts. Quizzes and tests were tough but it is not supposed to be an easy class. Use the textbook, practice a lot outside of class, and go to Professor or TA office hours.

One of the better teachers for MATH2551. His exams are generally easier than other teachers, and although his lectures can be boring at times, he is lenient in terms of grading, always looking for areas to give points back. Overall, he is a good teacher. MATH2551 requires effort to grasp some of the concepts, but nonetheless I would take him again.

he's not exactly the most “student” oriented prof, as i think he prefers teaching mainly upper level math majors so teaching a sophomore math gen ed didn't seem up to him. regardless i think he explained topics pretty well and dr lehman's videos could supplement any lectures you missed. wish he had more office hours tho. made tests decently fair

He's a great person, but inexperienced with teaching an underclassman course. He wrote all lecture notes from scratch with questionable handwriting, so I spent most lectures deciphering instead of understanding. He doesn't post note templates; homework content was not tested. I didn't know what I should know for exams until the end of the semester.

tbh I learned mostly from studio, do NOT skip it if ur taking multi it's a lifesaver. Lectures could have been way worse, he's good at introducing topics but usually started losing the class during example probs. i agree that it would have been much MUCH easier if he simply copied the alr typed out notes from dr. lehmann, as his exams were similar

analysis.name: Timothy Brothers
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Best professor I've had. He clearly cares about students and puts effort into teaching. The labs are long and challenging, but they do a great job reinforcing the material and were very helpful at reinforcing material. Exams are fair and closely reflect the course content without being unnecessarily difficult.  (Also he zooms/records lecture)

Brothers is one of my favorite professors I've had at tech so far. 3058 is a very tough class, but I really enjoyed Brothers' lectures. He's incredibly knowledgeable and does a great job explaining concepts. The labs are very time consuming, start early and go to office hours. Tests are open note/open internet but still hard because of time limit

Brothers' computer architecture class has been my favorite class at Tech so far. Very interesting content and great lecture slides. Labs are HARD but they reinforce the lecture content very well and force you to understand the concepts. Exams were take-home Canvas quizzes (40 mins, mostly MC from slides, a few short answer) with an overall curve.

Class content was older and a bit less helpful in that sense, but he presented the information very well and I learned a hell of a lot from the class.  He had some times where he was rather derogatory and kind of feed you to the wolves mindset, but it did pressure me to try hard and learn so it worked. The first labs were hell tho and took forever.

3/5 for the 3011 with brothers, not really for brothers as a teacher. Junior design was a lot more work than I think it should be, but there is an arguement that it's my fault for doing Junior -> senior design path. Has a lot of energy, good vibes.

analysis.name: Ryan Blunck
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 42 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Mythical pull of a professor. He explains the concepts well by relating them to real-world applications, and the example problems are essentially the ones seen on the tests. The tests shouldn't be too difficult if you carefully review the packets and pay attention in class. Someone here said he was like a parental figure, and I fully agree.
Great professor. Lectures are engaging and clear. He clearly cares about his students. Goes question by question when explaining what is going to be on the test. You will not regret taking his class.

He's the best!! He clearly cares about his students and tries his best to make accounting fun. He tells you every problem before the test so just review/memorize the problems from the notes and you will do fine. You don't really need to do the recommended textbook problems and he has videos on the concepts if you miss something in class.

Had this prof for MGT 4026, MGT 4029, and MGT 4043. His classes are straightforward with outlines and lectures videos you can refer back to. I wouldn't really recommend stacking his classes because he puts his exam dates on the same day for all of them.

BEST PROFESSOR AT SCHELLER! If you're considering taking Accounting 2101 with anyone other than Professor Blunck, DON'T. I can't stress enough how amazing he is. He set up his class in a manner that makes it easy for all his students to succeed. Accounting is a difficult subject, but Blunck made it much more digestible.

analysis.name: Rachel Behrmann
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 31 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: She really was invested in what she was teaching and really loves what she does. She also treats students as peers and is engaging. She really made class a very fun enviroment. Tests were a little weird (MC) , but after the first test it was easy to see what she would ask. Overall amazing professor and person (it was ECON 2803)

I can't stress how easy this class with Professor Behrmann is. Attendance is technically mandatory but it's only enforced with participation quizzes that she gives every two lectures. I barely showed up but she uploads extensive notes, and allows you to have a flashcard for the exam. Weekly quizzes are open note and on Canvas, AND, no final.

Prof. Behrmann is awesome. She is super friendly and is extremely passionate about economics. The class is fast-paced and lecture heavy, but the exams are not that difficult. Assigns easy weekly HW quizzes that boost your grade and allows notecard crib sheet for every exam. Overall, I enjoyed taking this class and learned a ton.

Great professor with good lectures. The course itself is a bit challenging if you have never taken economics. The class is also very exam heavy (64% of grade) so slipping up once can mess you up for the whole semester. Overall not too hard or stressful though. Attendance taken only a few times using an access code.

Great professor. Super helpful and willing to answer any questions. You can always go to her office hours for help. Explanations are really good. Weekly quizzes and tests aren't too hard. Participation isn't required most of the time, but other times there are participation checks on canvas. Recommend taking her class!

analysis.name: Bachir El Fil
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Expects students to have 20hrs/week set aside for this class. During exams, it was common to see people crying. The problems were unlike those we went over and were impossible to complete in the given time. Studied for the final for a week, 14hrs/day, and could not complete half of it. HW graded harshly and barely any review material. Ok to reach.

Avoid at all costs. He's a nice guy and cares a lot but his expectations are way to high. Teaches purely conceptual in class and then expects you to learn everything on the homework, which is impossible without a software that he doesn't teach you how to use. Class is 20+ hours of work per week. Tests are abysmal and good luck finishing in time.

Only section that didn't have a take home final, and got the lowest avg on the 2nd exam. The hw's are long, and graded harshly and the lectures are conceptual. I helped other sections study for their finals and their review question were far easier. We got only two review questions per test. Hardest tests I've taken at GT. Caring guy.

This class was by far the most work I have ever done. The homework in this class would take around 12 hours per week, and that is not an overestimate. On the final, there were things that we had never seen before. Teaching-wise, a limited amount of foundational concepts were covered, and you were just thrown into the fire to figure it out.

Extremely hard class, DO NOT TAKE AT ANY COST, don't believe these fake reviews, this class genuinely felt like hell. Homeworks were extremely hard and took almost 20 hours per HW. Exams were similar to HW questions but 5 times harder. Extremely hard class and professor.

analysis.name: Michael Best
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: One of the best professors I have had. Very approachable and genuinely cares about student success.

Listen there aren't enough characters to describe how horrendous this class was, there's 0 structure, his lectures have almost no relevancy to the ridiculous amount of readings he assigned, 50% of our grade occurred in the last 2 weeks. Don't take stia with him. Wait for a different professor. If you're going into ur last semester, stay for 4 1/2.

He is an interesting figure with an interesting career but aside from that, not much recommends him as a good or even decent professor. His readings are adequate but the main problem in the class was his lack of constructive feedback, clear instruction, and preparedness. 60% of class grade was still undetermined by the last week of the semester.

Take this class with P. Brecke. Dr. Best has an ego bigger than any other professor I've ever known and enjoys reminding students how much more he knows. Don't ask too many questions or send a single email, he gets petty quick. and most importantly: Do NOT have a different opinion or belief. Your grade will feel his retribution.

analysis.name: Justin Biddle
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Biddle is a very passionate and interesting lecturer, and the class is pretty discussion-heavy.

Dr. Biddle is NOT accessible outside of class. Does not respond to emails. This sucks because each absence from his class is 2% off final grade and it's hard to communicate. However, class is relatively easy and discussion based. I've learned a lot from his class. I just wish he was more lenient to absences and more responsive. He's cool I guess.

Dr. Biddle is a chill and awesome professor. I would recommend taking his philosophy class. Participation counts and the semester is broken into 3 parts: 1. do reading before class and have discussion on Perusall & have discussions in class, 2. individual essay (some in-class time given), and 3. group essay/presentation (in-class time given).

Dr. Biddle is a great professor and his lectures are interesting and enlightening. His class consists of daily readings and lectures that clarify the author's message. The only graded assignments are weekly pop quizzes to ensure you're actually reading, and take-home essay exams for the midterm/final. Understand the material and you'll do fine.

Prof. Biddle cares about his students, and wants his students to learn. Had to read before each class (1.5 hrs of work) to be able to do his pop quizzes and participate in class (there was no homework). However, pop quizzes are easy - they are very high level. The midterm and final were take-home, and consisted of a few essay questions.

analysis.name: Keagan Callis
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Does not teach well at all, no point in showing up to lectures. Also super disorganized, would never post notes, or announcements. Super hard to reach outside of class, would never respond to emails either. Studio is where I learned everything.

Tbh stopped attending lectured after the first 2 months bc they tend to be very slow and boring. I felt like studios were much more helpful to learn content because we practiced what we learn so attend studios and make sure to do the practice exams that are posted because the exams are pretty much the same questions and format.

He often shows up to class late seemingly in a rush - also seems like he is learning his presentation slides as he goes along. Like he is surprised by what is on them. Gets half of the questions wrong and doesn't have a clear format for how he wants to teach. Get someone else, but 2 hour linear you can somewhat learn on your own. For 1553 not 1552

I went to the first class, and immediately knew it wouldn't be worth going ever again. ADHD, disorganized, doesn't stay on schedule. There are videos posted on Canvas by a much better professor you can just watch instead. Homeworks are very fair, and tests are quite easy. Overall, I would take him again ONLY because lectures weren't mandatory.

terrible unorganized lectures and cannot answer ed discussion/emails to save his life. our section was apparently the easiest tho idk. exams are not horrendous but often harder than his practice exams. quizzes were incredibly unfair and he didn't do much to remediate the consistently failing quiz averages.

analysis.name: Cheng Zhu
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: As other reviews have mentioned, lectures are not helpful. This semester, Dr. Zhu began his unit by saying that he had put the slides into AI to generate AI lectures for us to watch. He noted that some of it is incorrect so we should use our better judgement to know what is right. After 4 lectures, less than a quarter of the class was attending

Decent professor. Cares for his students. Wants his students to understand. One of the best professors that I have in BMED. YOU SHOULD DO ALL THE HW AND THE PRACTICE TESTS!!! HE LIKES TO REPEAT PROBLEMS!!

It's awful. Exams are weighted very heavily and the questions on the exams were not representative of any of the material we were given, especially for the second and final exams.
Quite frankly it sucked. Also very unclear on how the class will be curved and the class needs to be curved since almost everyone had failing grades going into the final.

He is one of the worst professors I have ever taken. He made our test too long on purpose, then told us in an announcement that it was designed not to be finished in our allotted time. His lectures are terrible as he faces the board and lectures to himself. The slide decks have to be downloaded to PowerPoint and rearranged for viewing. Tech BME

Ineffective lectures. The grading schemes for quizzes and tests are not representative of processes taught in class, and zero consistency in what's important to understand. TAs are unhelpful and often misleading. Average on half the assignments was under 40% Never have I felt less control over my grades in a class.

analysis.name: Gerandy Brito
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 154 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Brito's teaching pace is great, and he keeps class very interesting: extremely funny. Sometimes doesn't follow the textbook or slides, but normally his ideas are better and simpler than those presented. Struggled to fall asleep in linear algebra, that's a feat.

I loved this class and Professor Brito. One complaint however is with the TAs. This is the first class where TAs are less approachable than the Professor and this might be due to how the class is structured. Some TAs were really nice and helpful but others TAs (namely one) on Piazza who would demean students constantly with their replies.

Brito is a great professor who clearly has a passion for the material and can keep students engaged. HW seemed like a lot for me but it really helped me learn the material. There is adequate study material for each exam and Brito tries to keep the class as engaging as possible.

Being an easy professor who gives high grades despite failing exams does not translate to being a good professor. He never released homework answers or exam answers or even feedback, just whether it was correct or not. This made doing homework worthless. For the final, he explicitly said specific topics were not on the exam--they were on the exam.

His tests are easier than the other sections, which is big in 1553. His lectures are pretty funny and entertaining, and he's a really nice guy. At first I thought he was going to be really disorganized, but he really knows his stuff and he's pretty good at teaching if you pay attention.

analysis.name: Chi Hoi (Kyle) Yip
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: UNDERRATED PROFESSOR!! We need more profs like him at Tech, he geniunely cares about his students and isn't afraid to adjust his HW/Exams/policies to prioritize fairness for students. Very available to help, he posts about his office hours often and is very helpful even if you are super lost. He isn't trying to trick you, he wants you to do well.

Professor Yip is a very caring and approachable person. His lectures are straightforward, delivering content in a clear, easy-to-understand way. The exam questions are very similar to those in his lectures and on the sample exams. He is always responsive, answering students' questions and addressing their needs.

It is kind of hard to understand his notes but his exams/quizzes are predictable and there is no hw for the class (only quizzes), he gives partial credit on exams and provides practice, the textbook is optional

He's one of the kindest and most organized professors at Georgia Tech. His clear structure made it easy—and genuinely fun—to follow along and learn. He's also very understanding of students' diverse situations. We need more professors like him who truly invest time and effort in teaching.

Professor Yip is a great professor who is not only knowledgeable but also very caring and understanding. He's a little soft-spoken but he explains concepts well and is always willing to spend extra time with you if you don't understand something. He's also very nice and reasonable with grading quizzes and exams.

analysis.name: Cedric Stallworth
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 142 reviews, fairly reliable

I enjoy being in his class.

I got a 58 on the first exam and was absolutely devastated and thought I was gonna fail the class (freshman canon event), but I studied really hard and managed to get an A in the class. I learned the most by going to recitations and the TAs (shout out to Victor!). The MATLAB grader is extremely useful for exams. Lots of extra credit opportunities.

Funny guy, but bad lecturer. Goes off topic and rants a lot, making students unprepared for his very difficult tests. TAs are way more useful; go to them if you need help. All he does is talk about his daughter or his 2 minutes on the Packers as their kicker. Rarely talks about the topics actually needed on exam. analysis.name: Frank Clark

review_highlights.comment: He's a good professor and you can tell he's super into music. The course is just thick with info and hard to get into and study. Exams had multiple choice, true or false, short answer, and an essay question timed and Honorlock. The course was a lot, but he is genuinely a good guy who's really passionate about music and kind to students.

Class is pretty easy to get an A in, but you will have to do some work. Projects are graded based on meeting the requirements and not your musical ability, which I liked. Project 4 was pretty confusing, though. Exams were pure memorization, but class was a nice break from my other classes, and you can get creative with the projects.

I absolutely loved this class, this is without a doubt one of the kindest and most sympathetic professors I've ever had. He's very easy to reach via email and is always trying to make the experience better for the students he teaches. The video lectures are well done and help you work at your own pace which I really appreciated.

If you are at all interested in jazz, take this class! Video lectures are pretty short but very thorough. I had fun going to jazz clubs with friends for the concert reports. Tons (up to ~30%) of easy extra credit. 4 online honorlock exams that are pure memorization of facts.

The lecture videos are very lighthearted and delivered well, and this is one of the few classes I've seen where the instructor is perhaps more active than the TAs. Information comes out pretty early, and there's plenty of support in online tutorials if you need help.

analysis.name: Christopher Jankowski
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 110 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: His lectures are great; I even have friends that wake up for his 8 AMs that aren't registered. He paces himself well and clarifies any questions. You don't have to go to class except for the occasional in-class poll (3 get dropped, 5% of grade). Quizzes are pretty easy (1 gets dropped), and midterms are fair (but slightly harder than other profs).

Linear algebra is not my strong suit so I struggled bad. Jankowski was always super easy to reach and responded quickly and effectively for my accommodations. He's a nice guy who loves math, but you have to pull your weight to pass. He gets strict near the end with final cumulative grades and doesn't round.

Really good lectures, really enthusiastic that makes you enthusiastic about math (which is a feat in itself). Pretty tough exams, but usually the averages were right in the middle of the curve of the other classes, so they were fair. Very helpful in office hours, etc. Highly recommend.

This class is not too hard to get an A in if you study well. The tests are kind of difficult and it's easy to get points off because a lot of questions are true/false or select all that apply, but if you understand the content well enough, it's usually fine. He has lecture videos and slides posted, so you don't have to go to lectures either.

Professor Jankowski is a great professor. He was a good presenter and would explain in class. It is easy to access him via Piazza, office hours, or after class. Apart from being a good lecturer, he was a personable guy and would yap about his life stories. He is the course director and posts plenty of resources. Use resources and ask for help!

really wants you to get better at the language so lots of speaking involved. theres a good deal of work to do outside of class but not too much or difficult to deal with.

If you don't already have knowledge w/ CS this can be a very long and challenging course. Wayyyy too much HW for an intro class, but there is extra credit. The tests are hard because they are all or nothing, so it's easy to get a poor grade if you don't write out the solutions perfectly.

Dellaert is a caring professor that listens to students' concerns, and actively tries to ensure students in lecture understand the content. The content itself is quite difficult, but there's more than enough time provided to complete projects and receive full points. No in class exams reduces stress.

Is very passionate about the topic he teaches, however completely centers his course around a textbook he wrote and a library he created. This feels less of a lecture/course and more of him flaunting his own works and forcing students to use them, even if they can be useful. Homework is long and lots of busy work. Lectures are complex but useless.

Pretty intense math/concepts and new ones every lecture. Difficult homeworks feel like "so what?" when you finish them. Entirely dissuaded me from doing robotics ever again.

it takes weeks for grades to be returned to you. in addition, the criteria for the lengthy reflection portion of projects is extremely unclear, and the weight for each project in canvas is wrong, causing unnecessary stress for students. lectures were also incredibly hard to follow. don't take this class.

analysis.name: Nabid Farvez
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly

Despite the tight deadlines, he encourages hard work with rigid schedules and stiff grading.

Professor Farvez was an extraordinary teacher. He reached above and beyond what should be expected from a professor, and always offered up advice or just a friendly face to talk to whenever his students needed it. Ask him about his youtube channel!
In these trying times, Professor Farvez was honestly a bright spot in a difficult semester. Despite his intimidating accomplishments, he's a humble and nice instructor who truly wants you to succeed.

I haven't gotten a chance to take any of his real classes yet but I hear he's an overall nice guy. Actually not a professor yet but maybe one day.
Professor Farvez really makes you work hark in this class, but you learn so much! One of the best professors and best classes I've had and taken at Tech. Truly lifechanging.

analysis.name: Nihad Farooq

Take another professor. Readings were way too much, so make sure to study for the exam. Also only graded by a few things.

she's a great prof and very passionate about ob. class is chill and always ends early/or we don't have class to work on the semester long group project. project isnt bad if you have good teammates. there's extra credit too. only downside is mandatory attendance and you need to speak up 3x in the semester

review_highlights.comment: She really expects you to sleep for 4 hrs or less. She also expects you to be doing work at every hour of the day which is unrealistic. She wants to put pressure on students to make them better but she just does it in an unhealthy and harmful way to her students.

Very smart and passionate in her own right, but quite obsessive in her student's individual projects. Will say one thing and want another and will not defend you in front of the jurors even if they make a point on something that SHE recommended for YOUR design. Unrealistic expectations and run her section way more difficult than the other studios.

This is the only instructor that I have had where studio is my least favorite class. She does not give good feedback, and has unrealistic expectations. She has no care for students at all. While her work is good and she is definitely smart, she does not know how to teach at all. She pushes her designs on everyone, and CANNOT communicate at all.

Super intellectual and in her own mind. I am sure she had some brilliant thoughts, but she could not communicate them well. I question the validity of her position working with the level of students I was a part of, as she expected us to sacrifice a lot (eat, sleep, fun) to achieve a level in our work that she didn't even know if was possible.

A truly engaging and passionate professor. The studio was demanding and expected a great deal from me, and I consistently felt challenged. However, I also feel that I grew the most in this studio precisely because of the rigor it required.

analysis.name: Omer Inan
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Great Professor, and very insightful and inspiring to learn about for topics in Biomedical Instrumentation.  Attendance is not mandatory, but content taught is not on slides. Picks project apart, make sure you choose the right topic, and get feedback before he grades. Could've been a bit more Canvas-savvy. No practice quizzes, likes design quizzes.

3 exams lowest dropped. 1) sig proc, 2) heart anatomy, 3) research design. Project is a lot of work, and Inan will pick your project apart, but has many office hours to get help before youre graded. Really nice and smart person. lectures cover stuff not on exams but you will benefit from going. ~3.7 GPA is accurate.

I took this class as a BME with little circuit knowledge not knowing how circuit heavy it was. His lectures are taught at a very high level assuming you know alot of the terminology with op ams and filters. I would make friends with EE's in the class early and use chat gpt to look up concepts from this class and you should be fine.

One of my favorite profs at Tech. Only graded by 3 easy 100% HW's and the highest two test grades. The Group Project is 50% of the grade and is pretty time consuming, but not worse than what you've already done in the curriculum already. Class always ended 30min early and we still learned a lot of interesting material. More of a grad student class.

ECE 4781 is tougher than 4782 but it is still a great class. I got an A by averaging 99 on exams, 100 on HW and an 80 on the project. He grades the projects harder and lowers your score if you pick the easier review project, but if you want to pass the class you don't need to put much work in. Still drops a test and HW, so don't worry about them.

analysis.name: Ikenna Nometa
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He was very kind and always present for asking questions, but the lectures could be hard to follow so I had to rely heavily on the 50-minute lecture videos that Math 1554 Common leaves up. I won't be too harsh though, it was his first time teaching a weed-out class at Georgia Tech, and he has all of the qualities of a good professor.

he's kinda difficult to understand and i don't think he explains the concepts well, but it was his first semester so i guess it's understandable. i will say he seems like a nice, genuine guy. i personally stopped going to class after the first couple lectures and instead watched the videos from cuyler warnock or sal barone, which i found helpful.

linear is a hard class. not many attend the lectures, but they are helpful to get the content down, although some lecture can be self taught. he's helpful and explains hard content well. the harder questions are usually the conceptual questions so you need to have a great understanding of theorems which is very hard to do in this class.

The only negative thing I have to say is that sometimes he didn't explain certain concepts very well or would skip through them during lecture, but he made up for it by always being available after class to explain better, other than that he was great. This was also his first year teaching so I'm guessing he will improve over time.

Dr. Nometa is a great professor. He explains concepts very clearly and connects the topics of Linear Algebra together very well (which is a necessity for this class). He's very accessible outside of class and cares about his students. The only downside is his accent, which can be hard to understand at times, but you'll get used to it.

analysis.name: Ilya Gokhman
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Such an insightful class. The professor cared about students walking away having learned something from the class. You learn a lot about yourself and how to lead in this class and highly recommend it to anyone interested in leadership or self reflection.

I think GC could be fun, but Ilya (with all respect) can make this class seem like hell. He can be very adamant about his methods of doing things and creating teams and wont allow you to explore a little more. He will also question you a ton during pin ups. Just submit all your work DONT FALL BEHIND and go to lectures and it will be an easy A.

Easy A class. Show up to class and ur good. Make sure you choose a team, not necessarily friends, but amiable people with different perspectives. I actually really liked the involvement of ChatGPT in the class cuz we can already see the impact of it, so it was nice to see that prof-led encouragement for good usage of it. Fun engaging discussions.

Grand Challenges is very fun, but Ilya makes it unnecessarily challenging to enjoy this class. Regardless of the teacher, this class is a free A, if you submit all your work and show up to class.

- His lectures don't make sense
- He will rip you apart during pin-ups so be prepared to answer random questions
- Not really an approachable guy

I absolutely loved Professor Gokhman's class. I took Organizational Policy with him and the class was really interesting and fun. It was a 3 hour class, which would seem horrible, but he made it tolerable. I found the content interesting, and he would always get the class' input for anything we would do. I would recommend.

analysis.name: Igor Belegradek
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 48 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Weekly quizzes on ungraded HW and MyMathLab enforce learning. Tests are straight-forward, and based on the HWreview sheet but can be tough even so. Russian accent forces you to concentrate to follow the lecture. Attendance helps understanding- Igor is very enthusiastic about the material. Grades were slightly curved at the end: 85  A, 70  B, etc

It certainly felt impossible to succeed. I skipped lecturesarned through recitations, tutoring, and the textbook. Practice problems are given out before each exam that mimic questions on exam-if you have ALL answers to these problems, you are solid. Obtaining sufficient answers to theory questions is easier said than done; Piazza is a life saver

He was a kind soul, but his accent was pretty heavy. A majority of the class ended up attending other professors' lectures. In the grand scheme of things, your linear grade will likely be the same since everyone takes the same exams. He's a decent lecturer. Oftentimes, he ends up rambling/stuttering, but he is always down for questions.

Lectures were rather proof and example based rather then going through how to actually solve problems in practice and intuition. Professor does make himself available before and after class to answer questions. Would rather recommend reading the textbook then going to lectures as he goes a bit fast.

Great at answering questions, clearly cares about the material. Can be hard to understand at times, skips over certain processes, rushes through content. Make sure to ask questions if you don't understand, and read the textbook before class as that is one thing that proved helpful.

analysis.name: I-Hsiang Lee
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 46 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He's not a bad professor in terms of his teaching; however, this class is a lot more work than the other ISYE 3770 sections. All homeworks are written in R and they are quite time consuming. He has 2 in class "projects" that test your knowledge of how to use R. Also, the final is a decently large portion of the grade. Edit: HE CURVES THE FINAL!!

Strikes the best balance of hilarious, engaging lectures + excellent teaching that I've seen at Tech. Lengthy homeworks requiring R but I guarantee you'll understand the material better than if you took any other instructor. Only complaint is no practice tests and difficult exams which is unfortunate, but learn the material well and you'll succeed.

Ethan is one of the best professors I've had. He cares for all his students and knows everyone's names. He really wants u to learn the material so his exams are more difficult than the other sections, but it is completely worth it. He's hilarious and u will know way more than the other sections. He makes u learn R and curves! Please take him!

He has very high expectations and can make you feel stupid if you ask questions. Above all else though, the homeworks are grueling. Not necessarily because of the content but because it must be types in R. I almost lost my mind several times this semester because of having to code the hw which took hours.

Makes you feel stupid for asking questions at office hours. HW is basically coding in R, and the exams are difficult with very little partial credit and unnecessarily difficult instructions intended to confuse you. Attendance is mandatory but lectures are very boring. Be prepared for a hard time if you take his class.

analysis.name: Jechiel Jagoda
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Jagoda: course professor. The real reason I'm here is the trash TA's. We had 3 labs: 25%, 40%, and 25% (10% notebook). They couldn't correctly grade if someone moved their fingers for them. Had to put infinite regrade requests for things that were blatantly correct if you took a few seconds to read the reports. Over a month to get grades back.

Snoozefest! He may be an emeritus prof, but he can't really teach or use technology. Stopped going to class after about a week. Lab reports are graded using a rubric and are very time consuming. Expect each to take 10-15 hours of time. They are tediously graded and the TA's are strict about including specific things. Suck it up and get it done.

The criteria for doing well in this class is not at all clear. I lost a lot of points on reports because of unclear grading criteria. You only have to go to lab ~6 times per semester though, with 4 lab reports (25% of your grade). These take a lot of time. The lectures were incoherent and slow, but you also only have 4 of those.

Lectures are unclear and unhelpful. Grading was highly ambiguous, subjective, and nit-picky (TAs' fault primarily). Course schedule is structured poorly so if you're in section X you'll have weeks of back-to-back lab reports that are extraordinarily time intensive. Responses on Piazza are vague and conflicting, if you even get one.

This is one of the worst classes I've taken at this school. The lab manuals are incredibly unclear, and the course has major organization issues. The TAs will take points off for things that are clearly in your report, and you won't ever get a report back before the next one is due, meaning you will make the same mistakes over and over.

analysis.name: Jerry Seitzman
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He can be a little scary in class because he calls you out for little things. I don't enjoy going to class because he gets mad at people when they're late and highlights people's errors in front of the whole class, but attendance is mandatory (and he will figure out if you're missing it). The class is at least very easy.

Too much work for a one credit hour class. Yells at students. You can never do anything right type of professor. Will always find an issue with something you're doing and loudly announce it. You will learn, and he's effective at making his students learn. But you will not enjoy taking his class.

Not lenient or understanding at all, rude and will call you out for the smallest things in front of the entire class. Would've been a straightforward and enjoyable class, if he wasn't teaching it. Super nitpicky, will find something wrong with your work for even the simplest assignments.

I took Professor Seitzman during Summer 2025. One of the best professor's I've taken at Tech. AE 4451 is not an easy course to take in 5 weeks, and his homeworks are tough and challenging, but his style of teaching is awesome. I suggest for anyone who wants to go into propulsion, to take him.

Dr. Seitzman is the most intelligent and quick-witted professor I have ever met. He has transformed my engineering intuition for the better and I am grateful to have had a class with him. Although sassy, he wants to help you understand the concepts. Homework and exams are tough but if you put in the effort to go to office hours, you will be fine.

analysis.name: Jessica Roberts
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She assigns readings to look over for about every other class, but you only have to skim them and pay attention in lecture to have an understanding of what's going on. Assignment requirements are communicated clearly and the TA's and Roberts give good feedback, so it's easy to do well on assignments and get an A in the class overall.

The class itself isn't difficult, but she is an incredibly dry lecturer and it's difficult to pay attention to how she rambles in monotone. Also, grading criteria is not clear at all; despite how easy the homeworks are, it's equally easy to lose points on something not previously mentioned in the directions. Would suggest the other Ed Tech prof.

If I am being honest, the class was okay. I wasn't always excited, but she was very nice and clear with grading. A lot of unnecessary reading. I never read any of the readings and did fine. I would recommend that you all take her if you want an A. The group project wasn't too bad, but you wont be able to just coast your way through.

I expected it to have lighter work than it did but honestly it is worth it for a chill CS class. Lectures are a bit dull but there were a few class activities that I enjoyed. The class is mostly a semester long project that you work alongside a team. There is one midterm and a presentation of the project.

Prof Roberts's Ed Tech class was wonderful. You'll learn a lot during lecture, and she really engages students. The class is what you make of it—if you apply yourself and are passionate about the group project topic, then you will really enjoy it. There is a good bit of writing, which is to be expected. Great class overall!

analysis.name: Justin Kim
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I need to point this out: this man decided to make the class only 85% exams and 15% homework even though he had FULL ABILITY to change that grading scheme. And why did he decide to keep it this way and why did he make his exams nearly impossible for his students so they could be in tears when handing in their exams? Because he simply doesn't care.

Do not take this professor. Exams were unreasonable and an incredibly high portion of the grade. I studied for over 30 hours for the most recent exam and left with half the problems blank. He is not an enjoyable professor to have, and I would not recommend him in any form or fashion.

I think Dr. Kim forgets that we're learning new material for the 1st time, with our previous knowledge of Chem 2311 being so far back. No amount of feedback and critiques would ever change his mind because of his ego. Apparently he went to prestigious colleges, so he thinks he's the smartest and greatest of mankind. He's not! Opposite actually.

He's a nice dude, would be great for grad students who already know the material. With 85% of your grade being exams, and 15% being accuracy based problem sets, there is no padding to your grade. Exams are extremely difficult and at a level of difficulty that should have a crib sheet and are not representative of resources given in class.

I did every single practice problem available (400+ online WileyPlus questions), textbook problems, practice tests, PLUS session practice problems, problem sets, material review, and STILL did not recognize anything on the exam. Miserable experience, I would not take this prof if you can avoid it. I will probably end up dropping this class.

analysis.name: John Smith
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 41 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Be prepared to memorize absolutely everything Prof. Smith says. His tests are ridiculously specific, you have to have his lecture memorized and he sometimes puts things in the tests that he didn't even say. The entire grade depends on 3 tests and 5 quizzes, which are all extremely hard. I had a terrible time, don't take this class if u want an A.

Only three tests are given, which your grade depends on. Every single word he says in the lecture should be memorized, as well as every reading given, which are all stupid things that do not lead to an overall understanding of history at all. Irrelevant content, irrelevant class, terrible grade for a humanity.

Prof. Smiths class is extremely test heavy. The tests are 50 questions, 50 minutes, and the questions are incredibly hard. His lectures have practically no words so you basically have to write down every thing he says because his test are very specific. Your entire grade depends on quizzes and tests. Way too hard for a humanity.

Professor Smith is a great teacher and very passionate about what he does. However his class structure is archaic. You have little to no wiggle room time wise during the exams, the lecture slides have almost 0 words on them so you need to take detailed notes, and there is no opportunity for bonus points. Tough class for a humanity.

I am crying in frustration and laughing at the audacity... Why am I putting more work into this class than my STEM classes - let me remind you this is GT - and STILL getting worse grades? 3 tests make up 90% (!!!) of your grade. No study guides, no notes, no extra credit. Impossible to succeed. Wanna pass? Memorize every word he says. Good luck LOL

analysis.name: James Stroud
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Super engaging professor and talks a lot about his own research and other research at Tech. As long as you can validly explain your answer you'll get credit. In-class activities are really helpful for test-prep, and he drops 6 (so you can miss 6 free classes). Grading scheme is pretty test-heavy, but the tests are all written so grading is fair.

Professor is really nice and cares a lot about the students. He also does not accept any bs from his students and believes you should put in 110% work. He cares A LOT about ecology and genuienly passionate about his work. He is tough grader and he looks very specific answers which is sometimes difficult to figure out during a test.
Professor Stroud is a decent professor, but the exams are graded so much harder than needed. You have to give the exact answers he is looking for and the exams are weighted a lot.
Grade is composed mostly of exams. Exams are graded so harshly and there is no cushioning.

analysis.name: Robert Kirkman
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Nobody is excited to attend an Ethics course, however Kirkman does a great job making his lectures interesting. Writing isn't too hard and neither are the exams. Overall a solid ethics class

Only grades for the semester are weekly essays and a final project. He gives lots of feedback on the essays which sometimes is super harsh. Classes were him talking about the assigned readings with no slides or other material, he just talks at you for 75 minutes. He was very friendly and the class didn't demand too much, overall a good class.

He gives you a lot to read, a lot to write, and can sometimes feel like he's harping with his feedback and unwilling to just say "Good job". But he does actually care- if you talk to him just a bit outside of class, do all of your work (as tedious as it may be), and take his feedback seriously, you can almost guarantee an A.

3109 online meets MW for 50 minutes, discussing ethical topics, these meetings are not bad and you don't have to participate.  Friday discussions are on case studies where you can discuss and debate an ethical dilemma from an engineer.  If you get a good TA, this class can be great

Class GPA is high, I feel like it would be easy to get an A if you put in the effort he asks. That being said, the final project effectively determines your grade, and this is frustrating because you need a perfect score (no partial credit) and everyone knows how bad group projects are at Tech. Easy class but stressful if you don't like risk.

analysis.name: Katharine McCann
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Out of the 3 NEUR 2001 professors, she was the best. Her lectures were engaging and interesting and she made sure that we understood all of the information. The unit 3 midterm (the unit she taught) was extremely straightforward and easy, especially compared to the other 2 tests. Overall amazing professor.

she def cares and is very accessible for help outside of the class. she does truly want her students to succeed and structures 3003 highly around getting feedback. good lecturer, boring topic. the tests in this course are a bit tough but the grading scheme allows for leniency. can average B on tests and a B on the term paper for an A.

Dr. McCann is by far one of the best professors I have ever had at this school. She is kind, knowledgeable, & very passionate about what she teaches!! I would take as many courses as I could with this professor since I not only feel like I learned a significant amount, but also enjoyed this course so much! Also I took 3003 with her, not 3001.
Super sweet and great with communication. Clear grading criteria. Super passionate and in-class participation are relatively easy.

Very kind and understanding, I had her for 2001 and 3003 - she teaches well and seems to genuinely care. Class structures for both were Not The Best, but I dont think that's on her. Out of any of the neuro teachers she co-taught with, she explained things the best, if not a little fast though. Highly recommend taking her classes.

analysis.name: Sriram Kalathoor
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Genuinely might be the best professor at Tech. Incredibly smart, amazing lectures, interesting office hours, great grading policy. Your grade is based on the effort you put in. If you want to actually learn, take him. Reconsider which classes you want to take purely to get Sriram. 85% of the knowledge I have actually retained came from his classes.

Aero may be hard, but Sriram makes up for it by being one of the best profs in the AE department. Super accessible outside of class, great lecturer, and cares about the students (he's one of us). If you ever have the chance of taking a class with him or meeting him, take it. You won't regret it.

Truly Incredible. Your grade is almost entirely decided by your effort, poor exam performance if often recoverable due to generous grading, extra credit, projects, attendance, etc. Difficult material but Dr. K is masterful. Homework will take a large amount of time but is really rewarding and extremely useful.

CFD with prof. Kalathoor was a great experience. Exams were certainly tough but fair, provided you studied the content properly, and homework assignments were definitely on the longer side. The project was a big time sink but very rewarding once the simulations finally gave realistic solutions. Highly recommend, he was a great lecturer and resource

The best professor, creates such a safe space for learning. Sriram's care for the subject and his students shines through in his engaging lectures and flexible class structure. HWs take a long time and exams are difficult, but you learn extremely relevant skills. Super smart, pick his brain, go to OH, and you will come out knowing so much more.

analysis.name: Mijin Kim
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: For reference, I took this class in Spring 2024 - her first class. She was incredibly nice and explained topics well when I reached out for help. She moves really fast in lecture but she does give practice exams which are helpful and representative. This was probably the easiest Chem class I've taken at GT so far and I'm not that smart.

Dr. Kim is a nice professor. But she reads off slides during lecture and makes attendance mandatory for in class problems.  Her tests are similar to the practice and recitation problems, so just study those. She gives extra buffer points on tests. The final was so much harder than all of the tests, but she lowered the grade boundary, thankfully.

She is very nice professor, but her lectures are awful because she makes many mistakes and is very hard to understand at times. The only reason to go to the lecture is to do the mandatory in class problems.

The best way to succeed would study by yourself and go to recitation.

Also her tests will have many errors, so ask questions during testing.

Be prepared to have the slides read straight to you every single class. There is no point in showing up for class at all except for the fact that an in-class problem, for what you literally just learned. The final was 33% of the grade and half of the material wasn't even gone over. Emails are hardly even answered.
Dr. Kim's lectures were sometimes a little confusing but she was very nice and gave bonus points on exams. Additionally, she gave lots of extra credit and even lowered the grade boundaries.

analysis.name: Raquel Lieberman
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Lieberman isn't the most engaging lecturer, but her lecture videos get all the information you need across and her tests were very easy and fair. The flipped classroom is not as bad as the other comments say. Other professors might be better, but if you take it with Lieberman you have nothing to worry about.

flipped classroom is terrible. you have to learn everything alone and the videos offered are so terrible. I had to watch another random professor on youtube to learn anything. she sounds so uninterested in what she is teaching and sounds like she wants to be there less than you want to be. DO NOT RECOMMEND BIOCHEM WITH HER!!! TAKE WITH SOMEONE ELSE

Her tests and quizzes aren't bad, as long as you study and understand the material. I liked her lectures, not the most boring professor. However, she does have an attitude when she feels challenged by students. So don't use your phone or turn over a test or quiz paper unless you want to be scolded in front of the whole class. You've been warned.

Dr. Lieberman is an amazing professor! She's funny and knowledgeable. Bchem-I is hard to grasp and master, but her flipped classroom helped take time to learn content outside class and address all concerns in class. You also see real life application in class through group activities. If you put in effort, you will get so much out of this class!

Her tests and quizzes are decent if you study really well, though there were some questions that came out of nowhere. She's kind of condescending in office hours and so was the TA (both unhelpful) so find a good study group. Overall good course, informative, interesting lectures. Don't slack, study hard, and this course will be easy.

analysis.name: Shana Kerr
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 65 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Seems really approachable in class BUT BEWARE if you go to her office. You will likely see students in tears.  She is not known for her personality!

Kerr seems approachable and nice when you first start out, but it is quite the opposite! She talks faster in her lectures than any human should ever be able to speak. Be prepared to "infer" (her words) what parts of the book you should be reading because the readings don't match the homework or the lectures and of course not the test.

The most important thing to do is to read and take notes on the textbook, as her lectures are basically regurgitating that. You can get around the participation by doing the learning catalytics from home; going to the lecture isn't necessary as long as you read the textbook. The tests can be difficult, but reading the textbook helps.

I saw the other rating, and it's accurate. She appears nice and approachable but when contacted one-on-one does not care about the success or feelings of students. Also, her lectures are a little all over the place because she often loses her train of thought and often can't answer questions confidently.

She goes so fast you cannot possibly take notes, and doesn't explain things well. She doesnt take time on the parts that are the most confusing, and goes on long tangents about stuff that isnt relevant. There are assignments unrelated to the content are harshly graded, and take up time. During office hours she is condescending and confusing.

analysis.name: Lenny Stendig
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He cares a lot and takes feedback which he reacts to quickly.  Had a couple knowledgeable entrepreneurs, investors, and lawyers talk to us.  Did a class project giving us experience in pitching and coming up with problems/solutions.  Provided great resources for us to learn ourselves.  Easy class teaching new perspective, not much knowledge tho.

He made sure he recieved feedback and used it to become a better professor. Very willing to help students get credit back on assignments and did test corrections for exams. Also just entertaining in class. He had attendence as extra credit. Overall made the class enjoyable

His lectures didn't vibe with me. I ended up textbook grinding the class since the lectures didn't help me with the class. Overall, the copious amounts of extra credit and help he provides to excel in the course make up for the somewhat lacking lectures. I overall enjoyed the class and think he was a great guy but the topic for me was just bad.

Prof. Stendig is a great guy, he definitely cares about his students. I didn't really love his lecture style, so I did most of my learning from the textbook which was pretty effective. Offers lots of Extra Credit opportunities (atendance is extra credit) and test corrections, which I highly recommend doing.
He is a phenomenal Professor, deeply cares about his students, is very passionate about economics, and is frankly hilarious. Gives a lot of extra credit and second chances too. 10/10

analysis.name: Michael Lacey
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 47 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Lacey is in general a good guy and I believe he does genuinely care about his students, however teaching just isnt his thing. There were times when he would be going through example problems and he would get stuck in the middle of them, give up, and move on. We missed a lot of important concepts this way. I pretty much taught myself using mathlab.

Expect the following in each lecture: 1. "Oops! Did I make a mistake?" 2. "How many minutes do I have left? I don't think I can finish this example." And yet in his own words, he is "a leading expert in Fourier series." Year in, year out, despite constant critiques, Lacey never attempted any improvement - always coming unprepared for the lecture.

Lectures were awful. It was extremely difficult to get the important points out of his lecturing. He often wasted 10 min at the beginning of class talking about irrelevant info such as hurricanes, voting, etc. Then he would complain that we didnt have enough time to finish that section in the chapter. He rarely went back to finish them.
Really dry, only talks about theory and never really applies any of the ideas

I've taken calc before and I got totally lost in this class. Homework, lectures and tests are like three different classes, none relevant to each other. The test questions are the hardest possible questions he could ask. Does not collect homework.

analysis.name: Ling Liu
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I have been in GT CS for 5 years and this is THE worst of all the ones I have taken. The instructor is knowledgeable about the content she teaches. However, she is extremely rude to students and makes the course overly arbitrary. The rubrics for assignments are vague and the workload is too heavy for the final paper. Time wasted.

The CS6220 course experience is one of the worst at GT CS. TAs are non-existent. Homework is poorly designed with little instruction on what to do. Grading is quite random as well with no clear standard. However, if you just need an easy A and don't care about course experience, this course might actually be pretty nice.
Using public humiliation as a form of motivation is not valid. I don't need to know that another student is doing poorly in the class or is going through "family issues"

This is not a Systems course. This is rather a collection of topics the instructors is excited about. The same is reflected in the assignments, project-topics, and the review subjects. This class felt more ML and LLMs heavy than Systems heavy.

Also, lectures felt very vague, and most of the learning happened during the assignments and projects.
