Genuinely a crashout, rude, grades hard for the projects and has a huge final paper. Haven't finished yet, but I've heard the curve is huge because of this. Most of this wouldn't be too bad if she wasn't extremely rude too.

analysis.name: Michelle Rinehart
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Rinehart is very passionate, but she can also be very strict, is not afraid to call out and raise her voice at students for being on their phone/talking in class. The 3 sketchbooks are not difficult but are time consuming and graded harshly. They're due immediately when class starts, if its 1 minute late she will call you out in class.

Michelle's lectures were genuinely interesting & VALUABLE for us architecture students. Lectures become warzones for staying awake if you're not genuinely interested, so take notes, draw, etc! You're graded on 3 sketchbooks + 2 digital assignments that give you a month each, so PACE YOURSELF! Your grade depends on your time management + attendance.

This class had the opportunity to really engage students during their first year but instead chose to show us a slideshow every day. Weirdly timed (5-6pm) so kind of hard to be engaged. The assignments were lengthy but not hard at all. Not super nice to put into portfolio once you're past first year. Weird about sick excuses. Shes not bad per say.
Lecture may get “boring” at times as it usually doesn't directly relate to assignments, but an interesting class and great professor nonetheless.

The professor made lectures bearable by sharing personal stories about some of the places on the slides and strongly encouraged class engagement. You are graded only on work outside of class, which is time-consuming but straightforward. All assignments are graded based on completion and effort, so getting an A should be easy; don't procrastinate.

analysis.name: Mayra Pineda Torres
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Most of your grade comes from exams which are based on the lecture materials, so it's important to take good notes. There's lots of opportunities for easy extra credit, take them it will make you less stressed at the end of the semester.

Exams are worth 60% of the overall grade, but many of the problems are very similar to the problem sets so if you complete the problem set you will be fine. The lectures can be a little confusing at times, but Prof. Pineda Torres does a good job of conveying information in an understandable way. There are also several opportunities for extra credit

New professor, huge busy-work assignment every few weeks. Professor over-emphasized her concern for academic dishonesty and seems to actively hunt students who cheat. Easy A if you do the work, don't take the class for granted just because it's easy. You'll need to show up to class for quizzes and be prepared for busy work out of the textbook.

Dr. Pineda-Torres is incredibly cohesive, articulate, and nuanced when discussing concepts. She values the theoretical as well as empirical sides, which gives realistic insight into economic research and its applications. If you do as expected in the syllabus and speak relatively frequently in class, the course should be very manageable.

analysis.name: Michele Rosbruck
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 76 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Extremely easy class. Definitely take 1040 over any of the other health classes if you can. You don't have to show up at all to this class if you don't want to. Only 8 grades, 3 tests, 3 quizzes and 2 writing assignments but they're graded really easily. My high school health class was more advanced than this.

This class was very easy. She loves to pull questions from an online test bank which you can find using questions in the back of each chapter. 3 assignments are given but are easy 100's if you do the work. Encourages participation in class but no one ever shows up because it's not necessary. Guest Lecturers are important though for test questions.
Her class is all tests that are on canvas, and asynchronous. Attendance not mandatory, and up to 4 extra credit points through different things during the semester. VERY EASY class.

You can either come to lectures or read the book and pass without a problem. Lecture notes are always posted to T-square. Offers up to 4 percentage points of extra credit. Requires just about zero effort, which is, coincidentally, how much effort the professor puts into the class.

This professor is so funny sometimes.This is a health class no one goes to after a while so people just stop coming and no one responds to her questions in the lecture so she'll crack jokes at that and it's honestly amazing, this professor deserves so much better because at the end she takes it so sweetly and still makes lectures fun and engaging.

analysis.name: Maysam Nezafati
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Nezafati is a GOAT! He is a very understanding and caring professor who takes time to make sure his students understand the concepts of class, not just a pattern for problems. PSS was very helpful, and his lectures reinforced material well. The homework was time consuming and quizzes were hard, but by the exams you were good and an 83 was an A.

Dr. Nezafati cares a lot about his students and if you're going to take bmed2110 definitely take it with him. The class itself is a lot of work but if you take the time to watch the lecture videos and understand the homework, the quizzes and tests aren't terrible.

Great teacher! 3 exams (1 was the final) - each one was based on what we had learned since the previous exam so nothing cumulative and each one had 3 attempts (with grades averaged). Explained everything very well. Rounded my high B up to an A (I went to every class and did every assignment) and I'm very thankful. Very manageable class!

Dr. Nezafati has been a great 2110 professor, especially with learning such different concepts than normal classes. He has always been very open to questions and helping outside of class. He seems to really enjoy the material and makes the class a lot more interesting. There is a lot of homework but TA hours are always really helpful (PAUL!!!)

Dr. Nezafati was very enthusiastic about the material. He explained everything very well and was very helpful when asked questions. He emphasized the small details, which are very important for this difficult course. He also made the online lectures this semester which were great. Definitely wouldn't want to take this class with anyone else.

analysis.name: Mark Moss
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 93 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He's a great lecturer, breaking things down simply and traces through examples. The hardest part is unfamiliar content, but review and find a TA during OHs for project help early and you'll be set. I'm taking him in the fall with projects weighing ~60% of your total grade, so you can afford to struggle with the quizzes like I did.

Honestly, I am just dropping a rating here for the TAs. Moss is such a boring lecturer in my opinion (have zoned out in basically EVERY lecture), but the TAs make it all worth it. I would genuinely describe office hours as a religious experience. I have learned weeks of content within just a few hours!!

Don't get me wrong you can tell he's passionate about what he teaches, but I found his lectures to be incredibly boring. It lacks a lot of depth and he often goes over things not ever covered in the quizzes. I stopped going to lecture and solely learned everything from lab/textbook. As long as you do those two things, you should get at least a B

Moss is a very good lecturer, it does take him a bit to get to the point sometimes but he's very enthusiastic and engaging with what he teaches. He also posts all his lectures to Canvas. Labs were essentially just mandatory recitations were never on-pace with the course (as in they were almost always ahead), making them a drag to go to biweekly.

overall he's a kind and chill teacher. he does have a hard time getting to the point in his lectures but other than that he's a great prof. unfortunately, i got the worst TAs possible which makes the class more challenging than it was supposed to be. they're incredibly unhelpful, rude, and straight up ruins the class. other than that good prof

analysis.name: Nikki MacKenzie
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 53 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof MacKenzie is chill the work each week is light of just watching videos for lecture, doing an online quiz, and doing the online assingment. Lecture in person is also useful shell do practice problems and re explain the concepts from the last weeks lecture. Exams were easy usally about 20-25 mcq and 2 written questions.

Accounting is like learning a new language so it was extremely difficult at first, each test is worth a big chunk of your grade so be careful. She is a good professor with the hybrid class, and prepared us well for the exams. Don't fall behind, or else its extremely hard to catch back up and truly grasp the content as the tests are in depth

Kind of confused by all the low ratings. I had Professor Mackenzie for my online accounting 2101 class. It was very easy to follow along with the online lecture and guided notes. She explains concepts very well and in depth and makes it easy to understand. Exams were mostly multiple choice and were not to tough.

Accounting was new to me so I had to put a lot of time and effort into studying for this class. The professor is pretty nice, although sometimes what she says about the level of difficulty in a test is not true. The homework takes forever. If you can avoid the hybrid class, do because I think in person would have been better.

idk if all the other reviews just were horrid test takers, but this was actually one of my lowest effort classes. read the syllabus, watch the lectures, do the practice in the notes, show up to class (or not honestly) and u will be fine. group project was annoying but manageable, plus done by thanksgiving. boring teacher but what can you do...

analysis.name: Nivedita Bhattacharya
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 72 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Bhattacharya is an amazing teacher and her class notes are the best! She provides a lot of learning resources and explains concepts very clearly. But what stands out most of all in my opinion is her respect for the students.

She was a true gem virtually. Whenever I needed some clearing up or had a question on piazza, she answered in LESS THAN AN HOUR. Her lecture videos were very well done. Even when I had technical issues on the first exam, she let me email my exam to her with no complications, she was totally understanding. I WISH I COULD TAKE HER AGAIN!

Professor Bhattacharya was very knowledgeable and delivered clear and informative lectures.
She doesn't go too fast, and you can tell she cares about her students. Also answers questions thoroughly.
Very clear on how to succeed in the class, and she provides numerous resources like class notes and practice
exams to help you.

Professor Bhattacharya is one of the best professors I have had at GT. She is very accessible and helpful. She will respond to emails very quickly, and if your question can not be answered via email, she will set up a private call with you. As a non-ECE major, I felt she did a fantastic job at making the content understandable and not too complex.

One of the best professors at Georgia Tech hands down. Professor Bhattacharya is very caring and she really just wants you to understand the material. If you have any problems she will understand and help. The only downside is that the class was fully online this semester, but at least the lectures are recorded.

analysis.name: Namrata Dey Roy
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Dey Roy is one of the best professors I've had in all of literature. Our class focused on Disney's literature and critical analysis in the pieces. She definitely cared about the students, and helped everyone whenever necessary. Her grading was constructive and accommodating. Participate in class; it's worth it.

She was an amazing professor. Her English class topics are always so interesting. She was always so caring and kind. She really fostered a love for English that I never really had before college. She doesn't do book reading, instead more focuses on movies, excerpts, theories, shows, etc. Also, her feedback is tasteful and helpful. :)

This class had a fun theme and was very light. We had 3 major assignments that were all given 3 weeks before they were due. Grading was easy and clear, and the attendance/participation grade comes from discussion posts in Canvas. I had a good time in her class she is very flexible!

I took Dr. Dey Roy's ENGL1102 class over the summer, and I absolutely loved it. Every day was interesting, and we frequently watched movie clips and had debates. Grade was based on a few major artifacts and one final portfolio. Extremely funny, kind, and accommodating professor, would 100% take her class again.

Dr. Dey Roy was very caring and kind with students. The class was very fun and only had a few projects as grades and a final portfolio. What is needed to make an A is very clearly written in rubrics. We often watched movie clips and class discussion was a huge part of class. Occasional readings but no other homework besides that.

analysis.name: Nimisha Roy
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 62 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Outstanding professor to take for a class that people only appreciate after getting an internship. There are a lot of people who are just rude to a really good Professor. Professor Roy makes the class interesting and while there are a lot of work, people need to keep in mind this is not a 2 credit hour course.

Pretty great teacher. Was very receptive to feedback and genuinely wanted to improve the course. Lectures are pretty fast, but I found that to be a plus. Overall, 2340 as a class just sucks, but Prof. Roy tried her best to make it somewhat enjoyable.

agree with other reviewers in that ur experience rly depends on whether u get a good group or not. MAKE SURE u get a good group (or switch) so ur not bogged down by project work all sem like me 😭 class is p hands off and material isn't too difficult, but assignments + tech (android studio) can get annoying and stack up if ur not on top of things

Prof. Roy did a great job with the hybrid format, although I am not a fan of the format.  She figured out a balance between hybrid, providing long-form videos with in-depth notes while summarizing the important details in class. Getting a good team in class really helps.

2340 is an awful class, but Professor Roy did a good job running it, and was very responsive to questions and overall helpful. The midterms and "mini-assessments" don't weigh a lot but require you to actually learn the "content", which led to poor performance that seemed to bother her more than it did the students. A fine professor for a bad class.

analysis.name: Onur Birol
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 61 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Birol is one of the worst teachers I have ever had. He makes his tests overly difficult and is not open to the student's concerns. The test is in 50 minutes and I have to search through over 500 pages of notes so you're set up for failure. He doesn't respect students at all/very passive-aggressive. I would avoid him if you need to take BIOS 1108.

Made physiology very interesting and made topics relatable. Exams were straightforward, but some questions were difficult. Final exam was light, 60% of it came from previous midterms. You can do well by going to class or self-studying with the book. Homework = easy grade booster. Pre-lecture quizzes were annoying timing-wise, but he dropped a lot.

Dr. Birol co-taught this class with Dr. Richards. Birol is clearly passionate about biology. I went to 70% of the lectures and made an A. He is a good speaker and helps us understand material better. The only issue is that some of the exam questions were based on what was said in lecture and not found in the slides, but it wasn't that big of a deal

Dr. Birol's lectures were extremely helpful, and I felt that exams accurately reflected content taught in class. Pre-readings were required for this class. If I did not understand a pre-reading, I knew that if I went to class Dr. Birol would clarify it for me. Great teacher!!
To do well, attendance isn't necessary. Just rely on the textbook.

co-taught w/ robbie richards. birol focused on animals and was generally better. didn't ramble as much. he tries to draw focus to what goes on the test, but there's just a great amount of content. recitation is helpful. some tests focus on what is explicitly talked about in class and not clearly shown on slides, but attendance isn't mandatory.

analysis.name: Osvaldo Cleger
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Cleger is such a pro. His classes are interesting, easy, and informative. You'll always ba able to get a lot out of his lessons, and he's kind of a pro in general. You should definitely take his class if you get the chance.
Osvaldo is the man!! He is adorable, and I absolutely love this class. He is very smart and entertaining. If I could retake this class, I would. Osvaldo is amazing. Highly recommended.

He is a really cool guy and cares for his students. I didn't do as well as I would have liked but mainly because I didn't participate in class that much. He is difficult, but maybe just shouldn't be teaching 3111. I recommend him to people who are very knowledgeable of Spanish.

Loved taking this professor! I learned a lot about Cuban immigration to America and more about assimilation of Cuban Americans into American culture. The papers and weekly speaking also helped me improve my fluency and depth of knowledge of the Spanish language.

A passionate and funny professor. Expects a lot out of his students in upper level classes. Sometimes expects a baseline of knowledge in other subjects (ie, got upset at class for not knowing economics principles.) Remember, upper level Spanish classes are moreso random history classes just taught in Spanish. Expect to read a lot.

analysis.name: Omar Asensio
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: One of those teachers yaps each and every class period. This class has a lot of potential, but unfortunately, professor Asensio makes it far too theoretical. If you want a relatively easy class and need to fulfill degree requirements, take this class and push through. If you want to learn, STAY AWAY.
Too technical, experience given for granted, too many speakers.

analysis.name: Thomas Orlando
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Decent lecturer, very disorganized class. Files were extremely disorganized and deadlines kept moving, there were two textbooks and it was often unclear which one he was referring to. Many exam questions were exact copies of homework questions, but no crib sheet or equation sheet. Letter grade was unknown until the end of the semester.

He attempts to keep us engaged in lectures. He shows derivations in lecture instead of applications, but HW and exams test on both. Weekly HW that's graded on accuracy, but textbook usually has answers. 80% of grade is from exams that reuse HW problems. He'll give more weight to your 2 midterms OR final, whichever you do better on.

Dr. Orlando is a great lecturer, but the class felt disorganized at times due to the nature of notes (no slides, only handwritten notes) and the grading scheme (he doesn't tell you what the A or B cut off is and there's random extra credit and participation points that aren't clear where they end up). Overall, good class but lots of effort needed.

The class/content was just hard itself- thermo/derivations. He posts hand-written lecture notes and goes over them in class; he'll tell you to read (I never did), but he clearly states what will be on his exams. Review sessions were helpful; study the homeworks. There were 2 exams + 1 final with 2 possible grading distributions. EC given.

Has handwritten notes that are really disorganized instead of any PowerPoints. During lectures, he goes on tangents. Tests are difficult but predictable. Extra credit involves reading scientific papers (most of which are his) and reviewing them. Class was fair enough, but it was disorganized, which made it a lot harder.

analysis.name: Olufisayo Omojokun
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 175 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: The lecture videos are pretty brief but cover enough to do the assigned homework. You don't really see the professor much outside of his videos, so your experience is based on your TA (shout out to the head TA in the dual enrollment section). Also, idk who makes the instructions for the final but I had a stroke trying to understand.

This class was essentially entirely TA ran. I only saw the professor during major exams and he rarely answers questions on piazza. His lecture videos were okay but lack details, you're better off finding yt videos online. 80% of the grade depended on 4 exams and a lot of the questions were memorization based and some weren't even relevant.

I tend to prefer asych classes and have performed well in them before. However, this class is horrible. The videos hardly cover the basics and then ur expected to apply that to the really complex hw's. Feels like you are trying to code without rly understanding how or why any of it works, which makes it rly difficult. would not recommend
Tests - 80% of class grade - full of trick questions and/or topics not covered in lecture.

I thought that the amount of effort put into the creation of this class was just pathetic. The lecture videos used are of such poor quality that any random YouTube video would explain the concepts better. It's a complete waste of a class if you are genuinely trying to learn new content (I already knew most of this so online was better). HW was ok

analysis.name: Dmitrii Ostrovskii
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: One of the best math profs I had at GT. Dmitrii is knowledgeable and clear with well-structured notes, plenty of textbook references, and intuitive and interesting examples. He will make you think and put real time in, but well worth it and makes one really learn. Highly recommend PhD students to take a class with him. Prereq in analysis is helpful

Dmitrii Ostrovskii is highly knowledgeable and supportive. He's very accessible outside class and gives great help in office hours, including useful research feedback. He also provides strong resources. The presentation/paper discussion (instead of an exam) was very helpful for grad studies.

You should take his class if you want to do math. I think the bad reviews come from people who expected high school level lectures or dislike math itself. He's very smart, I learned a lot in his class. Lectures were tough, yes —as a math class should— but grading's very soft. And his availability is without exaggeration the best I've had in GT.

Higher effort (and higher reward) than I anticipated. I think he understands what he teaches on a much much deeper level than teaching the class requires. Attendance isn't mandatory, but it's fun to see how passionate he is about the material. Definitely take if you care about getting an A (plenty of opportunities to do well) or you like research.

Prof. Ostrovskii is a fantastic teacher for a challenging subject. He presents high-dimensional statistics with clarity and insight, connects theory to intuition, and is very thoughtful in his explanations.

analysis.name: Olivier Pierron
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Great teacher. Definitely knows his stuff. Entertaining lecturer and lectures are very important. Tests make up 80% of grade and they are never curved so be prepared on test days. Overall very reasonable and makes the class enjoyable.

Pierron was not good for dynamics. It was his 2nd semester teaching it, 90% of grade is from exams (2 midterms, 1 final) and 10% is from HW. HW is just write 2 questions about the problem. Spent too much time deriving equations, attempted examples, didn't finish them and sometimes was wrong. Class attendance dropped so much after a few weeks.

Dr. Pierron is a great professor. While the class itself can present difficult problems, Dr. Pierron's lecture style involves working through a variety of different scenarios using a game plan that can be applied to any statics problem! 90% of your grade is from tests, but he's a fair grader and you know what to expect each time. Caring guy too!

Avoid if bad at physics, otherwise you'll be fine. 2 midterms + 1 final = 90% of grade (9 problems total). Takes off a lot of points for messing up the math, but also gives 70% for just showing you know the process. 
Depends how you look at it, for me it made the tests more stressful and that didn't go well with my other classes.

His lectures were clear and well structured, and the homework was a breeze. However, 90% of the grade was from the exams (40% midterms and 50% final exam), so you absolutely must do well on them. Fortunately, all of the problems are from the textbook, so pracitce well and you should be fine.

analysis.name: Lee Oh
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: There are so many things I want to say but not enough words in the English language to describe how goated she is. All I will say is she has never given a student below an A in her entire history of this course and she gave out max score on every assignment as long as you did it. Goated person and goated course.

I took KOR3415 online with her. The best professor ive had at tech, she is so sweet and genuinely cares about her students. she is very understanding, and her feedback on assignments is so kind. best prof ever

I can not even begin to describe how amazing of a teacher Mrs. Oh is. She is caring, kind, funny, and a great teacher. She always has a smile and never makes anyone feel left out of the class. She wants you to succeed and asks how you are doing even outside of class. 100/10 teacher and would take again if I could!

Professor Oh was incredibly kind, funny, and helpful. She made the class fun with plenty of games and snacks. We moved pretty quickly in lecture but homework was graded easily, so it was easy to make an A in the class if you studied. There was less emphasis on speaking and practice, but she provided office hours for those looking to talk.
One of the best professors at GT! She is quite caring and provides great feedback on assignments. This was an overall easy class but engaging.

analysis.name: Paul Verhaeghen
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This professor is awesome! His lectures are always so interesting and he makes complex content seem so simple! I definitely want him as a professor again!

pay attention to the lectures because virtually all of the exams are based solely on the lectures - his powerpoints are a little confusing to follow. exams are very easy (open note, not proctored, at home). you can tell he's very passionate about his work and psychology which is refreshing for a college course. very nice and easy to talk to.

The course material is fascinating, but Dr. Verhaeghen brings even more fun to the lecture with his quirky personality. Just show up to lecture and do your crib sheet, and you'll be set for the tests.
Awesome professor! Though attendance isn't mandatory, his lectures are so fun that it makes me want to attend voluntarily. Super flexible with grading and assignments. Super funny also.

Dr. V. was very caring and genuinely wanted us to learn how to meditate and practice mindfulness. The class was very easy going. Lectures consisted of meditation and learning about different techniques. Assignments included weekly reflections, a term paper, and two open-note exams. He also offers extra credit and is very responsive via email.

analysis.name: Will Perkins
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: 4 Midterms, 1 Final, 1 of 5 dropped. 80% of grade. Its a tough class and Perkins' poor handwriting and math/textbook heavy lectures makes it harder. His monotone/boring lecture style makes it hard to focus even you do attend. However, his homework's are very similar to the exams which are hard but fair and well written to fit the course material.

Will is great! I agree with the other comments about his handwriting, but because his lectures align so well with the textbook, you don't really need his notes.  The homework can also be a bit hard but the exams only cover the real basics of each unit and with all the partial credit are pretty easy to get A's on.  He's also just a super nice guy!

you can tell Prof. Perkins is a knowledgeable and a nice guy. but he has one of the worst handwritings ive seen at tech (doesn't use slides) and uses exact word for word from textbooks

The HWs and Tests are doable, but they give out the most outrageously terrible practice exams and study guide. Half of it is not his fault; just a terrible course.

He's ok. As other reviewers have said, his handwriting is AWFUL, making class notes very hard to decipher. Verbally the lectures are alright though. Homeworks and Tests are tough. Course communication is lacking, as he doesn't use canvas. He's clearly very knowledgeable but just not the best at making the content digestable.
the class would not be hard if the lecture were actually readable but his handwriting was so bad, the tests and hw were pretty fair but the practice exams caused so much anxiety before the tests

analysis.name: Prabha Padukka
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The availability of Padukka was frankly incredible. The semester I took her, she had a zoom meeting you could join that ran along side the in person lecture. Padukka lectures were also very good. She covered content at a good pace and always allowed opportunities to ask questions. Always willing to help students, even if they needed extra help.

Phys 2211 is very hard  (at least for me) and considered a weed out still but Dr. Padukka truly cares about her students and wants you to pass. Her office hours are helpful and she will even ask in lecture of hundreds of students how she can improve her teaching to help students to better on tests

Super nice! :) She answers all the questions students have in class or during office hours and even offered extra supplemental classes for those who have never done physics before. She does go through problems super fast, sometimes it was hard to keep up. All lectures are streamed online, but it's physics, so go to class or you'll fall behind.

Great lecturer, kind, and always ready to answer any questions. She also streams her lectures if you can't (or don't want to) be there. Make sure to look at the GPS and homework when studying for exams

Pretty straight forward physics class. She is absolutely amazing and super kind. Attendance is part of bucket points so you don't have to show up. Notes for her section and all other sections are posted online. Labs are super annoying, but online and peer graded. Also pretty good late policy.

analysis.name: Matthew Powell
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I would give zero stars if I could. Professor docks points for not showing work in the exact format he has in his head. Students shouldn't be punished for actually understanding the material. If the answer is right, the thinking was right. Avoid if you have any other option. Your grade will reflect his inane standards, not your actual knowledge.

Don't be fooled by the bad reviews. Powell is a very good teacher, multi is just a class that combines linear algebra and calculus so people dont do well. His lectures are very clear and paced well, and you are encouraged to ask questions or solve examples in class. I would definitely reccommend taking his class.

Best professor I had this semester. Very passionate about abstract linear algebra. Exams and quizzes are manageable if you are willing to work. The class was tough due to many abstract concepts but it was fun and worth it. Definitely choose over MATH 1554, but expect to work harder.

Although professor doesn't really matter for large classes, I will say this professor teaches like you're reading a mathematics proof textbook. He introduces topics in a very formal and theorem based way followed by examples I found helpful. It works for some ppl and doesn't for others. He's a knowledgeable guy, but remember it more abt the TAs.

Dr. Powell is one of the greatest professors I've encountered- not only are his lectures phenomenal, they're accessible for people of all ability levels, and he is very approachable for question and clarification- including mid lecture.

analysis.name: Calton PU
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Pu is the most inconsiderate and laziest professor at tech In lecture we watch videos of him softly mumbling slides in a thick accent 2-4 papers due weekly The week where our semester group project proposal was due we had 4 papers due An extension was requested He responded by blaming students whom he called noise makers for gaming his class

He asked us to summarize each lecture in which he only played pre-recorded videos reading each word on the slides out. Two reading assignments on each week requiring one-page commentaries. He was extremely MEAN when commenting on project proposals, showing his perfect mastery of rhetorical questions and sarcasm. DON'T TAKE THIS COURSE!

NEVER TAKE THIS COURSE. Firstly, he is very aggressive and inconsiderate, and any reasonable request is called gaming his course. Secondly, most self-drafted semester-long projects are said to be worthless, and he expects us to produce more creative and better projects than commercial products. Do not let this course be your nightmare.

Despite being somewhat easy, this was by far the WORST class I have ever taken. He just played videos of himself talking during class, which were incredibly boring, unclear, and unnecessary. The requirements for the class are unclear, which he justifies by claiming that its about "autonomous learning." Poorly structured and poorly taught. Beware.

Replays video lectures during in-person class times. Will repeatedly interrupt you during office hours. Dislikes being questioned on the structure of the class to the point of sending long rant-like emails not even a month into the semester. Incredibly time consuming class with most of the difficulty coming from the interactions with the professor.

analysis.name: Charles Peak
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: unorganized + needs a writing class since he's bad at writing coherently and without grammatical/phrasal errors making it harder to answer basic questions. When questions arise during exams, he wastes precious time by simply reading the question again. I also have eyes. That is unhelpful.

He is approachable one-on-one outside of class, but grading is very strict and can feel snarky. Assignments often lack clear guidance, yet points are deducted for minor errors like spelling. The class may feel discouraging, but students can improve by adapting to his expectations.
Snarky and rude. Picky comments and feedback on work. Could/should have shown more kindness towards students. Don't take his class if you're looking for respect.

analysis.name: Hang (Jerry) Qi
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He was super nice, but not the best lecturer. A lot of the example problems were never finished and he does have a bit of an accent which made it hard to understand him. Exams were exactly like the homeworks and you got 3 attempts per question. He was also very generous with partial credit. If you study the practice problems, you should do good.

Great professor. Def bods can be a little rough sometimes, but he is good at explaining the concepts and will go over them again if you ask questions. Would take again 10/10. The homework is from the most recent ed. of the textbook, but I just checked it out of the library when I needed it, and I relied on his lectures and slides for the material.

He's a decent, not great lecturer but has a really good understanding of the material and gives good advice. Tests and homework assignments are very short with multiple attempts per question and generous extra credit. The tests are very heavily weighted and the final is 40% though.

easy to follow if you pay attention in class. very similar to physics; if you understand physics this class will be fine. the only thing is that the class is very test heavy (exam 1 15%, exam 2 25%, and final 40%), but the homework helps set up well for the exam problems

Bad lectures, hard to understand. Left practice problems unfinished. Gave good partial credit on hw and exams. 3 attempts per question on hw and exams. Exam questions came directly from textbook, which had over 100 per chapter. Self study class basically

analysis.name: Qirun Zhang
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Very kind and approachable professor who is always willing to help and accessible during office hours. However, in-class examples were often hard to see due to small writing. Piazza responses were sometimes indirect, and grades were released very late, making it hard to know how I was doing before the drop deadline.

Really nice person, very clearly cares about students. Would even go out of his way to talk to me outside of class. That being said, he's a pretty dry lecturer and he teaches off slides he did not make. He does not answer most piazza questions with anything other than 'talk to me after class or in OH'. However, homeworks and projects are easy.

Professor Zhang is a very good lecturer who describes the content in a very methodical manner. The projects, while really involved, were super interesting, and I feel like I understand a part of Computer Science that was opaque to me before this class.

analysis.name: Moinuddin Qureshi
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Took ECE6100 (x-listed with ECE4100 & CS4290/6290). Lectures are not recorded so attendance is mandatory if you want to do well on exams, though, they are very engaging. Exams are a little tricky but there are ungraded "homeworks" with very similar questions and you can make a crib sheet. Labs are fine if you know C/C++ and are fairly scaffolded.

Awesome lecturer but slides aren't so good and lectures are not recorded. So attendance is mandatory if you actually want to understand content. Also made the first lab worth 4% of final grade due during the first week (while registration is still open). Exams are difficult purely bc of the amount of content you need to know, there is a lot

Great professor! Probably the best lecturer I've had at GT. Teaches with slides but in the most ideal way possible by using them as support, not as a crutch. Projects were fairly simple if you have decent C/C++ knowledge. Tests were a little difficult as they were modeled after the ungraded homeworks, but doable.

Lectures like he's telling a story–makes potentially dry content exciting. Projects were excellent (if a bit hand-holdy), with smooth debugging and problems interesting enough to ponder AFK. Tests felt hard, but there was so much curving and extra credit by the end that lower quartile class grade was a comfy A. Kind prof who will brighten your day!

Took CS6290 (crosslisted 4290/ECE 4100/6100). Lectures extremely engaging and helpful. Tests a bit different than lecture content, but studying previous exams and practicing computations helped. Final was ‘Do-No-Harm'. Projects were well structured with TA debug outs. Small extra credit opportunities were given. Favorite prof at GT, he knows a lot!

analysis.name: Qi Wang
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She is super passionate about film and also extremely educated. The lectures can be boring since she doesn't follow a specific curriculum, but cool. The entire grade is based off attendance, your final, and weekly film screenings. She def gets strict when it comes to the final project and your essay/film ideas. Do NOTTT take it at 5pm

Very sweet and passionate about film. Lecture isn't always the most engaging since she's speaking the whole time. For final projects, there were creative options (short films, poster series) or you could write a 10 page paper. She's always open to questions and is very willing to help or give feedback.

I think Dr. Wang is the victim of a poorly executed curriculum. She is a wonderful and bubbly human being, but she failed to pique my interest in film. Her class is strictly attendance mandatory (25% of grade) but absolutely does NOT need to be at all. She's worth taking as a professor in general, but I would avoid this course specifically.

Professor Wang is sweet and caring. But most of the grade goes to the midterm and final essays, which must be 10+ pages long, personally, I found that a bit annoying. There's a screening and a discussion about it on Canvas every week but you only have to finish 7 discussions for the semester.

Professor Wang is very sweet and cares a lot about her students. Lectures are long but the topics are often interesting and it isn't vital that you pay attention or read the textbook. The only grades are attendance, a weekly discussion post on an assigned movie, and two papers. She is very lenient on extensions for the papers and easy to contact.

analysis.name: Pamela Pollet
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 124 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Pollet is a pretty epic teacher. She has a wonderful french accént and tests are fine. They're often similar to the practice tests with the exception of the occasional curveball. Pollet does however like giving out extra credit for CIOS and midterm surveys. The PRS can be annoying at times as attendance and correctness matters but ok.

She is a good chemistry professor who wants her students to do well. There was a TON of extra credit given throughout the semester, that you didn't have to do too well on exams to get an A. However lectures are kinda disorganized. She jumps in the topic and goes too fast without giving a brief overview.

Cares about her students and tries to make class fun. She does move very quickly but she suggests reading the textbook before class (which I never did). Exams are easy since they are identical to practice tests which are posted online, along with worksheet solutions. She's ready to answer your questions after class. She's a bit disorganized.

Pre-Lecture videos are posted for each chapter - very helpful to watch before class since the course covers a good bit of material. Clicker questions every class for a grade. Every test had at least 5 bonus points to be earned; she is generous with CIOS points/midterm survey points when it comes to exams. The class was initially curved.

She obviously loves the subject and cares a lot about her students. The course covers material quickly, but she does a HUGE amount of things to help us (recording lecture, posting notes, solutions, answering Piazza, etc.). She probably puts as much time outside class into the course as her students spend studying for it. 10/10

analysis.name: Qiqin Xie
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The professor's grading structure has changed from previous years; there is no EC on quizzes and only a little on exams. The content and lectures are mind-numbingly boring. Homework is not graded so the exams are weighted heavily. I went to her office hours twice, once she was late the other time she did not show up.

Lectures aren't the most exciting but cover everything on the tests. Helpful but infrequent office hours. Generous class policies/extra credit and the tests are reasonable but not easy by any means. Can be hard to follow the lectures because they move so fast and cover so many topics, but that's just combo for you. Would recommend her in general.

She gives a HUGE amount of extra credit that it's almost impossible not to make an A. She is a great lecturer and explains concepts clearly, and she's very good at explaining what you're expected to know for exams/quizzes. She gives 20 pts extra credit on quizzes and 100 pts (yes, 100 pts) extra credit on tests. You can exempt the final (95+ avg)

Theres no extra credit on quizzes, only 20-30 points on tests (but its usually EXTREMELY hard to earn even one of these). Quizzes are weekly and difficult, and theres only two tests and a final besides that. She does give other extra credit opportunities that I would recommend taking advantage of. Its a hard class but I heard she's the easiest.

Weekly quizzes are time-consuming to prep for but not bad if you review lecture notes. The textbook isn't bad for this course but I mainly prepped for assessments using her lecture notes. For her exams, the best way to study for them is to go through the practice questions released before each exam (problems mimic those practice questions).

analysis.name: Dong Qin
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Qin puts in a lot of effort to be accessible and helpful for students. She cares that students learn the material and tries to keep interest high in the content. Tests are relatively straightforward if you read the textbook and lecture notes, but grading is very strict which can make getting high grades difficult.

As person, I liked Dr. Qin. She loves talking to students and having them show up to office hours. However, her lectures can be confusing and she doesnt explain concepts well. The quizzes are alright, and exams are pretty easy.

Dr. Qin is SO caring and gives great lectures. However, she's a very tough grader, and oftentimes expectations for assignments weren't super clear because of that. The expectations are high and can be tough to meet. Overall, I learned a lot from her lectures and assignments but this class will be more effort than you expect if you are an undergrad.

Qin is great, nice, & helpful. KEY TO AN A: During her lectures and office hours, if you listen to her, you'll hear tons of hints as to what will be on the test and by the time it shows up, you'll basically know what exactly is on it. The tests and quizes are also basically the exact same every semester so just study them & you'll do great.

There are quizzes every week, so make sure you're in class on those days. Her tests are EXACTLY like her practice tests so if you memorize those and past quiz information, you should be all set for tests. However, she is a super hard grader so if you miss even the smallest detail it's possible you only get half-credit for the question. Super nice!

analysis.name: Tobias Ried
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: It's his first year teaching an American class. A lot of the current reviews were written just after Exam 1. He saw we struggled on Exam 1, sent us a very heartfelt apology, made the hard questions extra credit, and made our second exam more in line with other sections. He's not an amazing lecturer, but he's a very nice guy who clearly cares a lot.

He really cares about his students and is very passionate about teaching. After a rough exam 1, he was very generous and gave a bunch of extra credit. He asked how he can better prepare us for the next exam, and answered students' requests by putting practice problem sets in Canvas that accurately reflected future exams.

I am pretty sure this is his first class, so he didn't really have a great grasp of what type of exam to give. He sounds like a nice guy in class, but the first exam was diabolical. There are a lot of improvements he can and should make as a professor overall, but outside of that exam, I cant really hate him. Pray in his next class he improves.

I will say this. Professor Reid is a very kind and caring man, and he genuinely does seem like he wants success for his class. I emailed him to speak a bit louder and a tiny bit slower during lectures, and the very next day he made the improvement. That said, he operates using the European style of teaching, which can be rough if you're like me.

Super nice person and professor. He very passionate about what he teaches and you can tell. However, if all differential classes were theory heavy I wouldn't have a problem, but comparing test to different sections it's kind of ridiculous. If you like theory take it with him, if you want an easier A just take it with someone else.

analysis.name: Suhasjain Suresh
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: solid prof, made the class engaging and easy

Made a really hard topic very digestible to someone who has never seen any of the class material before. Tests were just as difficult if not easier than the homework problems, which made the class much less stressful. Would definitely take one of his classes again.

He was very kind to students, lectures are well organized and very clear. He uses great examples and lectures are very interactive. HW are not very hard and they help you undertsnad the topcis better,

analysis.name: Turab Zaidi
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 67 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Decent at actual teaching; however, the class is filled with too many arbitrary rules. Grading for homework and tests is done harshly, although tests are fair. Homeworks are very lengthy and demanding. His class policies are uncompromising and he is unwilling to accommodate special circumstances. Do not take if you plan on traveling at GTL.

Exam 1 & 2 (each): 13.3%; Quizzes (3): 13.3%; Individual HW: 20%; Group HW: 10%; Final: 23.3%; Attendance: 6.6%. Thermo is tough. However Zaidi makes it feel "achievable". He truly cares about understanding the material and it shows with his personality in an 8 a.m. lecture. Quizzes and Tests were tough but clear. Would take him 100% again!!

Thermo is a tough class, but Zaidi is a really good lecturer and clearly cares about his students doing well and learning the material. His attendance policy is pretty strict and homeworks can be a little tricky sometimes, but exams are fair and only cover the material we learned in class.

Amazing professor, but he's not for everyone. His grading is tough but he clearly cares about your learning. He gives a lot of extra credit & will sometimes post lecture recordings, but don't skip class. There are a few group HWs & several long individual HWs.

The two major projects just throw you in the deep end with little knowledge on how to do them but just ask someone at the makerspace and they'll tell you know to do it. Just do all assignments and it's an easy A, just more work than necessary for the 2 major projects. He also very clearly loves his job.

analysis.name: Tatiana Rudchenko
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 83 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Rudchenko means well, she wants to help and will do what she can to do so, but she has very poor communication skills. She, the accent is part of it, but even besides that she can make manageable concepts much more complicated. But the material itself is pretty easy.

This class is a lot of easy busywork. Exams were exactly like practice tests that were also required for a grade. 3+ assignments a week, including an asynchronous friday class and many poorly made videos. Several times the class detours into hyping ChatGPT rather than the relevant content. Ruchenko is nice but hard to understand and out of touch.

I took 2250 with her, very easy so I took 2255 asynchronous over the summer. Similar difficulty to 2050, not bad. Just learn how to do the homework and memorize the excel formulas before exams and you will do well. Dr Rudchenko is so sweet and truly cares about her students. Loves talking about AI for some reason. Take her over any other prof!

Dr. Rudchenko was very passionate about the material, and she always sought to keep the class engaged. She made the lecture slides and videos easily accessible, so if we had to miss class for some reason we could still complete the excel assignment outside of class and get full credit for that day. Exams are easy if u do the hw and practice tests

Class is more work than needed. Tests are on MyLab (Pearson) and are relatively similar to practice tests and previous HW questions, so I'd recommend using those to study. If you go to class, do the HW assignments, and make a good cheat sheet based on everything in the HW, practice tests, you'll probably end with an A. Still a lot of work though.

analysis.name: Tianchi Yang
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Very difficult to understand and handwriting during class is tough to decipher. Took the class based on reviews before mine but he must have changed things because the exams were nothing like the practice or lecture and ridiculously difficult. When approached about why exams were so difficult he mumbled something about "figuring it out". AVOID HIM!

Easy exams (literally, study idk what to tell you). Not great lecturer, but the content is easy enough that you can learn it all the week before the test by reading the notes and do fine (I did this and got 100s). Really easy to get a good grade. He also doesn't require attendance. Homework takes, I kid you not, 20 minutes MAX a week.

Administered this class incredibly well by himself (no TA). Publishes handwritten and typeset notes for each lecture. HW/exam solutions are posted promptly (even before grades are returned), and grading is generous. Clear topic lists and past exams with solutions make exams very approachable. Lectures are textbook-definition-oriented, which I like.

Just got done taking the hardest midterm of my life. Talked to friends in other sections whose exams where SIGNIFICANTLY easier. Has an atrocious accent. Only good thing about him is he responds to Ed posts pretty quickly

Well-organized professor, communicates class information and requirements clearly. Has written and typeset notes available after each lecture. Exams don't feel like overloaded mistake minefields, and past exams make them easy to study for.

analysis.name: Alexey Tumanov
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He seems to care a lot about the source material, but it was a struggle to follow. The projects are absurdly time consuming and the instructions were unclear. If a certain few TAs didn't exist this class would be impossible if you're new to the topic. Lots of information but I feel like I barely gained any knowledge due to the lack of clarity.

Terrible Professor and TAs, I did not enjoy the class, he was very unhelpful with matters such as labs and especially exams, my online exam refreshed 5 times but they blamed it on me, no help provided. The professors tone on emails seemed very unwelcoming and unfriendly. Labs were insanely long and expected effort was not correctly disclosed.

The professor was horrendous at teaching and not helpful whatsoever. The TAs provided limited help and didn't seem to care much, just like the professor. It could've been a good class but alas it wasn't. Please avoid this class, the course content is sub-par, the difficulty is insane and expectations are unrealistic.

Really interesting lectures, but I recommend this class be avoided if at all possible: the projects take absurd amounts of time. I typically spent in excess of 15 hours per week working on them. The project specs are always very unclear, and getting clarifications out of the course staff is time-consuming, often futile, and invariably frustrating.

Absolutely awful at teaching, and extremely unhelpful with clarifications on the homework's or the subject matter. None of the TA's knew what they were doing and made the already difficult class that much harder. The expectations in this class were impractical. And the professors attitude in an out of the class was overall negative.

analysis.name: Sedina Tsikata
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Tsikata is very caring and helpful. For fluid mechanics, whilst attendance isn't mandatory, you will really be screwed if you miss a lecture! Also, the lectures themselves are quite long and have SO MUCH material, so I personally found it difficult to digest all of the information and feel comfortable for the exams.

Homework 40%, 2 Midterms 15% each, Final 30%. Lectures were boring, and slides had a lot of information, but not all of it was necessary. Grading took forever. Concepts were difficult, but she was nice and cared. A seemed impossible after M2, but there was a lot of extra credit at the end to get points back on the midterm and a curve for the final.

Short Answer: Only take if you don't want to learn the subject or want an easy class. DO NOT TAKE HER IF YOU WANT TO LEARN.

Dr. Tsikata is by far my least favorite professor I have had at GT. She does not care about you or teaching. She showed up late to class routinely and constantly had excuses for severely delayed grading and posting solutions.

Dr. Tsikata is a great human being. Her lecture slides can be somewhat uninspired, but she deeply cares about her students. I learned a great deal in her class. She is very busy, so she may seem distant at times due to this. I would recommend her still.

Often unreachable and condescending. She's straight up said she wouldn't respond to emails after I told her she had missed mine for a couple weeks. The one midterm we had was overtly difficult and no one finished in the allotted time. The content wasn't bad but the professor made it worse than it had to be

analysis.name: Thomas Collins
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 43 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: There were 2 projects with opportunities for extra credit if you put in significantly  more work. Imo project 2 way easier than project 1. The first half of the semester was insanely easy but everything is concentrated in Late October->December so plan for that. He has a tendency to not understand your question so you need to be specific.

2 projects with plenty of extra credit. All lecture slides are online. Make sure to start projects and homework early. Plenty of practice tests available on canvas. Office hours help a lot from what I have heard. Great professor, but I have heard Wills might be slightly better, but both are great. Pretty easy class, not very test heavy.

Pretty good professor, makes it very clear whats going to be on the exams. the 2 projects are weighted the same as the 3 midterms, so gotta start those projects early. Lots of opportunity for extra credit with the projects, and very lenient late policy.

Skip the pointless reading from Rapid Prototyping and lecture. Labs are as simple as following the (confusing) lab manual. Second practical exam was basically impossible, and the ONE exam asks about details so specific they're basically irrelevant. Extremely condescending when asked about grading mistakes. Pre-labs and lab reports are lengthy.
A really enjoyable and light class. Exams are extremely fair and there is ample opportunity to get extra credit on the two projects. Though, both of them are pretty time consuming. Highly recommended

analysis.name: Umakishore Ramachandran
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 76 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I genuinely don't understand all these horrible reviews. Ramachandran clearly knows his stuff, and it shows. Most people's issue seems to be that the class is tough. I can't stand when bum students blame professors instead of putting in the work to master hard concepts. There are countless resources to help you succeed.

I'm sure Kishore means well - but that's truly not enough for a course with such heavy and important content. Lectures are meaningless as Kishore tends to come unprepared and start lecture late, go on unrelated ramblings speak extremely fast and annotate powerpoint slides in such a fashion that no one can understand what is supposed to be learned.

He is a very nice guy, and super understanding and helpful one on one. But his class is really hard and he goes through his powerpoint slides (which haven't changed since the 90s) really quickly. He doesn't understand questions in class, and always has mandatory clicker questions. TAs for this class are useless. So good luck to you.

The concepts covered in this course are tremendously important for software engineers. Unfortunately, it's taught horrendously. The course needs to be entirely revamped, and steer far clear from the rote learning and mindless calculation path that it's currently on.

Kishore is not a great lecturer. slides are messy, often rambles is confusing, and just uses point solutions to force students to come. Most people watch Daglis' lectures instead, which are far more coherent. 2200 is probably the hardest class I've taken at Tech, exams are difficult and they grade Ed participation to make up for no TA involvement.

analysis.name: Richard Utz
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Utz is a very passionate professor, and I would recommend him to everyone. He truly cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He does have pop quizzes based on the books; however, they are very basic, and if you have read the text, you should do well on them. He is a bit eccentric (in a good way) and very encouraging!!
W prof. I was concerned that I wouldn't get an A by the end of the semester and I really shouldn't have mathematically, but I still did.

While Dr. Utz can be a bit of a handful sometimes, if you can meet him at his level, he is an incredibly intelligent, witty, and kind professor. He is a bit eccentric (which I like) but knows what he's talking about. He clearly cares about student success in and out of the classroom. Worth taking in my opinion, but not for everyone.

Holy respect on this guy. He used to be Dean of Ivan Allen and is now the assistant dean, so he has a ton of knowledge about LMC. This class is an intro to LMC class, so we get a taste of the faculty under LMC. He's lenient when it comes to grading as long as you follow ALL his instructions. Very engaging with the class, also has fun stories

TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!! He's such an easy grader. Wants everyone to succeed and is always available outside of class. You'll have an assignment due about once a month. Two solo and one group presentation. No homework, test, or quizzes. Extra credit if you activity participate. Class is "mandatory" but wont dock your grade if you don't show up.

analysis.name: Jun Ueda
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is a great professor, young and friendly. Never shows arrogance nor does torment you with abstract math. Although I sometimes couldn't understand his lectures due to his accent I go back and watched lectures again, which made so much sense. Prepares you well for the quizzes and exams. Easy A, but you have to actively check Canvas for any changes because the dates change a lot. analysis.name: Jerry Ulrich

Take Uelzmann!

Please do not take this guy. He could be an expert in his field, but the problem is you don't know what he's talking about. He is so mind numbing and boring. I've seen sessions where less than 10 people are in class. The only reason people show up to class is due to the attendance quizzes.

Very Monotone, and very quiet professor. Used to finish lectures 30-45 minutes early. However, class participation dwindled from 300 students (plus waitlist) to about 10 students. Professor is very hard to listen to and learn information from. TAs + other professor were great.

analysis.name: Cindy Xiong
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Xiong is a good professor who makes lectures enjoyable. The class is straightforward, with weekly assignments due Fridays and two tests. Assignments focus on HTML, CSS, and JS for data visualization, while tests cover lecture material. Attendance is technically "required", but slides are posted online, so it's manageable if you miss class.

Cindy Xiong is a good presenter. Most hws were about coding in HTML, CSS, and Javascript and working with D3. They weren't too bad but we weren't given any instruction during class on how to use D3 so you have to figure it out on your own. There are two exams, no finals. The class finishes before Thanksgiving so that is nice. Would recommend class.

Super chill professor, she has interesting lectures which are easy to follow, especially with the countless examples she gives. The homeworks are intriguing but not too hard and the labs are available through Git and pretty self-explanatory. Only 2 tests and the class ends before Thanksgiving. Overall would recommend.

analysis.name: Shuman Xia
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Shuman is an excellent choice for Statics. Lectures are done on whiteboard and are very engaging. Explains concepts really well and goes over old physics/math concepts if you need. Homework is on WileyPlus and takes 2-3 hours a week max. Exams are 88% but are very easy if you do the homeworks. TAs are also great if you even need help.

Dr. Xia is caring, yes, but it can be hard to stay engaged during his lectures. I might be biased because I had lecture at Kendeda, and it was hard to understand him due to a combination of his thick accent and loud air vents in the building. The TAs were helpful.

Great guy and good lectures, though they are long and packed with info. He is not the best at explaining concepts or helping with homework during office hours but hes genuine and is there to help. Tests are hard but he is a very generous grader which helps a lot. overall good

Shumans lectures were very good, he could simplify concepts into digestible ideas. I took in the summer asynchronously, 88% of grade comes from tests (2 midterms and 1 final), 12% comes from HW. HW wasn't too much, typically one HW a week through wileyPLUS. Provided practice exams and a practice final. Great professor to take statics with.

Took him for summer online course. He was one of the best professors I have taken at Tech. Gave good lectures, didn't waste any time, solved example problems in class, gave fair quizzes. Not too many homework but could take some time, but he was always available to help even via email. Would recommend to everyone!

analysis.name: Lei Xu
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: she def cares but sometimes things get lost in communication. lectures are boring and long and tend to focus too much time on things that dont matter while the important parts get looked over quickly. she is always willing to help. the tests are fair but hard. she tells u what the frq is on and the mc is just a gamble that you hope and pray on.
Overall an ok prof. Communication can be hard because sometimes because her native language is chinese. The lectures are very long, a lot of self study to get a good grade.

She's a great person, but her native language is Chinese, so she's not very good at explaining concepts in English. Sometimes kids would ask questions and she would just repeat what she said earlier. If you're fluent in Chinese, there were some kids who apparently got a lot from learning with her one-on-one. Otherwise, self-study.

analysis.name: Helen Xu

Everything is either lifted from previous semesters or from MIT. Terrible lectures and the slides barely help. The exams have no rights being as hard as they were given the teaching quality

Exams were pretty difficult, but do-able, and consistently had averages in the 60's. The last programming assignment required in-depth C++ knowledge.

Very cool prof, but the course structure is terrible. Packs too much information per lecture. If you are taking many courses or have major research priorities, this course will leave you learning most things very superficially, except MPI. Programming assignments (26% of grade) are challenging & graded unnecessarily strictly (no partial credit).

Grad and undergrad sections have exactly the same hw and exams - this is a grad-level course. Prof assumes you already have extensive CS knowledge and is awful at explaining complex concepts - as a CS minor, this is the hardest class I have ever taken. If you are forced to take this class, be prepared to put in an insane amount of effort.

Class is not nearly as hard as people make it out to be. You just have to study. interactive lecture model sucks. barely gives any notice and expects us to make time.

attendnace at lecture is mandatory but I couldn't focus on his lectures or follow him most of the times he talks about topics as if students should already know about it, so I used the textbook and online resources to teach myself a lot of the topics there are long weekly hw that usually don't add anything to test prep, but focus on the sample exam

not an easy class by any means, but hillegass is a great lecturer who clearly knows and cares about the material. while i didn't get to interact with him directly, i've heard that he is very personable. there were some hiccups at the beginning of the semester, but he was more than fair with correcting and accounting for any issues with the course.

all-around good guy. he knows this class is insanely difficult and time-consuming, and is trying his best to make it bearable. the TAs really carry this class on their backs; i was practically camped out in office hours every single week. class is fun, but expect it to be your heaviest workload by FAR.

analysis.name: Aaron Lanterman

He's goofy, but in a very helpful way.  Great class!! Also there is a lot of emphasis on the lab and homework, so one bad test won't kill you.  No curve in my class.

analysis.name: Aaron Santesso

review_highlights.comment: Santesso is a great professor for LMC2000! He cares a lot about his work and makes assignments feel meaningful and directly related to all the texts gone over in class. The material is very interesting as it's mostly focused on satires in different mediums. Overall, the class requires dedication as the essays are long. Considering his lectures are very fascinating (& him saying B= "very very very good" but A= "exceptional"/"wow"), I recommend him to anyone wanting fun, a push or a B.

i think someone else mentioned but hes a good professor but i just didnt really vibe with him but thats different for everbody. why did i just find out he has a wikipedia page? He tears into your paper but dont take it personally; dont think your writing is goated he'll knock you off that peg.

I would say my only "issue" was that he did not use Canvas for grades, so you need to keep track of your own and do your own calculations. Also, participation in class matters!

analysis.name: Aditi Das
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Das connects course material to real-world examples. She occasionally goes on tangents, drawing on her own experiences and broader scientific topics which makes the class fun. The class required significant studying. I appreciated the open-note format, though she mentioned that future offerings may be closed to internet access.

Instructor was an expert in the subject matter and taught with a lot of enthusiasm. There was lot of opportunities to score through homework, quizzes, and open exams to promote conceptual learning. However the lectures was fast pace with occasional misalignment between lectures and exams. The FRQ portion of the exams were hard.

The class was engaging and rewarding . Dr. Das's enthusiasm and emphasis on understanding the “why” behind complex pathways helped me move beyond memorization. The course felt like a meaningful exploration of metabolism pathway and strengthened my appreciation for biochemistry as I pursue medical school.

This class prepared me for metabolism and the TCA cycle, which is great for MCAT. Real-life examples made complex ideas fun and memorable. She didn't make us memorize TCA cycle which was a big relief.  The mechanistic approach in the class and challenging ‘what if' questions pushed my thinking. Overall, I liked the class.

Course was reasonably organized, engaging, and intellectually stimulating. It is application-based, with problem sets and exams that emphasize critical thinking. There are also a lot of easy quizzes. The professor is supportive and creates an inclusive environment. Exams are challenging and office hours are helpful. Gets you ready for med school.

This rating is meant to help future students as well as Adrian Gardiner if he is reading this:
The teacher only taught about theory in the class, speaking at about 15 words per minute. He taught a total of about 3 classes on the technicals of excel and SQL which is OUTRAGEOUS considering the homeworks included FAR more than what we learned in class

Dr. Adibi is a fantastic lecturer who is clearly very passionate about the material in this course. Participation can grant you extra credit. analysis.name: Alexander Adams

Awesome summer class! Learned so much about sensing methods and designing future devices. Assignments were engaging, and Prof. Adams was generous with guidance and resources. I really enjoyed Health Sensing and Interventions with Professor Adams. The class was interactive and project-focused, with hands-on work using real health sensing hardware.
