Even with GT documentation, he will not follow up for exam remakes. Class grade comprised of exams only and two random concept quizzes. Poorly paced and condescending. Tests don't reflect content.

I'm guessing that the difference between current and previous semesters was the modality, but if you can take him in person, avoid it if you can. Lectures were extremely poorly paced, and tests were badly designed, which doesn't make sense for a class almost entirely graded by exams. Very little structuring or support materials, and no crib sheets.

Lectures were super disorganized and the slides were super unhelpful for studying. He speaks so quickly, has really poor transitions between concepts, and just does not explain things well. I probably learned 5% of this class from him and the 95% rest from YouTube. Exams were fairly easy but there was basically 0 review/prep material for them
This class is so weird. Nothing feels to match up and exams take up so much of the grade. If you can take another class, do it!
Super bad lectures and exams. Cant understand anything he is saying and then exams are completely different.

analysis.name: Adam Steinberg
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Steinberg is phenomenal. AE2010 thermo-fluids is an extremely difficult course, but Steinberg made the material very clear. The homeworks are hard, as are the tests, but the TAs and professor grade rather generously. The lectures are optional, but I strongly recommend going. If it is too early for you, the professor posts the lectures online.

Genuinely great professor. The course isn't easy, but Steinberg really does his best to make sure his students understand both conceptually and practically. As long you as also put in the same effort as he does, you'll do fine. Tests are open note, open book, so they can get pretty difficult

Steinberg was a great professor, and his lecture style was beneficial to my learning. He explains concepts which we then apply in the homeworks (41% of total grade), but also does a few basic examples in class to help students. Tests are extremely difficult, but open notes and textbook, and he is a very lenient grader. Would recommend taking him

Dr. Steinberg is a decent professor. Early on, he mainly lectures without examples, making concepts harder to apply. However, he improves over time, balancing examples and lectures better. Homework is challenging and heavily weighted. Exams are very tough, but the class is curved, so doing well is possible if you do a LOT of practice.
Grades incredibly harshly, test averages were in the low 60's high 50's. I took the course since many people gave him a high RMP rating, but I honestly regretted taking thermo with him.

analysis.name: Adam Decker
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 106 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: His ratings are high for a reason. He makes lectures for a course that is almost strictly memorization entertaining. Anatomy always ends up with the worst lecture times and locations but it is always worth going. Attendance isn't mandatory, but I would strongly recommend going as he sometimes tests material not in the slides. Very caring guy too.

Hands down my favorite course at GT. I appreciated the course was very challenging and I was up for it. Dr. Decker takes difficult concepts and breaks them down in a unique way so we understand. We just finished drawing the brachial plexus and although challenging it was fun to draw along with him on the whiteboard. I can't wait for Human Pathology

I was really struggling with anatomy and school/life  in general. He was the only professor that took the time with me outside of class to help me. I will forever be grateful for this man. I wish more professors on campus cared half as much as Dr. Decker did.

WE LOVE DR. DECKER! Genuinely the best prof I've had at GT. Lectures are engaging, go to them! Even if you can pass the class without attending, the things he says in person will stick with you for the rest of your medical career. Exams are a bit tough, make sure you deeply understand the content and are not just memorizing. Flashcards are a must!

Had him online for short summer session. His teaching format was powerpoints with attached audio narration on each slide. He seems very passionate about what he does, which makes the lectures interesting and engaging. He also adds some hilarious jokes in there. Really cool. Down to earth. The assignments teaches you about yourself. Take good notes.

analysis.name: Ian Afflerbach
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Afflerbach is the kindest and coolest professor I have had so far. His classes are very interesting, and the projects assigned are very manageable. Though there is a lot of outside reading, be sure to do it so you can participate in class. 20% of the grade is participation. Afflerbach is very responsive to your comments in class and is  helpful

Dr. Afflerbach is great. Interesting/engaging lectures. While he can be a little bit of a tough grader on some things the main thing he's looking for is effort. If he sees you're trying, you will be rewarded. Any time I needed help or had any questions his feedback was always EXTREMELY helpful. I would recommend his class.

Dr. Afflerbach was an amazing English teacher! You can really tell he is passionate about teaching. Although there was a lot of reading, it was interesting and the discussions we had in class were always great. And go to office hours! He always gives very helpful feedback and seems to genuinely care about his students.

Dr. A is hands down one of the best teachers I've had. His class is structured as a discussion that he facilitates incredibly well. He's knowledgeable,  fair and engaging. He sincerely wants to help you succeed as long as he sees your efforts.

If I had another English class to take, I would 100% take another class Afflerbach taught. If you need help, stop by office hours. They make a huge difference. He is very responsive to emails as well!

analysis.name: Agniva Roy
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof Roy's classes and homeworks were very proof heavy, but the exams were pretty easy. He knows the material pretty well and really cares about his students. The exams often had extra credit too. He spent some time reviewing 1553/4, so there was only a little bit I had to do by myself. If you got through 1553/4 ok, this class won't be bad at all.

Professor Roy is incredibly understanding and cares about his students - he was one of the only professors to modify the class and communicate with us clearly when we moved to remote learning. His lectures are interesting, and the weekly assignments aren't difficult. Exams are straightforward and fair, just study the lecture notes and do the HW.

Professor Roy truly cares about his students. He is very understanding and will accommodate to his students as requested. His class is distributed by the homework, midterm, and final exam. You need to go to class and follow the textbook or you will be lost. As long as you work hard, you will get the grade you deserve. 10/10 TAKE THIS CLASS

Professor Roy is a great professor with very reasonable grading criteria and class structure. He is a solid lecturer, and I would highly recommend him to other students. As long as you keep up with the material and stay consistent, you will do fine in this course.

analysis.name: Pradeep Agrawal
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: AMAZING professor. You will here stories about this class, and while he is an extremely difficult professor, he is an excellent lecturer and is extremely willing to help you out! Also, if you put in the effort, a B is atleast manageable, because he has an enormous curve (anywhere above a 65 should guarantee you atleast a B)

Although Dr. Agrawal does give difficult tests, he is a great lecturer and very willing to help you during his office hours. You will learn so much in the class and taking a class with Dr. Agrawal is very worthwhile. Definitely one of the best lecturers in the chemical engineering department.
Worst professor ever. English is bad and he cannot hear you too. Homework grading is harsh and unreasonable. Exam is hard too.

analysis.name: Ahmed Saeed
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The professor is knowledgeable about Networking, but the course management was lacking. ALWAYS REQUEST REGRADES for homework, as TAs rely HEAVILY on the autograder. The professor's handwriting is VERY hard to read, and lectures focus on concepts while exams are calculation-heavy. The midterm had unfair conditions that the take-home didn't balance.

Take-home midterm did not offset the unexpected technical difficulties of the original midterm, which had unfair testing conditions. Lack of feedback on HW and exams; many unanswered Ed posts. TAs/prof gave misleading info about HW/exam questions. Lectures are very conceptual while HW/exams are very computational. Prof Ahmed is pretty solid though.

Spam regrade requests on EVERYTHING! Make up any reason or else they'll never give u partial bc TAs only autograde (half can't even explain anything). Pray u don't have to talk to the prof bc he does not care. Take a diff prof, others are actually nice & don't expect u to "already know the answer" to the HW (which is why they never release answers)

Professor is super passionate about the material. Lecture notes are not great and the textbook is hard to read. Exams are super content heavy so its best to stay on top of it individually. Homeworks aren't that great of a prep resource as  hws use wireshark and terminal which aren't tested on exams. Programming Assignments are not really useful.

Passionate professor who cares about networking and his students. Admits his mistakes clearly and works with students when they have issues. Handwriting in notes can be hard to read / understand sometimes though. Tests ended up being pretty hard (Fall 2025) but they got curved pretty hard so it ended up being fine

analysis.name: Ahmed Ahmed
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Extremely easy class. The summer online class is asynch with a couple of weekly assignments. Each week, you have reading quizzes (very light) and discussion posts. The only major assignment was the final "exam", in which you had to create a presentation on one of the multiple Arabic topics learned. Overall, the class was very easy, and I recommend!

I took his class for ARBC 3501 (Men-Women in Islam) and I really enjoyed the class. Probably the easiest option for a humanities credit. Sometimes assignments could be annoying but even the slightest effort can get you an A. Also very understanding and let me turn in a lot of stuff almost a week late.

Prof. Ahmed was a very helpful and respectful professor who made this class an enjoyable experience for his students. You have to show up to class and you get 3 absences before it affects your grade. The quizzes are not worth much and are easy. Just participate and you should get an A for both 1001 and 1002. Great professor and cool class!

Great professor! He does a good job of teaching Arabic basics and providing lots of different types of practice (reading, listening, speaking, etc). At first the class was intimidating since many people were already able to read Arabic, but I felt much more confident by the end of the semester. Very welcoming class environment!

Prof. Ahmed is so so kind and really caring. Sometimes the lectures are sporadic as theyre based on what students need, which was more difficult for me. No previous experience for me, so definitely had to put in work. Once we sat in the dark and just relaxed for a bit during a miserable hell week. Prof Ahmed is so sweet and it was a great class.

analysis.name: Mustaq Ahamad
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This professor has vague expectations.  He does not grade anything in his courses, yet claims that each assignment is crucial.  He does not teach anything, and he often invites guest faculty to lecture.  Final grades are arbitrary based on how much he likes you.  If you're an InfoSec major, good luck because this professor's courses are mandatory.

I'm giving him +1 pity point because he comes off as a nice genuine guy. His lectures are extremely dull and dry. He took an interesting topic and made it as boring as possible. Another major flaw was that all the projects were very poorly written and outdated. Errors in those instructions probably wasted hundreds of man hours across all students.

This professor is unclear and not helpful. He is unaware of what he is discussing in class and forgets what he tells students. He is not consistent with his grading, and changes his standards of grading each week without telling students. He does not understand the meaning of communication. Good Luck, avoid a class with this professor if you can.

I took him for Secure Computer Systems and found him to be knowledgeable with great recorded lectures (online). Two exams are worth 60% of your grade, but grades on a curve based on class performance. There is a quiz each week (worst 3 are dropped) and 4 projects ranging from easy to hard (proj4, start early). I learned a lot, would recommend.

His class is pretty useless, and his lectures are dry and boring. All you do is read boring papers that you learn almost nothing from. I did learn a little bit from the projects, though. I think his grading is predeterminedno matter what you do or don't do, it seems he's already decided what he's going to give you. Avoid if possible.

analysis.name: Krishan Ahuja
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: His course consists of filling in the blanks in his lecture slides. It's pretty boring. Mac-PC compatibility messed the pictures up. All in All pretty good.

He is an OK professor. His tests are almost easy if you have good memory. He is very quick in teaching, doesnt explain alot. always says "I dont have time to go in detail, please refer to you textbook". Tests consists of fill in the blanks which are directly from his slides, and the rest is problems. Thermo is supposed to be hard. but it was easy!

Prof Ahuja is your good old-fashioned professor. He goes over the material quickly, and often refers to the textbook, which you can for tables. The slides are often a mess, which requires a better understanding of the subject. However, the tests and quizzes are very doable. You can get an A in the class, just make sure not to fall behind.

Dr. Ahuja is an expert on aeroacoustics. His lecture slides are very organized and handy to use for whatever purpose. He doesn't go through details in lecture so after-class reading is important, even though the exams are really easy. Be intuitive and active in his class!

analysis.name: Ahmet Uzer
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: If you go to Georgia Tech, you HAVE to take a class with Uzer - you'd be missing out on so much otherwise!

Really funny guy, a warm, helpful professor who clearly loves what he does and wants nothing more than to make you understand the material. If you ever have the chance to take Uzer, you will not regret it.

The class in itself was pretty much a joke, but Uzer was an awesome prof. He is the ideal "college lecturer", meaning he's great at teaching the material and keeping you interested, but he's not available outside of lecture. HILLARIOUS! If anything, go to class for his jokes. (By the way, he looks like a crazy Ben Stein). Very easy class overall.

The class is hard, but it isn't Uzer's fault. He explains the material VERY well. The tests are REALLY difficult, but all of them are. There is a lot of homework, but it's manageable. Whatever you do, DO THE BONUS HOMEWORK. It seems like a hassle, but it is definitely worth it. Uzer knows his stuff, and he's really funny. I recommend taking him.

Insanely difficult class, but he definitely taught me how to think more like a physicist. He will take the time to make sure you understand the material, but he'll grade you as if you're taking classical mechanics, not intro physics. Very funny and intelligent. He will likely remain one of my favorite professors.

analysis.name: Mishal Ahmed
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Great professor. Attendance is taken randomly over the semester. All material is covered in lectures, textbook is not necessary at all. All tests and final exam are all multiple choice, and they're all pretty straightforward (there will be one or two trick questions though). Overall a very fair professor. If you show up and pay attention, easy A.

Homework is just the right difficulty, enough to keep a solid grade and still learn a lot. Tests are all multiple choice, and he drops your lowest. Final is cumulative. Possible extra credit from CIOS. I don't like random attendance, especially for an easy class like this, but that is whatever. Good lecturer, you learn all you need to in class.
He clearly cares about students and what they think of the course, responds well to feedback.

Relatively enjoyable class. You get to drop your lowest test! The professor really knows and understands the material, so he is able to answer all questions clearly. His tests did sometimes have tricky or confusing questions, so read carefully.

Quality professor, or actually grad student. Gets grades back in an hour most of the time which was great. Good clear lectures. Fair exams. Very solid choice for an econ professor, would recommend. Only downside is random attendance checks.

analysis.name: Ahmet Erbil
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The class itself (Intro modern) was pathetically easy and shallow. Prof Erbil, however, is an incredibly passionate guy who clearly would have loved to just teach to anyone who wanted to learn, even without requirements/grades/external motivators. Seems to me he wants to go into more depth than the course allowed. He seems like a really cool guy.

I had Erbil for Physics 3. Physics 3 is much easier than Physics 2, and unfortunately he realizes this. Unlike Physics 1 and 2 where the worst test is dropped as a buffer, in his Physics 3 class there is NO hope of redemption after a bad test grade. The final was 10 MC at 25% of your grade: one stupid math error drops your final grade 2.5 points.

I had Erbil for Thermodynamics.  He's a fairly easy teacher as far as grading goes; he's well-grounded in reality and insists that his students do likewise.  He's average when it comes to explaining material or fielding questions.  Erbil's big advantage is that he's very, very concerned about his students' learning.  Overall a solid teacher.

Compared with other physics classes at Tech... his was awesome.  I really enjoyed him... and yes he does talk about himself a lot, but it's all interesting... he knows a bunch of random famous scientists (or so he says).  Anyway, if you can get the old tests... you'll be golden.  Oh yeah... and an 80 is like an A... so that's nice too....

Without a doubt the BEST professor I've had at Tech.  He is always willing to help his students, and you can tell he enjoys teaching.  His tests are very reasonable with most of the averages turning out to be in the 80s, which is very high for a class at Tech.  I really enjoyed the class and would highly recommend it.

analysis.name: Alex Moutaftchieva
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Great organization and structure throughout the course. Always accessible outside of class and clearly cares a lot about students' career placement. Consistently connects what you learn in class to real-world applications, which makes the material much more meaningful. Easily the best professor in the major.

Alex does a great job in teaching Intro to Construction Management. She introduces new concepts in a way that is digestible for all students. There were a lot of valuable lessons that came out of the semester-end project that could be applied to the Building Construction world.

Alex has a lot of industry experience and really cares about you paying attention in class. It's pretty obvious that she is teaching because she wants us to actually learn something, not just lecturing to lecture. Very open to questions and assigns work that is actually relevant to the industry and what we are learning.

analysis.name: Charlotte Alexander
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She is very enthusiastic about the topic and gave good examples in class. You get a double sided crib sheet for every test, so as long as your notes are good then the tests are easy. There are also 2 case studies which are hard to study for, but the class is easy overall. There is no homework which I liked and you don't need the textbook.

Literally one of the best teachers at Scheller. Explains concepts simply using real world, RECENT examples. She is super engaging and intelligent. Not a lot of grades, just exams, random attendance, and case studies. Exams are easy and multiple choice. Case studies are also easy, just review the content before. You also get a crib sheet for exams

Super nice professor, very enthusiastic in lectures. She uses good examples and engages the class, easy to pay attention in her class. Tests were kinda hard but you get a cheat sheet. She was very available for help and going over past tests, genuinely cared for student success. Definitely recommend her as a professor

By far my favorite professor I have had at Tech!!! I thought this class was going to be boring, but the material is actually really interesting and she is super passionate and knowledgeable about it. She makes sure her students are understanding the material and is easily accessible by email and office hours. TAKE HER!!

I 100% recommend her for legal aspects. You get an entire page front and back for a crib sheet on tests (type this). You do need to pay attention somewhat in lectures and show up. The last unit there aren't slides so be sure to pay attention and take down notes. Super easy class tbh.

analysis.name: Alan Ritter
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Really horrible lecturing, shocking considering GT should be good at ML. He struggles with basic public speaking (every other word is um, like, basically, right) making it hard to stay engaged in the material. The assignments have little to do with his lectures so youre forced to learn it all on your own. Avoid Alan if possible, at least for 4641.

Professor Ritter absolutely killed my interest in machine learning. It is impossible to follow along with him in lectures as he simply circles and scribbles all over the slides. The projects and homework assignments are nothing like what he teaches in class -- at ALL. The only way to succeed is to teach yourself everything and pray you're close.

Don't go to the lecture, just read the textbook and online resources. He will only talk about the math, not the reasons or concepts behind. He is very good at killing your interest in machine learning. And you will never get answers for any assignments because he wants to re-use them in the future. God bless you if you have to take his class.

Easily the most difficult class I have taken in my time at Georgia Tech. The tests and assignments in the class did not relate to the lectures or material and you are forced to heavy research outside of class to complete questions. Lectures are extremely math intensive, but not very useful since he just says exactly what's on the slides.

Professor Ritter poorly explains material in-class while only underlining the material he is talking about and not writing anything down on slides. Each lecture leaves students lost in the material. Assignments have very little relation to the material taught in the class requiring outside resources to help students guess at an answer.

analysis.name: Paul Alonso
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Tough grader but honestly didn't care about that too much. What I did care about was busting my behind the entire semester with an A average, just to get a participation grade that dropped my average by a whole letter. Mind you I had documentation. Not understanding. Maybe he just didn't like me. Made me not want to minor in spanish. Devastated.

He is very knowledgeable on the subject, which made the class interesting. I learned a lot and developed my writing/speaking skills, however he is quite intimidating whenever you speak up (which is required for participation). He takes points off of assignments for seemingly no reason and there's a decent amount of homework so beware of that!

It's a good class. It can be difficult, but as long as you do the readings and put in good effort, you'll get a good grade. Professor Alonso is a little intimidating but has good spirits and wants all his students to be engaged and interested in the material.

Not an easy A. He grades essays harshly, particularly on grammar and Spanish errors. A few presentations, and he assigns lots of reading and movies to watch - like 3-4 hours before each class. He really likes to talk (ramble). He does know his stuff and has strong background in journalism. His English isn't great which can lead to some confusion.

Would not recommend, especially if you want an easy A. His grading is ridiculously harsh and he can't explain why he took off points well either. He also is intimidating and will call you out randomly to answer a question. As much as the content was interesting and he knew his stuff, the stress of going to this class was not worth it.

analysis.name: Allen Robinson
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: His lectures were really good, but the rest of the class was not great. The labs take way longer than the designated lab time, and the exams and lab quizzes are a massive time crunch. Thankfully, even though it takes a lot of time, it's not difficult to get good grades on the homeworks and lab reports.

Dr. Robinson is an amazing lecturer - writes everything out on the board. Cleared up many misconceptions from 2040. Exams are super time-limiting. Labs are extremely time-consuming. If you can separate the very stressful exams and lab structure from the great lecture content he is amazing.

~6 hours a week on lab. 6 HW ~3hr . Lectures are GREAT. you must go! Nice person but you need to contact him in person, because he is very slow to email. he has a lot going on (W/F in office only i think). Homeworks and exams graded very harshly, and prep material is limited, but I dont care because I like Robinson and I learned a lot. ~4 pt curve?

He is a good lecturer but has absolutely no concern for the well-being of students. Never replied to students' emails, and impossible to find for office hours. He had confusing due dates and assigned difficult homework, barely relevant to the class, which made everything seem poorly organized.

Prof Robinson is very good at breaking down complex topics into simple ideas, but his lectures are only 50 minutes so they move fast and aren't long enough. Labs each week take varying amounts of time and closer to the end you almost will have to go to open lab hours. Though, if you read the theory in the lab manual beforehand it'll halve the time.

analysis.name: Alex Hsu
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Hsu is a cool guy, he was very passionate about his research and it sounded very interesting when he talked about it. That being said, he didn't really know much about how to teach this class (tbf, it was his first time teaching it). You are graded on 2 tests and 4 hws, and he doesn't release practice tests. Class wasn't too hard though.

I wouldn't recommend the professor as hes poor at consultation and doesn't answer questions for practice midterms and finals or in general. The TA is the saving grace for this class, but the professor is poor at teaching. Not to mention, his exams have questions that one may never encounter in class or assignments. Overall, don't take him.

There was not a single practice problem or helpful example done the entire class, or posted online so the average grade of the final was a 56. He is a terribly boring lecturer and does not stick to the topics of his class. Terrible class, would not recommend

He just read off slides and did not explain well. But a lot content with details showed in exams. Didn't give very useful resources to prepare for exams and the content from lectures did not fully cover content in final.

All the nice reviews are spam and written on the same day by children, go and read them. The class would be 100x easier if he did the bare minimum and released answer keys and work for practice problems. The class is difficult and the slides are horrendous and not helpful at all. He's definitely a chill guy but he's just so so so bad at teaching.

analysis.name: Aldo Ferri
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Attending his lectures help. They're super clear, & I had a thorough understanding of the material just attending his classes. The assignments do take time, characteristic of any grad course. Super friendly & caring guy, with a sprightly sense of humor. Doing the previous year exams he gives is all the prep I needed to get an A.

if ur hearing good things, it's all true. he's really funny and good at making dyn easy for u. his exams seem extremely scary when ur taking them but he is such a lenient grader that if u try to maximize points, you're completely set. offers around 3 full points of extra credit total if you use every opportunity (DO ALL HW QUESTIONS) take ferri!!

The goat of Dynamics. By far the best teacher I have had at Georgia Tech. Super clear lectures followed by example driven classes to help you understand the topic. Super friendly guy and answers questions clearly. Love Dr.Ferri.

He clearly cares about teaching and it makes showing up to lectures rewarding. He clearly prepared his lectures to make them clear and understandable. Homework can be difficult, and unfortunately does not count towards much of the grade. Exams are 90% of class grade but he gives plenty to prepare for them, and they are not unreasonable.

Fantastic professor. Class can be hard, but that is just the nature of a masters level dynamics course. He is super accessible and a great lecturer. The homeworks are really helpful and he includes the final answer to make sure you are on the right track. The tests are very similar to the homework but don't require a ton of actual math.

analysis.name: Alberto Fuentes
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Fuentes is great. His lectures are interesting, he's clearly passionate about the course material, and grades are diversified among reading quizzes, worksheets, and exams. I really enjoyed INTA 2050 and highly recommend taking his class.

I enjoyed Dr. Fuentes class, the lectures were fascinating; I learned tons. He's a fair grader. Just be ready to take detailed notes if you want to succeed. Readings are assigned 2x a week. Quizzes are on the readings, so take good reading notes too. Exams are bit difficult, but multiple extra credit opportunities at the end. True difficulty: 3.5.

Was an interesting lecturer but the class is way too difficult for an elective class, be prepared to put STEM level effort into a non-STEM class. He doesn't post lecture materials or notes and moves through his notes pretty fast.

Fuentes is great. Lectures are in-depth and thoughtful. He cares about what he is teaching and he's good at it. You actually have to do the reading assignments and attend class to complete the in-class worksheets. Exams are 60% lecture material, 40% readings, but it all really works together. Similar difficulty to an AP history class.

Dr. Fuentes is a great professor-- one of the best I have had at Tech. The work I had to put into to succeeding in this class was worth it since lectures were valuable. I left with so much more knowledge. I really appreciated the readings quizzes at the start of each class because it meant everyone was doing the work and made for a better class.

analysis.name: Amanda Hampton
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Not the greatest professor but the class is really easy especially if you took calc in high school. No attendance but if you don't know calc then I would recommend going because it's kind of hard to learn on your own. 15 quizzes and she drops the worst 5, and 2 midterms and a final.

I was surprised to see such negative comments about her because my experience wasn't terrible at all. Although some may find it boring, I actually enjoyed her lecture style. She gives so many optional practice problems that undoubtedly show up on the test, so literally just do the work and you're fine.

Students who already took a calc course struggled less with her. There are suggested problems you HAVE to do to succeed (even though there is "no hw"). For an intro calculus class for non-STEM majors, she offered "reading the textbook" as a way to improve performance. She writes out definitions and walks through practice problems rather than teach.

She isn't even a true professor, this class took up tons of study time. By the end of the semester we had been given over 800 practice problems, not mandatory but they are the only way to prepare for the test. The problems she goes over in lecture are a fraction of the difficulty of what shows up on the test. 0/10 class avoid at all costs

I know many had a negative opinion on her, but she wasn't bad, I enjoyed lecture. At the end of the semester she went through everyone's grades and tried to get everyone to a C (minimum). Her exams were very difficult, if you have no calc knowledge, but she adjusted as we went on. Go to office hours, she noticed any effort on your part.

analysis.name: Mandy Moore
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment:
Wish I had more space, but to summarize:
-Teaching style made the course's fiber arts theme surprisingly engaging
-Graded on participation points (only need 100/130 for an A)
-4 fun & easy projects with minimal writing (video, podcast, presentation, and embroidery)
-Most importantly, she is the kindest and most understanding professor I've ever had

I had a very pleasant experience taking the class. Homework mainly consisted of short readings that were to be discussed in class. The final grade was not done on a points scale and instead was about completion and shown effort over the semester, which took out a lot of stress.
It's very clear that Dr. Moore puts the student first.

Dr. Moore is a great professor! The projects we did were non-traditional, including making a podcast, a blog post, and learning a new fiber craft, which I really enjoyed. She makes it very clear exactly what we needed to do to achieve an A for each assignment, and gives great feedback. She is also flexible with deadlines and attendance.

some readings before class, but very doable and easy (you can also get by without doing the readings). class theme was toy stories (pretty interesting). all the assignments were either process assignments in preparation for the main artifacts or reflections on the artifacts (all easy). is boring occasionally. All the assignments are self-graded!
Genuine participation class. Lots of projects but reasonable class time is given for them.

analysis.name: Amelia Stokolosa
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The class is pretty engaging overall, and she genuinely cares about her students. Best class this semester!! I used to look forward to class every week, because yes, it is THAT fun. Would take her again 100% . The exams can be challenging at first, but it's all centralized across all 1553 sections.

Overall super engaging class, she goes a little fast sometimes but takes on the somewhat complex topics in an approachable and clear way. Do not recommend skipping any lectures though as a lot of the concepts pile up on each other quickly, especially towards the end of the semester.
Sometimes goes a tiny bit fast but other than that, she is slay and had us learn a tiny bit of French for funsies. Some classes made me laugh out loud

analysis.name: Amy Stone
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: In mathematics, understanding concepts and processes is essential. Learning should start with simple problems, building knowledge step by step; lectures often jumped very fast to applications relying on a single method. This limited students' flexibility and made it difficult for those without math backgrounds or extra support to succeed.

This teacher had a great personality and was very funny, but was a poor lecturer. She consistently made mistakes during lecture that confused us all. She would need time to figure out problems as if she didn't prepare for lecture. Most of what I learned was through research online in my own time since her lectures were inadequate.
She is not knowledgeable about the subject, but has a great personality.

analysis.name: Daniel Amsterdam
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Very caring, allowed me to do alternate assignment when I had not done the reading. Very engaging lectures, and the reading was genuinely interesting, even though there is a lot of it. Genuinely cares about the topics he teaches, and I feel better off having taken the class and learned about the topics we did.

Prof Amsterdam was the best history instructor I have ever had. His lectures were well structured as he gave outlines for each one and his test were all from the lectures (so u gotta go to take notes cuz he doesn't post notes). Tests were very straightforward and the required readings were actually really interesting to read. Really caring

He's an amazing instructor, and even though attendance isn't mandatory, you will need to go to class in order to get a good grade since he doesn't post the lecture content on Canvas. Very chill guy, he dropped a few questions in our tests if he felt that it was confusing. He also dropped our lowest midterm. Make sure to take good notes

Lectures are not mandatory but DEFINITELY reccomended. Studying the material on your own or based off the notes makes the class so much harder than it should. Amsterdam is an amazing lecturer who makes the content  engaging, concise, and easy to follow, additionally he makes it very clear what parts of lecture are important/on the exams

Overall a great lecturer and a good guy. Also, the class is really easy- the only homework is 1-3 page readings for classes and 3 1-2 page "papers" throughout the semester which are essentially an automatic 100 if you do them. You have to go to class though bc notes are not posted online, but lectures are interesting and usually have a 5 min break

analysis.name: Amanda Girard
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 58 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Extremely and unreasonably tough grader for no good reason in what's supposed to be a fairly easy A class. Gave terrible and unclear feadback on assignments and didn't really follow the grading rubrics that were given. Overall awful, one of the biggest mistakes I made at GT was taking a class with this professor. 0/10

One of the worst professors I have taken at Georgia Tech. Extremely slow and unreasonable grader with astronomically high expectations. She has quite the ego for an LMC professor and will not hesitate to defend herself when asked about grading. AVOID THIS PROFESSOR AT ALL COSTS!

(CS3001) She has some weird policies including dropping students' overall grades by 10% if they miss 2 lectures. Apparently she has instructed TA's to not give students above 90% in section participation. She is also very much NOT accessible and doesn't respond to emails, citing her "busy schedule". Overall mid prof but not the greatest person.

(CS3803) AVOID AT ALL COST. WORST professor ever. RUDE, CONDESCENDING, DISORGANIZED. Does not understand either communication or anything technical, but teaches Tech Communication. More boring jokes and her life stories in class than useful lecture material, but taking notes is required as mandatory attendance. Changes syllabus arbitrarily.

Grades everything last minute and extremely harshly. Talks about nonsense during class yet requires attendance. Has a major ego and is very mean to students. I feel like she's a deeply unhappy person that believes everyone else should be miserable as a result. I'd take an 8am over htis class any day.

analysis.name: Emily Alicea-Munoz
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 147 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Alicea is by far the best professor for Physics. For those who say her exams are hard and beyond what they believe was taught, you're wrong. As long as you understand the content well and its applications, no matter the question given, you'll be able to apply what you know. Not to mention the generous partial credit given. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!!!!

She is an outstanding professor. I took this class online and found it much easier than the in-person version. The recorded lectures explain the concepts very clearly, and the ample practice tests prepared me well for exams. As long as you pay attention to the recorded lectures and utilize the GPS and practice tests, this class is a breeze.

The lecturer does a great job at giving you ample amounts of practice material, relevant examples through labs and group-work problems over teams, and has access to many helpful TA's while being very responsive to emails and questions on Ed-Stem. Tests are hard, with self-studying being necessary to pass. Hard class, good teacher.
Best professor for physics 2. Took this course online and it was easy.

Dr. Alicea is by far the best Physics Prof at Tech. She takes complicated information and presents it in an easy-to-understand way with TONS of examples. Physics II is a challenging course, and the tests reflect that. However, the grade breakdown allows you to succeed even if you don't do very well on the three midterms and final.

analysis.name: Adjo Amekudzi
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Amekudzi-Kennedy was an excellent teacher. You can tell she cares both about civil and about students learning and growing in her class. Exams are graded pretty leniently and she is incredibly kind and open to meeting and talking about anything CEE. The project was fun, and isn't bad if you incrementally work on it through the semester.

Dr. Amekudzi-Kennedy is very passionate about this course but isn't the best at relating to students and student concerns.  The grading criteria is slightly strange and she expects you to do a lot for the class outside of lecture.  She is a great person and very nice but the class was just average and tedious at times.

Group project heavy; you work with the same group all semester. some exams, but easy if you keep up with class content. the final is the group project, which is sort of graded tough. pay attention to techniques taught in class, because this is what they are looking for

Dr. Kennedy really cares about her students. Long homeworks/tests that are graded pretty tough but the group project should help with your grade. She is so kind and responds immediately to your emails. Overall an interesting class that really teaches you a lot about sustainability and civil systems. Probably more work than it needed to be though

Personally, this is one of my favorite teachers here at Georgia Tech! I am very interested in Sustainable Urban Development and although the class is called Civil Engineering Systems, it is amazing how she focuses on sustainability analysis of systems as the basis of the class. Additionally, she is the most respected in her field! So much knowledge

analysis.name: Amy Bruckman
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Online community was a pleasant surprise. Had a lot of fun working on the term paper. Lectures are interesting. Beware of the many and sometimes long readings. TAs were excellent as well. Generally an easy grader and very understanding about student concerns. A fun personality on top of all that. Definitely beating the reddit mod stereotype

Dr. Bruckman is one of the most engaged, passionate professors I've ever had. Every lecture kept me interested and was filled with stories that make the material memorable. She's funny, witty, and very kind. She gives clear expectations from the beginning. If you complete the readings and pay attention, you will do well. I highly recommend.

Dr. Bruckman's very caring towards students and her lectures are very engaging and interesting. At the start, there is quite a bit of reading + homework essays, but it gets way easier as the course progresses. Make sure you participate in Section and you'll be just fine. The 2 exams are detail-specific. Very easy course overall, would recommend.

In the first half, you have short papers due weekly. No final, but 2 midterm exams and a term paper due towards the end of the semester. There's a lot of reading assigned, but she basically reviews all of it in class the next day, so I don't read anything. Weekly discussion sections are long but interesting, depending on the people in your section.

Dr. Bruckman is the best professor I have had at Georgia Tech. As long as there is effort in the papers due each class, you will do fine. Dr. Bruckman is incredibly knowledgable, and she does a great job of conveying the material in a way that is easy to understand and engaging. This class is highly valuable and very applicable to the real world.

analysis.name: Amit Prasad
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I took this course Spring 2022. I found the lectures to be extremely dry. Prepare yourself to participate in class discussions, which are highly philosophical. Your grade is almost entirely dependent on essays. It seemed to me that if he didn't agree with your stance on a topic, you would receive an unfavorable grade for the essay and vice versa.

The readings can be long at 15-25 pages on average but you will do well as long as you show up to class, participate, and complete the assignments. Discussions in class are engaging and Dr. Prasad is not heavy on lecturing. He cares a lot about students and can give a lot of guidance on the two essays (which were 50% of the class grade).

There was a lot of reading and the material was pretty dense. The class itself though was interesting and engaging and Dr. Prasad was very caring about the students. There are normally three papers and a few small assignments. It's expected you do the readings before class to participate but not required (i.e. no pop quizzes).

The test averages were low (C's and D's) and grading was harsh. The professor was rude and often called students out for just asking questions.
Exhaustive class. A lot to learn.

analysis.name: Akash Dixit

review_highlights.comment: This guy was incredibly frustrating to deal with. I would not take him. He digresses from directions, makes up his own, and then grades based on things that he doesn't tell you. He was really a bad teacher and you should not take him!

Do NOT take this professor. He does not follow a textbook, he does not teach in class at all, all of his instructions are unclear, and to top it all off his grading is very harsh and inconsistent. Though I got A's on the tests and obviously understood the material, I didn't do as well in the overall class because his projects were ridiculous.

I was not doing well in his class and went to him for help. He spent 1.5 hours trying to explain the labs when he could easily have asked me to go to a TA. No doubt he grades hard but gives curves the grades. He gave 18 exra-points for exam 1 for a very simple assignment.

The class may seem difficult at first. But as soon as you understand the expectations and ask questions. You will be fine. The professor is happy to answer all questions as long as rules are followed.
He super nice. In office hours he spent well over an hour making sure i understood the topic. His grading is a bit inconsistent... but overall he is very fair. He also curves very nicely.

analysis.name: Aki Matsushima
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I had Matsushima-sensei for both JAPN 1002 & 1001. She is so incredibly accommodating to students, if you're sick and miss a quiz or exam she allows for make-ups. Very interactive lectures (expect to be called on at least once per class). I felt 1002 to be a significant difficulty jump from 1001, but matsushima-sensei made the transition easier.

Foreign languages are hard, let alone one that often uses three alphabets in the same sentence. Yes, you'll have to put in the work and you will have to memorize a lot, but Matsushima-Sensei is very clear about what she expects you to know and grow.

She makes it very easy. Great professor.

Matsushima-sensei is an amazing professor. She is very kind, makes expectations clear, and provides plenty of resources for studying and test preparation. Her lectures focus on speaking exercises. You are well-prepared for homework. Foreign languages take attending class and additional studying, but she makes the process very enjoyable. がんばって！

She forces in class participation which is scary at first but you'll get used to it. Pacing is rough at first with the alphabets but the course load is pretty light afterwards. She grades super nicely and gives exam formats beforehand.

Matsushima 先生 is so sweet. Japanese was my favorite class this semester. Attendance is mandatory, but going to class never felt like a chore. There's group work too, but it's fun to get to know other classmates. This doesn't feel like a 4 credit hour class at all. There's lots of extra credit too, so I never had to worry about my grade. ありがとうございます！

analysis.name: Caitlin Anderson
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Chill class. Not many assignments in her class and when you do have something due, she breaks it down to a tee what she wants making it really easy to do well. There's the group podcast project at the end which was fun to do and easy to do well in if you put in the effort. Try to take her if you can, you won't regret it.

Outstanding professor. Took class over the summer so was a bit rushed with only 5 weeks of material, but one assignment was due at end of every week (Friday). Two day extension always available. No final exam but English Department requires reflective ePortfolio. A bit tedious, but plenty of time is given in class to complete. Def recommend.

Very clear on everything needed to do well on any assignment, and was overall a fun class. Definetly one of the best English 2 professors; no horror stories (apart from in the novels we read/watch) that can be found from other classes.

In my class she claimed Frankenstein was the 'first transracial and transsexual person' so yeh she's a little woke, but who really cares? What matters is the grade you get, and with Anderson you are guaranteed an A. She has like 3 total assignments in the semester each of which won't take more than an hour and lets you scroll tiktok in class.
She made the class fun and the lectures were interesting. There were some assignments but they were all interesting to do and the group projects were fun.

His tests are nonsensical relative to what he teaches.

Dr. Paravastu doesn't fit in this class. A worthless class that is unnecessarily hard.

I can't even fully blame him because the course is designed by the department in this way. Whoever thought thermodynamics is best learned through fill-in-the-blank notes should not be allowed to be designing courses. Professor is often not sure of what he is teaching as he is following someone else's lectures. ChBE should follow MSE and Dr. Speyer.

I just couldn't understand how he wanted us to apply concepts we learned in class. Intentionally designs exams so nobody can finish and questions are worded weirdly too. But I can see he's trying.

I'm learning literally nothing in this class, it's the epitome of stupid busy work and wasting your time.

Great UX/UI course. I learned a lot and I found the class very useful since I want to do UX/UI as a career. The entire class is centered around group work however, so CHOOSE YOUR MEMBERS CAREFULLY. The class only consisted of attendance, small presentation, and semester long group project. The group project is the biggest part of the class worth 75% so choose your team members wisely. She had fun lectures to listen and learn more about UI/UX. Overall I enjoyed the class.

Professor Shree was my favorite professor by far this semester! She is so passionate, interesting, and understanding. I am by no means a English major but she has a way of engaging you and making you want to contribute in class discussions. HIGHLY recommend her class, it was an amazing experience!
She's very nice and cares about her students a lot. Take English with her for your sanity, especially if it's your first semester at Georgia Tech.
I LOVED prof Shree. She is the chillest prof. If the class needed an assignment pushed back, then it was. The most understanding and fair grader out

However, he was a kind and caring person, and he was genuinely interested in improving as a teacher. I believe in a few years he will be a solid professor.

This course is tough, but Shubin is extremely kind and caring, and he's always open to answer whatever questions you have, even staying late after class ends. I watched Jankowski's lectures for exam review, but I fault this to this being Shubin's first semester, and I definitely think he'll improve bec he is very open to feedback.
A nice professor with a bit accent

Shubin has a bit of an accent and doesn't elaborate that much but will any answer question you have no matter how long it takes. He is very smart but not the best lecturer. We fell a little behind towards the end of the semester

Professor Kumar was my ENGL1101 professor for the Fall 2025 semester. He is extremely generous and kind. His course revolves a lot around 5 key projects/essays. The class was overall pretty easy. The professor is nice, but sometimes the class would get really boring. By this I mean that he would talk for a while about basically the same thing. However, overall a nice prof and will extend due date if needed.

Hes a really kind proffesor he cares for his students and is really understanding would take again definetly. Just do the work come to class. He cares what he talks about and his class isn't boring he likes to have giant disccussions

Lectures were really enjoyable especially for a 1 credit class. Great sense of humor, assignments were fine besides the poster and learning portfolio at the end of the semester. Otherwise a very straightforward class.

analysis.name: Ariel Fried

She is an excellent professor willing to be flexible on deadlines, and she gives well-constructed feedback to make students stronger writers. Outside of class, Dr. Fried is also very accessible. I couldn't recommend her enough if you have the opportunity to be a part of the class.

Great professor, she actually cares that you understand the material and doesn't assign too much readings. Lectures could be a lot sometimes and the work can pile up fast if you aren't paying attention, not a free A but definitely achievable if you put in a bit of effort.

Dr. Fried is an awesome professor. She understands students are preoccupied with major specific classes and is flexible with deadlines as long as a student shows commitment in class and in other assignments.

Prof yaps a lot during lectures, lectures are quite disorganized and heavy with information that isn't explained thoroughly. Exams are very difficult and have questions that we have never seen examples of before. A redeeming factor is that he gives quite a bit of extra credit.

analysis.name: Stephanie Arevecchia

analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I was excited for CS3600, but quickly grew frustrated. The prof has no clear curriculum, comes unprepared, and answers Qs with “I don't know.” She skips key slides, gives unclear homework, and fails to relate content to AI. So far, we've done 8 graph search algorithms—none AI-related. A class w/ much potential became one I care about the least.

Would definitely recommend her for 2110, MUCH easier than taking it in ATL. She makes the class very fair with assignments, quizzes, and TLs. Reads off the slides from ATL, but you can tell that she knows what she's talking about. Slight language barrier that makes understanding hard sometimes, but overall a very solid prof who I would recommend.

Prior review was lazy & biased, didn't make it through the entire class. Extremely fair teacher & decent lecturer for her first time teaching the course. Could tell she was very knowledgeable, but language barrier hurt a bit. HW heavy, but a very very fair course compared to taking in Atlanta. Would highly recommend and I enjoyed. Also had for 2110

analysis.name: Ari Glezer
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Fluids is one of the toughest classes at Tech. Dr. Glezer teaches fluids every fall, and he is good lecturer. He has a great understanding of fluid mechanics as it is the primary focus of his research. He can assume that students know more about fluids before taking this class. He can also be condescending about not getting concepts immediately.

Fluid Mechanics is a difficult class, but Dr. Glezer's lectures are helpful and include plenty of relevant examples. The 45 min exams are stressful, but not overly complex. Grading scheme is extremely friendly, allowing you to drop the two lowest test scores (can exempt final). Homework solutions are posted with the assignment. Would recommend.

Handwriting was actually atrocious, we spend most of each class asking him what things say. His tests have too short of a time limit just so he can spend 10 minutes lecturing after we finish the test, you could go into the test feeling good and walk out confused if you even know the subject, Better than some professors friends had so ig worth it

really fast lecturer, but lectures are well organized and lots of content covered every lecture. he has horrible handwriting though so be prepared for 5 minutes of every class dedicated to questions of what a word on the screen is. exams are difficult, but similar enough to hw. doing hw and studying lecture examples is key to the class

Dr. Glezer is one of the best professors I have had at Tech. Let me be clear: Fluids is HARD. Plain and simple. Dr. Glezer focuses his teaching on the concepts behind fluid mechanics, which makes his class difficult. But he is extremely clear in his lectures on what will be tested.

analysis.name: Joy Arulraj
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is a knowledgeable & excellent professor in database systems, but his teaching style could improve. No lecture recordings and a presentation heavy approach without practical demonstrations made it difficult to fully grasp concepts tbh. Exams were lengthy & allowing more time would be very helpful. I had high expectations but sadly disappointed.

The core content for this class is very interesting and is taught well, but it is formatted very poorly. Half of your grade comes from two written tests which contain numerous questions on irrelevant C++ trivia

Lectures were a bit slow, but easy to follow from the slides alone. Great introduction to the finer points of C++. Programming assignments were excellent coding practice. Exams were quite challenging, with some niche questions on C++ syntax, but they were satisfyingly comprehensive and curved reasonably. Extremely understanding prof. No busywork.

Earned 95% without doing the extra credit project. Assignments taught me a lot about C++ and databases. Thought tests could be tricky due to potpourri style questions that could be on anything from lectures, but that was alleviated due to a generous curve. Participation was Point Solutions, but that was also curved. Overall, he's a nice professor

This class was great, Prof Joy gives a lot of real world applications and teaches all aspects of designing a complex database system. He is very kind and prioritize learning above grades or anything else. Lots of extra credit opportunities were given. I learnt a lot of C++ and systems fundamentals which were useful as I was new to it. Great course

analysis.name: Sybrina Atwaters
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I thought this class would be an interesting class to take for my first semester here at Tech. I hated this class by the second week. Her tests are so confusing. Most of the questions on her tests are horribly worded. I feel like I haven't learned anything. It also feels like that if you don't believe what she does and agree with her, you're wrong.

The professor is so obviously biased towards socialism that she forced us to write our final exam essays from that perspective. She cited non-peer reviewed research as fact in her lectures, which barely made sense to begin with. She was extremely argumentative and was a poor facilitator of class discussion. Does not round up decimal grades at all.

If you're a Challenge student, beware. She acts superior, overexplains yes/no questions, and loves to use the “threes” like “I came, I saw, I conquered” plus her favorite phrase, “By design.” Midterm questions are confusing, so the study guide is useless. Her TAs don't give feedback around her. One of the worst classes I've had.

Major superiority complex! She grades her students based off of whether or not they agree with her on everything. She tries to push her beliefs on everyone. Whatever you do, do not disagree with her, tell her she's wrong, or speak your mind. All her class is, is an hour and a half long rant of her beliefs and how she's above everyone else.

She thinks that she is some sort of prophet and will berate you if you do not exactly agree with what she does. Her exams are poorly worded and have objective answers with zero curve (nobody got an A) and she marks you absent even if you are in class if you don't do EXACTLY what she says as soon as she says it. Do NOT take this class.

analysis.name: Christina Athanasouli
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Incredibly CARING and KNOWLEDGEABLE professor who has a knack for recontextualizing difficult mathematical concepts into intuitive lessons. She took the time to know all of the students in her lecture hall by name and regularly checked in with her students to make sure they were prepared. Easy to talk to!

Math 1552 was hard, but with Christina, she made it easier. She really cares about her students, she learned every single person's name in the big lecture class and made sure to check in with them to see how the class was going. The class itself is hard, and she tends to go very fast, but I would definitely recommend and would take again with her.

Awesome professor that truly cares for each student. Was always early in class to talk to individual students, learn names, and chat. SUPER accessible outside of class. Great lectures with sufficient practice and test-application based problems. Tests are usually on the tougher side (especially multiple choice), but the optional final helps a lot.

Professor Anathasouli is amazing! Although Math 1552 is hard as a Tech class, she did an amazing job. She is always super prepared when she comes to class with slides, and she posts practice problems too. She genuinely wants her students to succeed and learned everyone's names and met them outside of class/office hours if they needed help.

She goes out of her way to remember every students' names and puts lots of effort into her lectures. I never attended since it was my 8am, but I used the online notes. I would still recommend attending. There are many ways to improve your grade and maintain an A, lots of extra study material and opportunities provided.

analysis.name: Athulya Ram
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: No homework or textbook assigned. Lectures were absolutely phenomenal. Studios were required instead of HW by giving participation points (20% of grade). Tests were very reasonable and weekly quizzes were similar to material covered in studio. Professor was extremely accessible outside of class.

probably the best professor I've had at Tech so far. She explained the concepts very well and made integral calc so easy to understand. make sure to attend studio though to get a lot of practice problems to prep for tests and quizzes
Overall she was a good professor and very caring, her pacing during class was just off sometimes but she posts her notes on canvas so not a huge issue.

analysis.name: Athanasios Mantalaris
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can

review_highlights.comment: He is a very sweet man who cares a lot about the students, but is not the best teacher. He would emphasize main points over and over instead of working through problems. Only reason I really understood the class was because of the amazing TAs. Still got an A because the TAs graded and they were lenient because they would watch him not teach us.

BMED 2210 is a boring and easy class. Learn it by yourself. Dr. Mantaralis isn't helpful and the TAs were sometimes clueless. However, this is not a stressful class. All materials are straightforward. You don't need to rely on professors and TAs a lot.
You need to read the book to really grasp concepts and examples. He is funny and very enthusiastic but does not answer questions well. This class is just poorly run in general.

analysis.name: Hassan Attarchi
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
