review_highlights.comment: I found Attarchi's lectures very difficult to follow. In retrospect, I probably would have done better skipping the class, teaching myself, and showing up to weekly quizzes. I didn't have much exposure to calculus before this class and his lectures really didn't help me grasp concepts I didn't know. He was, however, very caring and willing to help.

Very caring teacher. Wants to see you succeed, but the tests are just so hard. Even as someone who took AP Calculus in high school, the questions asked are very difficult and unlike the questions we see in our homework. Homework is due every Thursday at midnight. Actually do the homework even if it's only a tiny percentage of your avg. It'll help.

Let's just start with this: there are homeworks due every Thursday at midnight. There are also weekly quizzed averaging over just a few sections of the book that you will take in either the first or last 10-15 minutes of class. NOW HERE IS THE STRUGGLE: you do well on the quizzes and the test questions look crazy, never before seen. TOTAL BS CLASS

I'll be honest, I rarely paid attention in lecture and never went to office hours, but the few times I did listen to him it really paid off. There is homework due every week but it's honestly not too difficult. The online transition was pretty rough as expected for a math class, but he moved so many due dates and gave tons of extensions. Great guy!

He was really accesible outside of class and willing to help, but the problem is I don't think he remembers what it is like to not know the subject, and so he explains it as if we already know what's going on. the accent makes things a little difficult to understand too. He is caring when it comes to personal problems and will move a quiz if needed

analysis.name: Asif Khan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Great introduction to semiconductors and very in-depth coverage of MOSFETs. Video lectures are posted on his Youtube and sometimes go more in depth than he does during lecture. Homeworks are fair and pretty much exactly based off lecture slides. Super experienced guy with lots of industry knowledge that he sprinkles into lectures.

ECE3030 with Khan is awesome. Engaging class that will help you understand semiconductors and industry trends on a deeper level. Only complaint is grading takes a long time (over a month for midterm 1), but other than that I highly recommend this course.

Dr Khan is a great teacher! He does speak slowly, but I actually like that because it gives me time to internalize the information and take notes. He also digresses by speaking about related but non-class material in the real world, such as investors, or even what the yield of a chip is, and that's always interesting! Listen and you will learn!

He's a pretty funny guy. The homework is due weekly and there aren't late submissions allowed unless the TAs are feeling nice at the end of the year. The homeworks can be very difficult or super easy, no in-between. The Midterms and Finals aren't very difficult if you pay attention. All lectures are recorded and are on youtube.

Dr. Khan teaches this course at the exact level it needs to be at. He explains many of the topics very intuitively and very clearly, leaving little for the student to have to puzzle over themselves. The homeworks are straightforward and relatively short, and they are generally a grade booster. The class content is also interesting.

analysis.name: Robert Ashwill
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Let the students focus on their actual work, tone down the class a bit.

Obscene amount of information covered on tests & closed notes. Discussions in this class don't exist because lectures always fall behind schedule. Need to know all lecture and book content. Accuracy graded HW. Few grade padding points. Too time consuming as a non major class. Not worth making space in your schedule for this section of the class...

Rob teaches good lectures but his progress is often slow so that you need to read textbook sections that he hasn't covered but will be on the test to prepare for tests. He is willing to help and answer students' questions yet the tests, for me, are harder than I would expect for a intro-level class. You need to memorize a lot to get good grades.

This class is one that is very easy to succeed in so long as you keep up with the course material. A lot of the material that is covered on exams is talked about heavily during lectures, so even though attendance is not mandatory, it is a key factor to doing well in this class. Prof Ashwill is very understanding and I would take his class again.

Avoid this professor for an intro psych class. This class is doable, but I was always annoyed how much work and I had to put into this class compared to other teachers. If you want to make an A you must memorize the entire textbook and lecture powerpoints. Tests are mc, essay question, and fill in the blank whereas other classes are mc.

analysis.name: Ashley Bradford
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Bradford is a really good health policy professor! This class was not too difficult, but I learned so much! Highly suggest for anyone looking to take a public policy elective class. Each class does have pre-readings, but it isn't too bad, as you could still do well in the class without reading.
She is genuinely so good for US Health Policy. I learned so much and the exams are not too difficult.

Dr. Bradford is awesome! I was nervous to take a stats class but she is an amazing lecturer who helped explain things so well! She's also funny and pretty young, so she's very understanding! The problem sets could be tough, but she was receptive to feedback and offered many ways to boost grades. I would definitely recommend taking a class with her!

Dr. Bradford is an amazing professor and I definitely recommend taking her as she starts teaching new classes. The class is graded by 2 tests and 4 assignments, which are hard but if you attend lectures and pay attention they are easy to get through. She is very helpful, responds to emails very quickly and is overall a fun professor to talk to.

Dr. Bradford is awesome. Her lectures are packed with material, but she does a great job in making sure students understand what is being taught. There are 6 total grades, 4 of which are problem sets, which can be a bit tricky. Overall, Dr. Bradford is an amazing professor and I would recommend her to any student.

analysis.name: Ashok Goel
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I have very mixed feelings. I really like this professor, but CS7637 is the worst class I have taken yet at Georgia Tech. I learned more reading about the topics on Wikipedia than I did in lecture. This professor loves busy work too, so expect a bunch of pointless writing assignments. He just isn't a computer scientist, he's a cog psych guy.

A few problems I had with the class:
-Lectures are mandatory and long, and he always waits for 5 questions/comments from the class
-Assignments are writing heavy
-Class is more cog-sci focused than CS focused (one programming assignment was like 300 lines of if statements)
-part of your participation points are based off talking to AI TAs

Overbearing and uninspiring. Class is bloated with busy work and he throws a fit if you don't ask a question within 5 seconds of him asking if there are any questions. By taking this class, he will run cognitive science experiments on you as a student, which is something I definitely did not want to be a part of.

Course is well-structured and the professor supports his students. TA team is slightly inconsistent and aggressive in their approach to students (Head TA accused half the class of cheating in peer reviews). His accent makes it difficult to understand what he's saying at 1.4x speed. Overall, I liked the slow introduction to AI agents in this class.
Had him for intro to cognitive science.  Great teacher!  Very interesting subject too!  Reccomended for anyone who wants to learn how people think and learn.

analysis.name: Austin Christian
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Amazing and incredibly funny professor. He was always super helpful during office hours. 3 exams, HW, quizzes, and a final. Allowed for makeup exams. Gave practice exams that were very similar to the tests. Very good professor to take multi with.

LOVE HIM!! take him if you can, he is such a good professor. he knows what hes talking about, and makes the lectures make sense. he encourages office hours like no other, and when i went he was so kind and helped. dry sense of humor also. his practice exams help a bunch. pls go to his class he deserves it. slay austin!!

Took him for 4107. Has to be the best math professor I've taken at tech. I would take him over any professor. Knows his stuff like the back of his hand and legitimately cares that you understand the material. Could not recommend this guy more.
I took him a year ago and to this day say he was the best math professor ive had at GT. Take him if you can. He's super accessible at office hours too. Can't say enough good things about him.

Professor Christian was one of the best math professors I have had! His lectures were very engaging and he made a point to learn the names of everyone who went to office hours. He would also give a study guide before each exam that would greatly help with the exam's content. Midterms were pretty easy compared to other teachers. He was worth it!

analysis.name: Ashley Wheeler
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: (I ACTUALLY TOOK HER FOR 1554) Prof. Wheeler does not give full length lectures and expects you to know all content prior to attending the lecture. She will only do two or three examples that last a matter of twenty minutes. If you have any possibility to take Barone do it, unless you intend to learn from the TA's.

Cancelled class day of the exam 2x so we didn't get a review session. Lectures are hard to understand. Doesn't care about her students at all. Doesn't compensate for cancelled lectures with videos like other teachers, send her students to a different lecture WITHOUT even asking that professor causing students to be kicked out of that lecture

Very unorganized and the lectures are uninspired and unstructured. She does not go into depth on the important concepts and rather than clarifying them, she asks the students on their input (while most of us do not have familiarity). If you take her, you need to make extra effort to teach yourself or from the TAs (saved me). Take Barone if you can.

The midterms/quizzes for 1553 are the same for all professors, and attendance isn't mandatory. Wheeler can be difficult to relate to and hard to follow in class, so just watch Jankowski's lectures on the class page or read the textbook yourself- it's probably the only way you'll get an A in the class but isn't all that unmanageable if you enjoy it.

If you take her, you will often find yourself teaching all of the material to yourself, as she does not go in depth or teach it properly enough to do well on the exams. She does not exhibit expert knowledge on the topic and often leaves students more confused than when they entered the lecture. Linear can be difficult, but she makes it harder.

review_highlights.comment: This was an acting class. As an aspiring actor, I NEVER walked out of a single class feeling good about myself as an actor or even person. He was very rude, curt, and un-constructive in his comments/grading. Does not care and will not help u achieve your goals (even if they are class-related). Very subjective grader. Different opinion  lower grade
He is the worst teacher ever.  He is a very hard, unreasonable, grader.  His class is very boring.  He is a very dirty, nasty person who's office and body is filthy.  DO NOT TAKE HIM!!!!!

He is a horrible teacher. He has no idea how to keep his students entertained, thus making the class boring. The only reason I went is because attendance was basically mandatory. He is not a fair grader. I received a 79.8 as my final grade, and he made me get a C in the class. He's rude and filthy. Save yourself, don't take any of his courses.

Quite judgmental and the workload is heavy. Long papers and many assignments. Limited opportunities to act in front of a camera. While there is a lot to learn about acting, there is not enough time spent actually acting. It can be frustrating for those who want more hands-on experience.

He really changed his teaching stype recently due to numerous past complaints. His Performance Studies class was incredibly easy, you don't need to do the readings to get an A. Just take notes on what he says and study the day before the test. Again, his teaching style has greatly changed and he grades much more leniently now. Everyone got an A.

analysis.name: Audrey Duarte
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: One of the worst professors at tech. Does NOT care about her students. So many complaints about her from my peers about rudeness, lack of empathy, and inflexibility. Made this class way harder on us than it had to be; didn't let us review our past exams and the term paper rubric was too vague.

Was completely unaccommodating during the COVID-19 pandemic. I had many exams, finals, and projects to worry about in other classes as well since I was graduating that semester. She was not only inconsiderate but unnecessarily rude when discussing what she wanted for the class.

She was not approachable or understanding at all. Any time I had any questions or concerns she made me feel bad about not understanding something which was really discouraging. When I asked her for help she was reluctant to help me and basically told me she was not willing to put forth the effort. Do not recommend!

She delivers engaging lectures, and consistently engages the class to ask our questions about the topics in question. Her tests are very fair, and a good estimate of the amount of time spent on each concept in class and the depth needed to know information. Attendance isn't mandatory, but was recommended. Very caring and understanding professor.

review_highlights.comment: Study the PT and do the HW and you will be fine. Cares for the students. Great guy.

Easily the most kind and caring professor Ive had, always making sure to let us know what to expect on exams and grades nicely. He explains concepts well, and works out lots of practice problems that are very similar to test questions. Allows for a crib sheet on tests and gives quizzes for extra credit. Occasionally throws in some humor too

he's a super sweet and chill prof!! he gets super happy solving problems so the examples are pretty easy to follow, almost follows the pp word for word. i got a 100 on the first exam by looking over the practice examples and the HW is pulled from the textbook. best prof for this class and probably one of the best ones at tech, take him if you can!!

Awesome professor! He cares about his students. Unlike many professors, he actually teaches his students. He is super organized and comes to class prepared and ready to teach. He explains concepts clearly. The PP notes are excellent, and he goes over sufficient examples to make sure we understand the material.
Prof. Ladshaw is fantastic! He's incredibly caring and really wants everyone to succeed. He's also a great teacher and explains things really well and gives clear processes to solve problems.

His teaching pattern is like he comes in class and does all kind of weird stuff and makes a lot of mistakes then gives a lot of hard assignment. His class is self study, if you think you will understand by reading the book, then go ahead but this professor is not recommended
not recommeded...look for another option if possible..long tests...unsatisfactory explanation of content and extremely unapproachable

This course is a great way to boost your GPA; there's not a whole lot of work and Dr. Avent-Holt makes lectures entertaining and informative.

review_highlights.comment: One of the best professors in the AE department. If you have the chance to take him for anything control related, definitely do it.

Prof. Awal is one of my favorite professors. Even though AE 1601 is meant to be an introductory class, he made it very enjoyable. He was passionate about his work and cared about all the students. Almost everyone in the class got an A as long as they did the work. God bless this man.

Prof. Awal is always willing to help his students. He really does care about how well his students do in class. His lectures are very organized and easy to follow. There's an extra credit project he gives out near the end of the class that's fairly simple.

Very Inspirational lecturer. I attended every office hour and did a lot of extra credit. He is the true reason why I want to become an Aerospace Engineer. He is the key connection to getting an internship

review_highlights.comment: Respectfully, the WORST professor I've ever had in my undergraduate career. The tests were extremely poorly written, very stingy with partial credit. The first exam didn't have much partial credit and two midterm exams are weighed 17.5% each so it definitely will cause major dent in your grade if you don't do well. She was the worst! Her lecture videos never fully matched what we did in the book. Made us buy WielyPlus just for quizzes. She never understood the material she was teaching and was very rude on piazza. The TAs were no help either. She graded harshly on the exams. Look at "Tuba Ketenci" for other reviews on her! DO YOUR BEST TO NOT TAKE HER!

Overall, the class is relatively easy, with online lectures that are mostly useless (she just reads the slides) and lots of extra credit. However, she may be the laziest teacher I've ever had. She showed up late to every exam we had and was often aggressive when responding to student questions. Her other RateMy is under "Tuba Ketenci."

Yes she doesn't teach this class. THERE ARE NO LECTURES. Its all just online videos that have a bunch of typos. But this class is fair, the questions on the test are very similar to the textbook questions. Just watch her lecture videos, and do the book problems. If you have any questions they will respond pretty fast on piazza.

analysis.name: Ayanna Cummings
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: I would definitely recommend taking Dr. Cummings for General Psychology. The first week when she goes over the syllabus it may seem like a lot of work, but do not worry. The biggest things are a few group projects which can be fun if you choose for them to be. Tests are the easiest, lectures can be a bit by the books, but Dr. Cummings really cares

Easily the best PSYC1101 professor at Tech. Lectures themselves are average, but the fact that she genuinely cares for her students really sets her apart. Tests are fair, and there are a few group projects that really aren't bad because she's very lenient with grading. She's very understanding and accommodating, as long as you communicate with her.

Dr. Cummings wants to see nothing but her students succeed. She was very lenient with grading and extra credit. The bulk of the grade came from group projects and a final research paper. The lectures were admittedly quite by the book, but what to expect from a Gen. Psych class. She gave very engaging activities during some lectures though.

I took this class Spring 2020. She was a great professor for Intro to Psychology. Her best quality is that she really makes sure that all of her students will succeed. She is lenient and understanding with your pace in this new material and with assignment milestones. Highly recommend this class for your start at Tech.

Professor Cummings cares so much about her students and wants to see them succeed. You can also tell she is very passionate about her subject. She is lenient with due dates too. Nothing but great things to say about her, would totally recommend.

analysis.name: Hayriye Ayhan
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She explains very well. However, she could be very bias with students, which make it very unfair. Tests are difficult but doable. And homework could be long and sometimes hard

Full disclosure it's been a while since I had Prof Ayhan for 3232, but the fact that I still remember her as a great teacher speaks volumes. I don't remember many of my Tech profs. My own kid is in college now which is why I'm on this site. I took 3232 in 2001 and it's crazy seeing Ayhan is still teaching this course 25 years later. She's great!

Professor Ayhan is awesome! This class is homework and test heavy, but if you go to class you will do really well in the course! Doing the practice exams and homework will also help you do well on the exams!

Very helpful, clear lectures. She really wants the class to be engaged in what she's teaching  and will nag you until you participate, which is good because you really have to be paying attention in lecture. Would recommend her for any IE class. Tests and homeworks are difficult but fair

Exam heavy class which is awesome! Ayhan is incredibly sweet and quite funny, but the lectures can drag on for a while. Tests include lots of partial credit. No concepts are incredibly conceptual difficult, but it does require a heavy amount of memorization of various formulae.

analysis.name: Azadeh Ansari
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The professor's attitude/approach to teaching were disappointing. She came across as arrogant, often implying she was intellectually beyond Georgia Tech. Her teaching style lacked clarity, enthusiasm, and genuine care for students. When concerns were raised, her justifications were often dismissive.

She is actually good at teaching IFF you go to office hours in person. She didn't have office hours in person until the last 3 weeks of school. She neglected the class until the last 3 weeks. P much screwed students out of getting an A in, what should be, a super easy class. When she actually put effort towards the end, she was a really good prof.

Right before the first exam, she changed the policy from open notes to one crib sheet. She told us OpAmps would not be on exam1. Day before exam1 released a topic list that included OpAmps. Released incorrect topic list for exam2 causing many students to fail. She just began doing in-person office hours. Online office hours are completely useless.

I am not concerned about my grade and just finished the exam for this course. I was lost during the lectures as basics of circuit theory is covered in this course. Most of the time, the professor is just copying the derivations without providing any intuitive link between the theory and physical concept! The teaching style does not resonate well.

I did find the lectures confusing and I enjoyed more going through the textbook by myself and I learned much more effective. I believe she should not teach such a fundamental course as it kills the motivations on ECE students. Every time we tried to convey the message that we were struggling she managed to justify by saying that it is a flipped!

analysis.name: Azad Naeemi
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: This course was broad and ranges from device limitations to system limitations. Dr Naeemi was amazing at getting concepts across to students of different backgrounds within electronics, and the transitions felt very smooth. This was the best course I took at Gatech until date- mainly cause of the teaching style. I strongly recommend this experience

Best professor @ GT. Very sharp and enthusiastic about course material (akin to his area of research). Approachable and fair. Was exceptional at determining what might be the students' stumbling block(s), and addressing said topics lucidly . Would recommend without reservation or hesitation.

Naeemi is such a bro! Seriously, I want to give him a hug he's so awesome. At Gatech a teacher of this caliber is unheard of! If you're wondering what professor to take 3040 with: STOP! This is him! Great teaching, prepares you for test, gives similar practice test online, and really cares about his students. Naeemi is a God!

Professor Naeemi did an excellent job of articulating the subject matter. He was very approachable and seemed genuinely interested in your understanding of the topics. Dr. Naeemi emphasizes classroom involvement, so make sure you're up to date before coming to class!

Naeemi was a good professor and managed well through a very difficult subject. He understands the content very well and provides a lot of supporting material to help students gain a better understanding. He is very accommodating and supportive and wants to see students succeed.

analysis.name: Amir Azarvan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This guy is great. Killer beard and stache should tell you everything you need to know. Funny, chill, understanding, impartial, the list goes on and on. Lectures are interesting, always relevant and intriguing topics. Participate, do the assignments, study for simple MCQ tests, and you'll do great. Multiple opportunities for extra credit. Take him.

He's a great professor with a great sense of humor and great stories. His lectures are always engaging and up-to-date. We had a presidential election simulation, really fun and offers a lot of extra credits. Too bad he's not an official prof at GT.

He is a very enjoyable professor and has interesting lectures if you go. I took his class at GT in the Fall of 2023. All of my exams were online and multiple choice. You also have to write 3 discussion posts (about 500 words) throughout the course on topics of your choice. This class felt like it was half a credit hour as opposed to 3. Easy A

Studying for tests and writing a few short essays is all you need to do to pass the class. Professor is very lenient and gives good lectures. Class debates and discussions are always interesting and professor is fair to both sides. Uses current events to keep things fresh and grab attention of students.
Professor Azarvan is the best; super easy class and a great lecturer.

analysis.name: Lesley Baradel
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 86 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Overall, this class isn't very difficult in terms of content. You typically have one or two writing assignments due every week that just ask you to reflect on what you discussed in lecture or an external website. Attendance is mandatory, but slides are uploaded to Canvas; most people do other work during lecture since there is no midterm/final.

Took this course asynchronously. We had a lecture and a few assignments posted each week. The lectures were quite engaging and required little work. Class focused on dimensions of wellness and helped me learn a lot of strategies to improve each! Overall, great class with a great professor and TAs who are always willing to help.

If you are just looking to get the required health credit done take this course! Mandatory attendance at lectures will take up about 2 hours, and then there's only like 2 hours of busy work a week. No tests, no quizzes, no long essays. Very nice professor, and lectures are interesting if you do decide to pay attention

Professor Baradel is amazing! All you had to do was complete the homework (generally very quick and easy, not graded harshly at all) and show up to class (she gives like 4 free absences though). She is super sweet and accommodating with assignments, too!

Took online async, 2-3 assignments open up per week due Monday 11:59pm. Slightly frustrating cuz some weeks I had more time and could've knocked out the next month's worth of assignment but only opens up 2 per week. Always sent out weekly announcements and plenty of reminders and always responded within the next couple hours of emailing her.

analysis.name: Katie Badura
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Badura was an amazing teacher for this class. Even though the course was at 8am, she managed to keep lectures entertaining and not once did I want to skip class because of her. She is super engaging with her students and loves what she does which makes it so much easier to take the class with her overall. 10/10 would take again!

Best professor ever. If you don't get an A in this class then that's 100% on you. She gives you everything you could need to succeed. I never took notes and she gives you what slides to study before the test. Just show up on the days you're told and study the slides she lists.

really liked her class and she's very easy to talk to. puts effort into learning everyones name and engaging people in discussion. would definitely take her class again, there's no final but each midterm (3) is 22% of the grade (tests are almost 70%). they're not difficult though, fairly easy and she posts the exact slides to study on study guides.

I loved professor Badura! She kept lectures interesting, learned everyone's names, and brought us donuts on the second to last day. She gives you a list of what slides to study for the test, which is extremely helpful if you have a busy schedule. Would take again!
Katie really is a wonderful professor, she is a rare breed that genuinely cares about both her class and her content. I honestly wish all my professors were more like her.

analysis.name: Martina Balic
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This class was extremely frustrating. She talks in the most monotone voice to show us how to use CAD, and if you don't sit in the front, it's hard to see what she does on the board. The TA will try to help but then you miss more of the lecture. Be prepared to stay after class to finish studio work later in the semester and spend hours on projects.

After this class, I am heavily considering switching majors. Not only are her lectures extremely boring and hard-to-follow, but her feedback is unhelpful and passive-aggressive. The only reason the class itself isn't difficult is because of the lenient grading--by the TA. 
This class is a 1-credit-hour-class, but be ready to spend 4+ hrs/week.

Professor Balic does go fast through lectures, and it can be hard to keep up and follow along. For 1070 be prepared to put in more time than you expect though. Attendance is graded but if you miss studio it'll be hard to catch up anyways. Grading wasn't too harsh but was mostly done by the TA, so it might vary from semester to semester.

She knows her stuff, but can be hard to follow lectures sometimes. If you miss a step, you might be confused for the next 15 min. There is very minimal feedback given on assignments, but you're likely to get a good grade anyways. If you have any questions, she is more than willing to help you. The final project was really fun and had extra credit.

Lectures could be a little dull but overall the course was well taught and very easy. Showing up to studio and paying attention was extremely important though as posted materials weren't nearly as thorough as lectures and comments made in lecture were crucial for completing assignments.

analysis.name: Nazanin Bassiri Gharb
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She's not a bad teacher but uses few examples and expects you to know more than she teaches. She isn't very nice to students, especially when talking one on one. She is very unforgiving.

Two midterms, 9 HW's which are just writing 2 questions per HW problem, final is no longer optional. Polarizing professor for sure. Responds sarcastically to some questions, lectures fast, and is a tough grader. To offset her rough exams, she provides 5 bonus points via bonus assignments which she would often poorly explain and are due next class.

Professor Bassiri-Gharb is the best professor I've taken at Tech to be honest. She's extremely caring, understanding and reasonable. She's very straightforward on how to be successful in her class, and her exams are very fair based off of in-class examples, homeworks, and past exams. Made Thermo easier to understand and loved taking her section

She is a great lecturer that knows a lot about thermodynamics, teaches her subject with energy, and clearly cares about preparing her lectures (which are both tutorial-like and self-contained). It was also cool when she answered students' questions with info she learned from her research. The classroom was also full and lively.

Professor is generally caring if you reach out to her, responds very fast. Midterms are difficult but generally not bad if you take good notes in lectures and redo homeworks, homeworks are also not bad at all. Takes random participation for some lectures but has pretty good extra credit. Had a good time and learned a lot.

analysis.name: Sal Barone

review_highlights.comment: Lectures can move fast-paced at times, but usually he makes sure that his students understand the gist of the lesson before moving on. Don't skip lecture and take organized notes! Homework is on MyLab, due every Tuesday - not bad. The exams can be a little difficult, but they're fair as long as you do ALL the problems in the review packet. Cool guy
The class was unnecessarilly hard. I like sal a lot,  but his lectures were all over the place and made little sense. He taught more to those who understood math at a very advanced level.
Sal is really enthusiastic about math and learning but sometimes that prevents him from being a clear teacher. He is really sweet, though, and wants to see everyone succeed.
Great Teacher. If you do all the review sheets/recitation papers, and review past test/quizzes, the quizzes and tests become much easier.

I didnt realize how bad of a prof he was until I took more classes. He never posted ANY material on canvas, he didnt have any lecture slides. I could barely keep up w/his chicken scratch. analysis.name: Meghan Babcock
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 48 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Pretty much exactly what other reviews say, extremely organized, with everything laid out from the start of the semester, and you can learn all the material for each exam the night before and easily get an A. The content is really interesting, and Dr. Babcock is super caring and engaging, and this ended up being one of my favorite classes at tech.

She is so kind hearted, organized and amazing at teaching. Her exams are a little long (60+ mcqs) but they do not test trivia - only main ideas. On her last class, she had us do a Jeopardy style preparation that was very helpful for the exam. I could not say enough nice things about her. If you can get into her class, take it trust.

Dr Babcock is exceptionally organized. She's very responsive to emails (even responding to me once on a Sunday) and understanding of her students. I did the extra credit assignments wrong but she still gave me credit cause she said she could see I put in effort. Online lectures are always difficult but she does her best to keep them interesting.

She is very understanding and responsive outside of class. Her tests are very fair and easy to prepare for with just a little bit of studying, even if you didn't pay attention during the lectures. Attendance is checked through random in-class assignments throughout the semester. The class is very easy and pretty intuitive.

Top 2 and shes not 2. Teaches so well and keeps things interesting. Review lecture slides and you'll ace exams (honorlock). All other assignments are straight forward and youll have ample time to do them. Genuinely not a single complaint.

analysis.name: Brian Beck

review_highlights.comment: You won't see this dude, quizzes depend on your TA. Go to class, read the manual beforehand. It's an annoying class but the TA's are helpful. Just learn the book properly and YouTube the theory and you'll be fine.

Everyone above an 89% got an A in the class. The homeworks also took a long time--they weren't graded for accuracy, but I still wanted to try and get them correct.

This class is like ECE 3043 but improved. That being said it is still a difficult class that takes a lot of time but you learn a lot more and get a lot more out of it. There were 3 tests which were fair, a final project, and a handful of labs which all took longer than the dedicated lab time. However, Dr. Beck was very supportive throughout.
If you don't get a good TA, good luck. Horrendously run class with zero room for error.
do not take during study abroad, he was unreasonably hard and his exams were ruthless. Most Ive ever studdied for a class and still did terrible.

analysis.name: Saad Bhamla

review_highlights.comment: Dr.Bhamla is very sweet and accessible outside of the class. The class is heavily about fluid mechanics, so be prepared for long and complicated math problems. Dr.Bhamla cares about his student and goes above and beyond to help. The material is difficult, so make sure you spend enough time to learn.

Professor Bhamla is the perfect example of a passionate, curious, and enthusiastic scientist. He engages the class in a way that unparalleled by any other professor I've taken a lecture from. Prof Bhamla constantly encourages audience participation and peer learning, and integrates fascinating videos showing the applications of Transport Phenomena.

Thermo is concept heavy, but Dr. Bhamla's biggest strength is explaining concepts. However, he doesn't have time in class to work out many numerical problems. 2130 deserves to be 3 credit hrs. Recitation/TA office hrs are key for understanding those. He expects you to be a good critical thinker. His homeworks are tough, but his exams are fair.

I get the vibe that he doesn't actually know much thermo conceptually. He's not bad at teaching per se, though he doesn't give much explanation. Terrible at answering questions, but he does try. He likes the practical aspect more than the equations so he shows videos in class that are quite cool. Overall, 7/10.
Doesn't understand much Thermo and classes are a mess.

Averages would be failing and he would say "I don't see any means for a curve"

He did a very good job of teaching the material and explained concepts well with good practice problems. Also is super funny and genuinely one of the most caring professors. Really wants his sections to succeeds, is super available outside of class, and frequently asks for and applies any feedback given very happily. Would definitely recommend.

I struggled significantly in this course, but that was no fault of his. Honestly, I believe I may not have even had the chance at passing this course without him. Dr. Behrens is very kind and considerate of his students. He goes above & beyond to help his students succeed. If you have to take this course, he is by far the best professor.
He was so kind and genuinely cared about each of us. He made sure his office hours accommodated every single student. He cares so much about us and physics which made the class more enjoyable.

Lectures: not helpful & boring

Test: felt like the lecture contents barely helped to actually answer questions - googling is much more effective

Seems like a great guy, but definitely does not need to teach MSE 2001.

Professor Brown moved slowly through material, leaving a full unit to learn on our own via online videos. Lectures were often unclear, but projects and test corrections were easy and boosted grades. Attendance was mainly needed for participation credit rather than understanding.

Dr. Brown is great at explaining things. One thing that I particularly liked was the fact that when he did not know something, he would take the effort to find out and explain it. However, he is a bit slow during lectures and we didn't even get to the last unit. However, I'm going to give him a pass since it was his first time teaching the course.

analysis.name: Biing Juang

review_highlights.comment: The instruction is good but there is too much content to cover in this class. TA's are lifesavers with recitation and office hours. You will never forget this class!

Prof. knows the content of the course well, but is very bad at transferring that knowledge to his students. Lectures are hard to pay attention to, there are no materials to study for the tests that actually reflect what the test will be like, and the only time I ever learned content was in recitation and by struggling on the HW. Take anyone else.

Prof. Juang is a very chill dude and he's pretty caring if you just reach out to him with your problems. I would say the hardest part of this class (besides attendance) is doing well on HW.
You should just ask ChatGPT to explain the content to you during lectures, since attendance is mandatory, and this guy acts smug while proceeding to say nothing of value.

The only issues I had with Professor Juang were more issues with how ECE 2026 is administered as a course. It's a weed out and is designed to be a little unfair at times. I can't fault Professor Juang for any of my complaints on that, as it would be the case with any 2026 professor. Very knowledgeable and helpful if asked for help.

analysis.name: Mohammad Najjartabar Bisheh

One of the better stats professors out there. He has a very generous grading policy, gifting you up to 15% free if you just show up to lecture. Tests were a bit difficult but doable if you studied. First sem teaching but did his best. HWs are easy, but nothing is representative of exams. Nice and respectful, just a wonky class structure.

analysis.name: Vicki Birchfield

review_highlights.comment: For INTA 3050- very nice professor and VERY easy class but her lectures are so disorganized. she tends to ramble for the entire class with no real point. Hated going to class, but worth it for the A!

Took the course in Fall 2021. Vicki has a notorious reputation for going onto tangents but she is an incredibly caring person and will do everything she can (both inside and outside class) to get to know you and help.
She was the program lead for FYFA and while she loved to go on about tangents, she is one of the nicest people I've ever met.

I've had Birchfield for another class before. She can definitely be scattered and hard to follow sometimes, but overall, she's a very good professor. While she and I may not always have same or similar opinions, she's not the sort of professor to hold it against you or effect your grade. I'm looking forward to taking a third class with her.

She does not directly use the book she says is "required" for class, but requires students to read several pages of it for each class module. Her field trips are not always well planned. Her slides are clumsy and filled with text, and scheduling of assignments is done verbally only.
She led a study abroad I participated in during Summer 2014. She was clear, concise, and was clearly vested in making sure we all learned from the trip. One of the best professors I've had at Tech.

analysis.name: Laura Bier

review_highlights.comment: 4 textbooks barely used.dont buy. u can get by by gogling the readings. And unless you have to turn in a paper, dont bother doing the readings. Too much assigned and a complete waste of time. Ask her for her expectation on midterm papers because she is alot stricter when grading those. Class borng. she needs to learn 2 teach rather than readng ppt

She is a nice professor. She gives out everything that is going to be on the midterm and final, so study that a lot. Don't turn anything in late.

For the most part you will pass if you read and understand the textbook, which the tests are directly based on. Most classtime is devoted to lectures which ho more in-depth. The teacher is very enthusiastic about the topics she teaches.

She's super passionate about what she's teaching. Lectures can be long, but interesting. She took weeks to grade things, which was rough. Just pay attention in class and at least skim the readings and you'll get an A.

analysis.name: Mario Bianchini
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: I enrolled in this course as an elective but was pleasantly surprised by how engaged I became in its content, as the professor does a great job in conveying his enthusiasm. Favorite course of the semester! Classes were discussion based. The readings were extremely interesting, and our class got to vote on topics to cover for the last few weeks. Tests were based on ability to apply concepts from class, and were very similar to the short weekly responses. Professor was very kind and respectful of everyone's opinions.

Very open-minded and respectful of everyone's opinions in this discussion-based class. There is a lot of reading and writing involved, and while the material is interesting, I wish the class was more engaging. Positive attitude and willingness to listen to feedback.

analysis.name: Steven Biegalski

review_highlights.comment: I'll be honest- I have no interest in Nuclear Engineering, and just had to take this class to graduate. However, Professor Biegalski was by far one of the best professors I had at tech. He teaches very clearly. His tests are extremely fair. He really cares about the well being of his students. I really wish I could have had him for more classes.

I encourage you to get to know Dr. Biegalski both inside ad outside  of class.  Assuming you like him, see if you can get involved in his research.  He send another girl from my class for a professional conference in Hawaii this past semester for her to present he research,  that would be a good GT experience,

Also ask him about fly fishing.

I had Dr. Biegalski for NRE 3112, and on multiple occasions he made it clear that he really does care about his students. Dr. Biegalski also does a good job lecturing and answering questions, as well as just being a really chill and affable professor. My only complaint is that he oftentimes is too nice and students would heavily abuse that.

I took his class to graduate during Spring 2020. He is definitely in my top 5 favorite professors at Tech. He teaches the material extremely well, is interested in getting to know all of his students, and I had a ton of fun learning about nuclear reactions, reaction design, and nuclear energy. I wish he taught more classes.
Very engaging professor and made me even more interested in nuclear engineering.

analysis.name: Bill Todd

He's very lenient grader. Show up and try; you will make an A.
This was a great class with a bunch of guest lectures from people in the health care industry. I really enjoyed this class

Professor Todd really cares about his students.  I would suggest taking this class even if you are not interested in healthcare.  Straight up grades, two essay tests, case assignments, and class participation.  Professor really wants students to succeed. LOTS of guest speakers

Class was pretty easy. Just show up to class. Most of what you see on the test was said in class, so attendance is key. He's also a pretty cool guy. His stories are interesting. He has a lot of connections so he's someone you would want to know!

Such an interesting course. If you have any interest in healthcare, take it. Professor Todd is the best professor! He has a discussion based class about half of the time and excellent guest speaker the other half of the time. He is genuinely interested in your success as a student. I wish I could take this class every semester!

analysis.name: James Blumling
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: At times, the only thing that got me through this class was knowing that his actor clips existed. While working on the hours of homework that I had every week, I would turn on one of those bad boys to feel better about myself. I didn't take MATLAB before this course (since it is no longer a prerequisite) and the exams felt nearly impossible.

Course is very challenging, and lectures were long and content heavy. Despite it being confusing most of the time, going to the lectures was important to grasp the material. Professor was very generous with grading along with an easy project grade, however he expects that you do your part in the learning process meet him halfway to be successful

I couldn't tell you a single thing I learned in class, and by the end there might have been 5 people going. Crappy Lectures. The homework wasn't too bad as you were allowed to use AI for coding, and the exams were open note(not open internet), yet this didn't really help with his slides. The project was fine. I survived but never again...

Dr. Blumling is a subpar lecturer. He likes to make material that is not just challenging but also often beyond the reach of the students. He wants to push students, but his methodology is not incremental, and it's frustrating because the class could be much more digestible and achievable if it were not made challenging for no reason.

While a considerate person, he is not a considerate professor... Does not work through content clearly, no examples, no practice. He seems to throw everything at you and assume you are not a good student if you do not go to office hours or ask how to do something--especially if he says you did it completely wrong. His tests are an overkill.

analysis.name: Nathan Blackburn
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Made Orgo 1 so easy to understand. He's very nice and engaging in class as well, and is easy to contact for questions. So many options for extra credit. Exams were very similar to practice exams and textbook questions. Definitely have to put in work because its organic chem, but Professor Blackburn does not try to make it harder.

I can't speak on Nathan's classroom style, as I've only had the pleasure of having him be a TA for my 2311 lecture and 2380 lab. However, I can confidently say that Nathan is an amazing teacher, and has a way of explaining and working through difficult concepts and making them significantly easier to comprehend. Take his class if given the chance.

I was terrified to take organic chemistry this semester, but Nathan genuinely made the class interesting and less intimidating, and I ended up really enjoying a class that I'd dreaded taking my entire college career. He gives out a good bit of extra credit and is super accessible for office hours and stuff! Goated professor.

Genuinely made Orgo a breeze, you can tell he loves it and knows a lot. Flipped classroom, but the lectures really help you lock down concepts because practice is built in. He wants you to succeed and will give CIOS bonus and extra credit opportunities. Just such a nice guy overall.
He has a great way of making difficult concepts easy to understand and is an incredible lecturer.

analysis.name: Matthieu Bloch
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I don't think he deserves all the hate that these reviews have been giving him. The class was fair and the exams were very similar to the homework. He is a nice person and mostly accommodating. He is very slow, but he also doesn't normally teach, and his section was only added to accommodate the influx of freshmen. This is not a deadly class.

Professor Bloch is an extremely caring professor, who is always willing to distribute knowledge on any subject he has on hand. Signal processing, machine learning, life lessons, he has and will teach about anything. Being in this VIP course has taught me so much, even when I started from no knowledge at all.

Lied to our faces about exam questions multiple times. Emphasized proof-based math questions instead of engineering/ system design ones, where the slightest error could cost you half credit. Only covered half of the material listed in the syllabus; we have to catch up now. His reviews for the graduate-level classes have the exact same complaints.

We got to early October's material in December. He regularly makes promises he doesn't keep.

He has described his own grading scheme as brutal. Every (lengthy) question is 2 points. If you write down anything you get 1 point. If you get the entire problem correct with no small errors at all, you get 2 points. 85% of the course grade was exams.

I thought he great, other guy talking about his french bit is just a hater. His lectures were super engaging and in depth, I feel like I really learned why things are implemented the way they are. The homework was also very helpful and translated well to the tests. It is true that he was behind in his material, but you can tell he's just passionate

analysis.name: Justin Blann
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Blann is very caring and considerate. The class is mostly comprised of 4 exams, 10 quizzes, and textbook work. To prepare for the exams you'll typically have 2-3 practice exams. Homework sets help you prepare, too. You'll also be allowed one note card for exams. For homework, the textbook is very helpful. Extra credit opportunities were given.

Prof. Blann cared about his students, and wanted them to learn. He was especially attentive about ODS accommodations, and never once made me feel uncomfortable about asking for what I needed. His grading scheme was forgiving, so long as you put forth the effort needed. My only regret is not having more time to dedicate to his class.

Such a fun class and professor! Unique approach of teaching valuable acct content in an enjoyable and low-stress format. Assignments include many small group projects, a few pop quizzes, and the final was a slightly larger group project. One of my fav classes I have taken at GT, so ABSOLUTELY take it if you need an extra MGT/accounting elective!

Professor Blann is super nice and accommodating!! His lectures are alright, but the class is pretty straightforward. I would only say that I felt like the online section got much better grades than the in-person section (I was in-person section). Attendance is basically mandatory since he has mini quizzes for attendance almost every class

Professor Blann is a great professor! Although the class is a little boring and lectures are mostly just him reading slides, Professor Blann provided several extra credit opportunities, homework's that really helped for the test, and a flash card on each test. He also is very understanding and will help you if needed. Overall, good class!

analysis.name: John Blazeck
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I had him for chbe 2140 thermodynamics. He's a very nice and knowledgeable guy. I'm not sure how he put my name to my face seeing as I've never introduced myself but that shows how much he cares about his students. Definitely a difficult class with absolutely no curves. Homework is harder than the tests and graded harshly for accuracy.

No curve, longer homeworks than the other sections, reference sheet only on tests (other professors have open textbook or crib sheets), and no notes posted so attendance is "mandatory." However, he cares about his students and he has so many resources available. He prepares everyone really well for his class; I struggled but I'm glad I took him.

Blazeck was a great 2100 professor, his lectures were great and it was clear that he knew the subject well. He doesn't curve tests, but they're very do-able and lots of partial credit. He also doesn't upload his notes from lecture, so you won't pass if you don't go to class. The homework is time consuming, but you're given plenty of time to do it.
Blazeck is tough, but a great lecturer and clearly a nice guy. No curve or crib sheet is absolutely brutal, but his exams are fair. His homework is very long.

Actually ended up really liking chbe 2100 with Blazeck. Pretty sure it was his first time teaching, but lectures were well organized and straight forward. He made it pretty clear what you need to do to succeed. Grades pretty easy relative to other teachers for 2100 and tests weren't too crazy. Would definitely recommend. Very understanding as well.

analysis.name: Alex Blumenthal
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Blumenthal is a chill professor, his lectures may be tangential at times, but teaches everything you need to know for the tests. HW's are varying in difficulty, however, they shouldn't take too much time. Overall decent professor, especially for math. Beware that midterm and final is worth 35% and 45% respectively.

He doesnt teach from the textbook, but he moves along it. His lectures are basically his thoughts/what's on his mind. That makes it sound unprofessional, but he's actually really good at explaining things, and even better at answering questions. Very approachable, and very helpful.

I took this course in Fall 2022. Blumenthal is very knowledgeable about 1554 topics; however, he sometimes forgets that his students are not. He rushes through the course content, which made it very hard to keep up - but 1554 is simply a hard class. He is caring for his students, but could be a better communicator. Take Barone!

Where do I even start with ol' Blue. Blumenthal is one of the better lecturers and while he may move fast, he covers everything necessary to ace the tests. Just hope he doesn't eat Twisted Taco before class and you will be alright.
Blumenthal's lectures are good, but I couldn't enjoy them because the course was super easy. A good load of homework, but not too bad.

analysis.name: Jacob Blevins

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Jacob Blevins is not just a professor—he is an intellectual deity sent from the celestial realms to bless us mere mortals with wisdom. Grading? Fair and just like the scales of truth. Feedback? So insightful it feels like prophecy. Passion for the subject? Enough to make scholars weep. His class isn't just education—it's ascension. ⭐11/5⭐

Jacob Blevins is the GOAT. Excellent lecturer. Material isn't boring at all and he takes time on the details of the notes. Solves problems himself in class rather than just rewriting steps from notes. Homework prepare you well for the exams. Jacob Blevins is a professor that actually cares about the quality of his communication skills.

What more can be said about the great Jacob Blevins that hasn't already been said. Much like Mithrandir in the Lord of the Rings, he is an unstoppable force for good, proliferating light and warmth to Tech Tower and beyond, a proverbial angel among men. His name can be heard spoken in the streets of Home Park, whispering of his greatness.

Blevins is hands down the best instructor for 2110. I took the 6:30 pm to 9:15 pm section but it was worth taking considering how much this man respected our hard work in the class. 2110 is hell, but he will make it WAYYY easier than the other instructors for 2110.
In a one on one decision between teachers, always bet on Blevins.

analysis.name: Greg Blekherman

review_highlights.comment: His class was the hardest in my degree, but I always felt confident because I knew he was always there for us. I see so many people saying he was a very tough professor and that the practices were nothing like the exam. analysis.name: Bolei Deng

a great lecturer, learned a lot in class and its very clear he cares abt the students. projects and exams all have extra credit portions, everything is graded reasonably. hw is a bit difficult but he is very helpful during office hours and it is reasonable to what we are learning in class. great guy would definitely take him again.

one of fav profs at gt, great guy, hard class but explained clearly. very fair prof. 30% 10 hw 1drop, 1exam 15%, 3project 10% each but 1st is free, 2&3 use matlab. 25% final not cumulative. bonus on tests. has zoom link for class and records. only criticism: he talks quiet. you will actually learn dynanmics here unlike patil where its a free A lol

analysis.name: Bobby Harris
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: He's awesome, made me want to do an econ minor. I think anybody who engages with the class and asks questions should be able to get an A. Chill guy, has good examples in lectures and asks class for input. Lectures can sometimes get boring but he makes the content easy to learn homework almost every week but its not hard and helped me learn the majority of the content, plenty of extra credit. Solid professor who cares about economics, practice tests are super similar to actual tests

I thought I could get away with skipping the lectures bit it was almost 9% of my grade - I would've gotten an A otherwise. The class is not hard, the homework assignments can be tedious but there is extra credit. The tests are just like the practice ones he gives and he reuses the same format and types of questions.

He is an amazing lecturer who is also very understanding and clearly just wants you to feel good about the topic. His exams are definitely more challenging than other ECON 2106 exams because he tests on applications not just concepts, but I think you get a far better learning experience.

great professor, very caring, learned a lot from this class. Attendance is mandatory, but you only have to meet for like half the semester. The assignments are not too bad and are really useful. material does overlap some with ECE1100, but there is new material and she goes more in depth

All the materials have been covered in ECE1100. There is no reason for school to offer this course as required to earn students' tuition. The content taught in ECE1100 is more useful than this course btw.

analysis.name: Bo Kim

Dr. Bo Kyoung Kim was an amazing professor for linguistics. Her interest in the subject made classes more interesting and engaging. Assignments were fair; all exams were online; in-class quizzes were quick and given enough notice for preparation.
Dr. Kim was such a nice teacher and her class was easy with a little effort. She always responds to emails and cares a lot about her students. Put in the work and it's an easy A.

analysis.name: Rodrigo Borela

CS1301 isn't a real intro. Rod goes way too fast. Labs and TAs are awful. Never take robotics. They claim it's easier but it's hell, with async topics that don't belong in an intro. I had literally no coding experience before going into class but found is really manageable. Lectures are recorded, so you don't have to go to class. I would recommend going to recitation and doing practice exams. Also there's like 2 points of extra credit added onto your grade at the end.

analysis.name: Bryce Truitt

analysis.name: Bo Zhu

This class has 8 super easy hws, 2 medium-difficult quizzes (depending on whether you studied hard or not), and a final project. I expected this class to be difficult or take a lot of my time, but it was honestly so chill. The instructions for the hws are very straight-forward and clear, and I never got stuck at all. Bho Zhu loves what he teaches.

Dr. Zhu is a goated professor. There are 8 straightforward programming assignments, 2 open-note take-home online quizzes, and the class overall is great. He's super knowledgeable and clearly knows his stuff, if you can take him for graphics, 100% do it

Hope this class becomes a permanent media/intel option

analysis.name: Brian German

German is legit my FAVORITE professor at this school. He is absolutely the nicest person you will ever meet, and he lectures like he's babying the class, NOT in a demeaning way but in a charming way. Mr. Burdell is AMAZING. He can be hard to find, but he's also everywhere. Being that he graduated with every major and accomplished much more, his stories are very inspirational.

Structures is known as one of the "hard" classes in AE, and Prof. Di Leo makes it bearable! Without a curve, we would all have failed the class, but we know from the start we get a curve.
