I hear GT is making improvements to BMED 2110 for future semesters, though, so it might get better than it was for us. Her biggest mistake was giving 1/2 the class only 2 hours for what was supposed to be a 3 hour exam.

Dr. Cross appeared to be a nice person but if I'm being honest, she didn't know anything in regard to BME. If you asked her a question, the first thing she would ask you is if your question made common sense, which is not something that I want to hear if I asked a question. She also shorted us on time for the final exam by an hour. Don't recommend

never showed up to class, and when she did it was to tell us to practice mindfulness, eat, sleep, and preach condescendingly to us about the course material. She does not know anything about the material. I asked her a question and her response was, "think about it." Im sorry, what did i take this class for? TA's make or break the course

analysis.name: Cameron Crotts
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Took history of jazz with Prof. Crotts over the summer. Class was taught either by him or his coworker friend. Tests are not hard if you memorize the slides. Content is really interesting and a nice break from these rigorous STEM classes at Tech. Highly recommended for that Humanities credit.

Wonderful class. Laid back instructors and interesting material. Bonus: we got out early almost every day. Great choice for a humanities elective or free elective during the summer. If you do anything in this class, you will almost certainly make an A.

This course is great if you need an easy A humanities course. I took this course online over the summer, and it was async and ended in the first week of June. There were three exams and one paper, which can be exempted if you get 100s on all three exams. Crotts was very caring and lenient, and he provides all the material you need to ace the exams.

One of the most easiest class at GT if taken online. The classes is comprised of 3 exams and 1 paper, all of which are really easy. The summer online class is asynch and self-paced. All the resources to do good on the exams are provided in Canvas. The research paper is extremely light and templates are provided as guides. Extremely recommend!

Took MUSI 3630 during the summer semester for my humanities credit. Best humanities to take. Very interesting (especially is you love music) and easy to follow in a such a fast-paced semester. Crotts is super understanding, very helpful, and very accessible. Would definitely recommend if you want an easy, interesting GPA booster + humanities req.

analysis.name: Craig Tovey
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: If you haven't taken AP stats in HS , don't expect to get over a C in the class

Smart professor , but teaching is not for everybody ! If you care about your GPA , don't do it !!!!!!!! Many students dropped this class because of the way it was taught . Expect ridiculously confusing problems and expect to get 10,5,20 out of 100 on your quizzes ! . (Did not get an A+)

There are good and bad professors and then there's Tovey. Literally the worst professor I've had so far. Not a good intro teacher to IE. Listen to the reviews and avoid AT ALL COST. Very disorganized, gives no partial credit, and should not be teaching at all. If you cherish your life and your sanity, you would listen to me and avoid tovey....

Do not take AT ALL COST. His grading makes no sense and it seems like he doesn't even grade correctly. Just gives points where he wants. He makes up the questions for the tests, and the answers have no clear explanation or reasoning behind them. He just slaps answers together with no clear thinking. Ok class but bad professor.

This is the hardest class I've ever taken. I did not take AP stats in high school and I have no idea what is going on in this class. Every time I show up to lecture it feels like I've missed a lecture in between. He is very unhelpful and is often incredibly condescending to his students. Do not take 2027 with him or you're gonna have a bad time.

analysis.name: Courtney Crooks
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment:
Professor was unwilling to discuss or move assignment dates, frequently released assignments late, and didn't post lectures after she said she would. Essays questions were very complex for the maximum length. Lectures were randomly mandatory and often dull. Easy to get an A, but professor was not easy to work with.
Class taken was CS4263.

Dr. Crooks is so knowledgeable in the field of cyberpsychology. Her lectures were so interesting and covered a lot of different topics related to online behavior and security in depth. Your grade is based on 4 short (2-3 page) reflection papers and 1 final (10-12 page) paper. She's a really easy grader and willing to help you out. Take her!

Very nice, but essentially reads off of the lecture slides. Don't come to class unless you care about the small extra-credit pop quizzes, otherwise look at the study guides she posts as well as the definitions for the book's vocab words and the tests will be a breeze. Very easy grader, very simple tests.

Dr. Crooks's section of General Psych was so much easier compared to others. We had 5 tests that were not cumulative and easy. Going to lecture is completely optional. As long as you read the textbook and can answer her study guides, you will be fine.

Class was super chill. She largely reads off the lecture slides which she also posts. She also provides a study guide before each exam. The exams are also multiple choice. Easy A and very little effort put in.

analysis.name: Cristina Riso
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Aeroelasticity is an extremely difficult class regardless of which professor is teaching it, but Dr. Riso is one of (if not my favorite) my favorite professors at Tech. Although this is only her 2nd time teaching, She's super caring and extremely flexible with deadlines, and is willing to hold additional office hours outside of her normal hours.

AE 4220 is probably the toughest course in the AE curriculum, but Dr. Riso is fantastic. Her lectures are great, and she is SUPER nice. The homework and exams were brutal but fair. Do not expect to pass by just memorizing how to solve the problems. At the end if you're on the edge and you have an outlier score, she'll bump you.

Difficult class. Extremely nice and caring professor. Dr. Riso is willing to sit with you 1 on 1 outside of regular office hours to ensure you understand the material. Everything is take home, but don't lower your guard. The exams are difficult because they require you to actually reason through the concepts to solve the problems.

Great professor, but the content in class as a whole is too advanced to be offered in undergrad imo (not Dr. Riso's fault). Unsteady aerodynamics - a graduate level topic appears in dynamic aeroelasticity, and you need a pretty good grasp of it to understand concepts such as aeroelastic flutter.

AE6230 Actually. 
Professor Riso is amazing. She is extremely reasonable and helpful. The lectures are well structured and to the point. The lectures and assignments complement each other very well. I learnt a lot in her lectures.

analysis.name: Jim Craig
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Took Dr. Craig for COE 3001 in Fall 2016. Homework assignments were incredibly difficult and time-intensive. Lectures lacked organization and were not helpful. Incredibly smart guy, great personality, but he made what should have been a simpler class much more difficult than it needed to be.

The professor is knowledgeable (wrote the textbook), but lectures are outdated—he mostly reads notes with little practical application. Few graded items; the final is 45% (avg was 57.5). Homework is time-consuming (5–8 hrs). Generous curve, so most get A/B. Advice: Skip class, self-study, and prep using past exams/homework, help classmates, pray.

Random question bank 10 minute biweekly quizzes. Homework is 25% while each exam/project is 5%. Final is 45%. Dr. Craig is a professor who has a severe disconnect between the course material and his students. Uses custom notation, changes it randomly, and very unclear when explaining topics. Usually only prof to teach this class, best of luck.

Yet another one of those GT profs who is plenty smart but has completely forgotten how to communicate to people for whom the material is new. He has lots of resources, which seems to be in lieu of streamlining the class. The homeworks are always huge and have to be done with one specific "method" he makes up. Each usually takes 8+ hours.

Genuinely the worst professor I have ever had. Do not take this professor, over 14 homeworks that are over 8 hours long every week, biweekly quizzes where the average is a 45%, and a final worth 45% of the grade, where the class average was a 55%. He doesn't teach well and is severely disconnected from how the students feel. Take with anyone else!

analysis.name: Cuyler Warnock
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: WARNOCK MY GOAT THE GLAZE IS REAL whoever called him the Lorax is so accurate my guy knows anything and everything about math. He is so passionate about Linear it rubs off onto you and he really tries his best in lectures to explain everything in layman's terms. Linear is hard but he makes it doable/even easy. I will miss him and his teaching sm :(

Professor Warnock is an excellent lecturer with some of the most clear explanations I've experienced. I've heard of other students even saying they come to our lectures instead. He also projects his voice really well. Even in the back of a 200 person lecture hall with no mic, I can hear him perfectly. I recommend him to anyone who can get him.

Grading: 3 Midterms + 1 Final (worst midterm 15%, all others & final 20%). "Bucket point" system for the other 25% (need 70pts/120 for full credit)

Lecture: 9/10; Passion: 9/10; Communication: 10/10; Flexibility: 9/10; Test Prep: 10/10

Quirks: Bad handwriting, likes teaching 8:25 a.m. MWF

Recommendation: Would be my first choice for this course.

W professor. The class is pretty hard but if you lock in you can definitely get a good grade. I would also recommend reading through the course textbook Lay Linear Algebra since it follows the course really closely and goes into more details than the lectures have time for, and you lowkey need that for the true and false sections on the tests.

Extremely accessible outside of class. Best linear lecturer by far, took his time to clearly explain material and did not rush through the content. Provided great reviews for the tests, and clearly cares about the success of his students. If you have a different lecturer and are struggling, try to come to his instead as attendance isn't mandatory.

analysis.name: Christian Cuba-Torres
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Real solid professor. Has helpful handouts for each lecture. Clear and straightforward with everything.
He does a good job with his lectures and provides handouts to help students follow his lectures. He is available outside of class and grades/curves fairly.
He is a great teacher who cares about his students. Will take him again gladly, even if he's only teaching an 8 am.

This course is quite tough and requires constant practice; however, Dr. Cuba helps as much as he can by providing: useful notes, midterm reviews, and great lectures. The class averages for all three exams were quite low, but he compensates most everyone who never gave up. Not an easy A.

The ratings who gave Dr. Cuba a 2/3 for kinetics are unreasonable. Though the midterm average was not the best, he kept that in mind and lowered the grade cut-offs based on our grades. He cares about his students. His fill in the blank notes are nice. He records his lectures, so if you miss something in the notes, you can always go back to watch.

analysis.name: Andrew Culbreth
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Culbreth is certainly one of the best professors I've encountered at Tech! His enthusiasm for philosophy is clear to see in his passion infused lectures. He'll challenge your thinking and his own as well, and it's quite honestly a marvelous aspect of his teaching. There is a fair amount of reading, so just pay attention and it'll be fine!

I took Dr. Culbreth for his Philosophy 185 course Emory this past semester, and I have nothing but the highest regard for him. Dr. Culbreth challenges his students to tackle discussion, find meaning and interpret text. He is a passionate, caring and immensely intelligent professor whose courses are rewarding and I cannot recommend enough.

The most passionate professor you'll find! He has definitely made philosophy fun, and during lectures/Q&A sessions you can see his eyes glow when he talks. Very reading heavy, but he supplies reading guides as well. Excellent class
Great teaching style. Cares about students

analysis.name: Jianbo Cui
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: His accent is very hard to understand, and to be completely honest, I don't go to class very often because of it. Still, he's a really nice professor and is more than willing to answer your questions. He's very accessible outside of class and understanding if you have to make up quizzes. If you have concerns, you can email and get a quick response.

Dr. Cui's accent is very heavy and it's hard to understand what he says sometimes. However, he definitely knows his stuff and he tries very hard to help his students; he's extremely good at listening to student feedback and clearly wants you to succeed. As long as you sit up front, follow along in lecture, and do your homework, you should be good.
He speaks with a very thick accent that makes him hard to understand in lecture. He teaches the content fine it is just hard to understand him.

Very heavy accent, but fairly competent lecturer. The structure of his lectures can be hard to follow but you can adjust to the accent. The textbook is free, online, and is an absolute godsend that can carry you through the class, regardless of your prof. His tests and quizzes are on the easier side for 1553.

Really heavy accent so it was hard to learn the already hard math subject. Tries to help out but I learned more from the TA. I just read the textbook, did the HW, and went to tutoring. Definitely more helpful than the professor himself.

analysis.name: Amalia Culiuc
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Math at Tech is HAAARD, but Amalia is both fair, supportive, humorous funny. The way she approaches lectures is very effective: she lays out the basic maths concept, explains it again in layman's words, then does a few examples. Practice your homework until you understand it WELL or you'll suffer. She curves, so don't freak out. Also: OFFICE HOURS.

Tests are fairly straightforward, shouldn't have to study too much; weekly quizzes which help a lot; lectures are easy to follow; Amalia is easy to reach outside of class and gives good feedback; class curved at the end.

She explains things clearly. She also moves at a very reasonable pace and reviews concepts in class instead of rushing through the material like the other profs. She's willing to answer all of your questions and she's super nice. She does make a few mistakes on the board though but she'll give out candy for every 15 mistakes she makes!

I had a lot of problems with this class, thankfully Amalia did her best to make my time easier. Gives very good feedback and is very responsive and helpful whenever you have concerns. She is very clear about the topics you should know for each exam and is more than willing to give a bit of a curve for the sake of fairness.

By far the best math teacher I have had at Tech. She explains things very clearly and moves at a pace so that you don't feel like the class is a week ahead of what you are understanding. The lectures are very interactive and she strives to get students involved during lecture. As long as you do the homework and go to lecture, the tests are doable.

analysis.name: Ken Cunefare
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The material in this class was super interesting to me. Dr. Cunefare has a definite interest in the material and does really try to get students to enjoy it as well. The class can get pretty tedious, and the homeworks are commonly over things we haven't covered yet in lecture.

Fantastic professor who actually made me interested in the content. He gives you everything you need to know in his lectures, and by the end of the semester, he makes sure everyone gets a fair grade, even if the semester is tough.
Enjoyed the IC Engines class.  It was difficult but Dr. C's lectures were well planned and the material was clearly presented.
Disrespectful to students. Doesn't care about you.

analysis.name: Jennifer Curtis
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 42 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Many times, she would skip over problems or an explanation stating that it was "easy", when I had no idea how to do it, or would make things much more complicated than necessary. However, she was funny which helped me not zone out in lecture sometimes. A lot of homework that is harder than necessary along with poorly written test questions.

Before taking that course I'd read on RMP that she made tons of mistakes when teaching;this is VERY TRUE. Every single lectures and every single examples she was making a mistake and followed it by "Oh, I made a mistake guys can you tell where" like no I can't I'm still in the learning process..? Class is an easy PASS though bcs of the grade scale.

Professor Curtis was an extremely difficult professor. Her lectures were not engaging and she made so many mistakes always asking students "Could someone point out where I went wrong?". How are we supposed to be able to point out your mistake when this is our first time learning it. Additionally her lectures were barely useful for the hard tests.

decent prof/lecturer. she did make mistakes pretty frequently but most were caught by students and corrected, so i thought it was fine. the class was not too hard in my opinion, but i did take and understood ap physics 1 previously, which was basically the same as 2211. curtis obviously isnt as good as alicea, but she's still ok to take imo

She was okay as far. Her lectures were often harder to follow, and she explained concepts in a way that wasn't always productive. There are definitely worse physics 1 professors, but if you can get Alicea that would be the best. Overall, the class wasn't too bad, the labs/bucket points help with grades, but the tests are very difficult.

analysis.name: David Rodin
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Best thermo proof at Tech. Does not make the class any harder than it has to be. All of the practice material is exactly like the exams so if you do all of it you will be all good. Super great guy he makes what could be an evil class so doable!!

One of the best professors I have had. Very accessible outside of class and lectures were engaging. Weekly homework. The grading scheme is very test heavy but he does give extra credit. Test are not very difficult if you do the practice tests.

The GOAT! Amazing, thorough, and incredibly helpful lectures. Super understanding guy. Tests are worth a lot of your grade, but they're incredibly fair, and if you do all the homework every week with fidelity and do the practice exam, you'll be set for an A. Overall, if you put in consistent but reasonable effort every week, you'll do very well.

He was great at adapting to the class and actually teaching the material. Very lenient and understanding in general. He was also effective at guiding his students through this coursework. The best professor someone can take thermo from.

analysis.name: Dan Kotlyar
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Hands down the best professor I have ever had. He provides all lectures as printed, fillable pamphlets and is a very good lecturer. Homework follows lecture content and is harder than exams. Grading is done quickly and very fairly. I always wanted to go to lecture because he was very funny.

Absolutely named Dan GOATlyar, one of the best professors I have had. I would definitely take another course with him. All notes were very structured and the homework was challenging, but followed them closely and he was easily accessible for questions or office hours.

The class is hard and daunting and its easy to get lost, but: Homework is very representative of the lectures, lecture notes are clear and concise, and Kotlyar is genuinely interested in what he's teaching and is good at it. You will need to stay focused in class, but he's generous in grading and his tests are the most fair I've seen at Tech.

Had Dr. Kotlyar for NRE 4210. He is easily my favorite professor in the NRE department. He is able to clearly explain complex subjects with ease, and his lectures are full of useful diagrams and equations to support the theory. He made the class a bit too easy this semester, but it was still incredibly informative. GT is lucky to have Dr. Kotlyar.
He makes the otherwise difficult material easier to understand. He's humorous and a genuinely good lecturer.

analysis.name: Rachel Dean-Ruzicka
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Dean has been a very pleasant professor to have! Accepts late work and is not a harsh grader/most grades are completion. Very friendly and makes it easy to participate and do the assignments without feeling forced to. She won't be like those English professors that are always looking for a specific answer.

I took Professor Dean blindly. She has a very interesting topics (Monsters), and she has a labor based grading system. She made attendance guidlines easier later in the sem so attendance is not too bad. She gives good feedback, and lets you redo assignments and projects. She is very understanding and helpful. Would def reccomend this English class.

She was very caring and sympathetic towards the fact that many students at a tech school don't care about English. The topic for my 1102 course was very interesting and our assignments were not just standard essays. Every assignment was graded on completion (as long as you met all the requirements) aside from reading checks.

As long as you do your work and put in a decent amount of effort, you will get a 100 in this class. She is a very easy grader and she gives excellent feedback. She also really puts an emphasis on creating an inclusive and welcoming space for all students. 10/10 would recommend her!!!

While she didn't lecture much, she was quite friendly and made herself accessible. The assignments do take a little while to complete, but grading is practically for completion, and she gives incredibly clear feedback on how to improve your projects.

analysis.name: Daniel Spieler
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 53 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He is a nice guy, but, he is one of the worst professors I have had at Tech. He is not very good at explaining concepts, which is needed in a stats class. Tests are extremely difficult, so don't be surprised if you fail them. He does curve the class though to compensate (I got a B). Go to class...even if it feels pointless. Good luck...trust me!

I didn't go to lecture because he would talk about nonsense instead of explaining anything. He gave 8 random quizzes. Lab was terrible, always took 3 hours. Homeworks were difficult, don't wait until last minute on those. I failed both exams, although we got 3 crib sheets for the exams. The grading was very harsh, but there is a curve.

The professor gives you a topic list to study off for midterms and finals, but questions are very confusing for an intro class. Some questions are too specific and frq grading is pretty strict. No clear guidelines for the frq. Lectures had a lot of unnecessary information and the professor often rambled a lot which can be confusing. $100 textbook.

Prof Spieler is a kind person but psych1101 was very frustrating. Test formats were unclear, I did horrible on the first midterm because the FRQ was difficult to understand. Lectures were easy to understand but I ended up just learning everything outside of the class on my own. TAs did not know what was happening in the class and were unhelpful.

FIND A DIFFERENT PROFESSOR OR DONT TAKE THE CLASS. Seriously it's not worth it. Made psych way to diffuclt for what it is. I was so jealous of my friends who were telling me they had take home online tests while I was working my butt of for a literal 70 on the first midterm. This is an intro class, should not be that hard. Bro deserves more 1 stars

analysis.name: Denis Tsygankov
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Where do I even begin with Denis... he's just been an amazing professor each time I have had him. He's nice and understanding and is by far one of the most human and enjoyable professors in the BMED department. If I ever see a course being taught by this man, I'm snagging it as fast as I can!

The lectures are okay. The PSS sessions are the most helpful and generally indicate what will be on the test or quiz.

He leans heavily on prior knowledge, especially from statics. He will teach you the problem solving methods which are straightforward, but get harder through the semester, and he expects a lot of self learning.

"No hope" is the advice he gave for studying for one of our exams. I really liked his lecturing style, he was very funny.

Be prepared to see things on exams you haven't seen before is my only warning.

Great Professor! The real gem comes during PSS where his humor, talent, & knowledge shines. Makes PSS fun to attend and also allows you to learn a lot during class through focusing on problem solving. Biomechanics is primarily graded by (2 tests + final) which are 25% each, so watch out for them and DO THE HOMEWORK without looking at the answer key

Denis is one of my favorite professors I've had. He's funny, lighthearted, and wants you to succeed. "I want to give you all A's- you just have to help me out a little" - Denis. The class is math and computer science heavy. Recitation sections were set up as group activities that was similar to homework and exam questions.

analysis.name: Christie  Debelius
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
Dr. Debelius is AMAZING! end of review. 

She's really caring about students, understanding, funny, and gives you extra time on assignments + chances to redo. Just make sure you manage your time and not take advantage of her extensions. Her class is such an easy A because she makes it engaging during class time w/ minimal homework. She's great!

Dr. Debelius is such a caring, understanding professor, and you can tell how much she wants us to succeed. Our unit was Romanticism, and I genuinely enjoyed doing the projects that we had. She is very lenient with grading and late assignments. The assigned reading can be a bit of work, but the pieces are genuinely interesting. Highly Recommend!

Dr. Debelius is a really great prof. The class has 3 main "Artifacts," and she uses specifications based grading. They're different multimedia projects and honestly aren't too much work, as she guides you through them and allows for revisions. Show up to class and do your work, but do be prepared to read quite a bit every night.

Dr. D is not only a great professor, but a great person in general. It's clear that she wants her students to succeed - but not to the point where she lets you get away without doing any work. The course is designed in a way that if you put in proper effort, you are guaranteed to get the result you want.

Dr. Debelius is a very caring and understanding professor, especially with deadlines and if you have other things going on in life. The projects weren't super heavy and she gives plenty of in class time to work on the larger ones. Also gives detailed and concrete feedback on assignments.

analysis.name: Shijie Deng
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Deng is very accomplished in quant finance, but the teaching in this course did not match its importance as a core QCF requirement. Lectures were often theory-heavy and lacked clear explanation in application. Most learning required heavy self-study. I hope the course format can be improved in the future.

Arguably one of the most important courses in the QCF program, but it's horribly taught by Deng. He spends most of class talking through the slides on theory/proofs and then glosses over real applications. Quizzes and tests are very hard.

My biggest gripe were the homeworks. I was a math undergrad but the amount of effort expected for biweekly homeworks was ridiculous. The homework questions often covered material completely unrelated to anything presentend in lecture! And of course the homework averages are really high because I'm sure everyone is cheating on the homeworks.

While the concepts covered were quite extensive his learning style is heavily theory based and he mostly just reads from the slides. The exams are twice as hard as the homework and ask you to apply theory to the most convoluted examples. He does care about the topics though so if you are interested he's a great resource
Overall solid professor, with good lectures. Tests are difficult but fair for a graduate course.

analysis.name: Denis Dorozhkin
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 94 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: No tests, 2 easy pop quizzes.  Attendance is 100% mandatory.  I took him his first semester here for 1770.  He has a thick Russian accent but I never have trouble understanding him.  Lots of work, but that's the nature of the course.  Pick simpler topics for projects and pray to God that your group isn't bad.  Would take again.

Chill prof and very useful class. I learned almost everything through the VERY LONG hw and lab assignments, not his boring lectures. Assignments graded quite harshly, taking off for little things. Should be an easy A if you do your work with decent effort. Oh also he'll call you out in front of the class if you're late or on your phone or whatever.

There are many benefits of taking Professor Dorozhkin compared to others (access to the best project materials, has free voucher codes for ~$100 SolidWorks test certificates, more flexible for deadlines/requirements, etc.). However, his fast-paced and somewhat monotone nature made some of the important, dull topics less engaging than they could be.

Insanely funny and chill guy, he makes some of the most annoying parts of this class fun. Workload is a lot. The TAs are nasty graders and will take off lots of points for small things. The team and individual projects are massive time sinks. But he gives you enough resources to succeed and makes lectures fun. Take him if you can.

He is an awesome and very understanding professor. He makes his assignments very doable, although some might take longer than others. If he saw that few students had turned in a homework he usually gave an extension to all his sections, which was very nice, especially during exam heavy weeks. Can't recommend him enough!

analysis.name: Sourish Dhekane
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I enjoyed this class and prof. I think the class is pretty standardized, because the homeworks are from UC Berkley's AI class, but they are interesting and helpful; they're also all autograded and you can submit as many times as you want. There's two midterms and some interviews, which aren't that bad, and you get good feedback from the interviews.

This was an easy course because the prof explained everything in detail. Course is graded by homework, tests and interviews which take time, but are easy using lectures and textbook. Making an A is relatively easy because of all the extra credit opportunities provided. He's very quick to respond to emails and answer questions. Highly recommended.

Really nice professor who clearly has a passion for teaching! The class was difficult but not unnecessarily so. It's hard to understand anything without going to lecture because the slides are not good, so I usually read the book. There are 2 exams which are super tedious for no reason, but they are take-home and you get a week to complete them.

analysis.name: Lucien Dhooge
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This guy is AMAZING. He makes every class interesting and cares about his students. Honestly one of the best professors I've EVER had. He likes to tell lots of anecdotes, and if you understand the basic concepts he teaches, the tests are common sense. The only downside is that each test is 1/3 of your grade, no participation or extra credit points.

Great teacher, had great examples for lectures and made coming to class very enjoyable! The best teacher to teach law, very nice and funny. The exams are online through canvas, and quizzes online through textbook! Would take again and highly recommend.

I took TBGEN 218 with him at UWT. He knows what he's talking about in class and is very engaging and makes the class interesting. You do need to show up to class to get the extra 14 max points. Doesn't really help you with tests/quizzes if you email but will answer in class and help you out. About 10 quizzes and 3 exams all online at home.

Professor Dhooge is by far and away one of the best professors at Scheller. There are only 3 test so yes each is high stakes but if you read your notes and pay attention in lecture no reason you cannot earn a high A. He tells funny stories. Lecture can get boring during certain subjects but he keeps it interesting for the most part.
I loved Professor Dhooge! He made lectures engaging and interesting. Although the tests are challenging, if you pay attention during class, you should be fine to get an A.

analysis.name: Changxin Ding
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Very easy to get full credit on homework and participation. His lectures were not very good at all, but I think if you went and tried to pay attention you could understand everything you need to. I would not take him if you care about learning proofs, but I would say it is an easy A.

Class was incredibly easy as if you just showed up you basically needed a 40 on the final to get an A. Biggest issue was his accent but otherwise his lectures were not as bad as people say. If you're a math major and complaining about the difficulty of this class or "how tough the grading was." Yeah these are proofs. You need to find a new major.

He had weekly presentation for proofs which was kinda odd. The class did a point system where you can earn 20 points for hw, 50 for presentations and 50 on the final, so 120 points total, standard cut off. He is super strict and doesn't understand english well, takes points off for saying things in way he doesn't understand,  also very dismissive
Avoid at all cost, exam is too hard to complete on time, and final exam contains all the previous content, which is hard to review all of them.
do not take. laughs at students proofs and is rude, and expects you to know everything.

analysis.name: Weiming Ding
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This professor is genuinely funny, and I really enjoy visiting his office hours—we always end up talking about our favorite video games. He's incredibly kind, and after every exam he reassures me that partial credit will be given, which is always comforting. The class itself is very straightforward as long as you attend PLUS sessions and studios.

Every calc 2 class takes the same exact exam, so the only difference between each class is who you take it with. Dr Ding is a very nice person but it is difficult to learn from his lectures. It's significantly easier to learn from Dr. Grodzinsky's lecture videos on canvas then go to class. 
Grade breakdown 
15% homework 
2% extra credit
85% exams

He's honestly a very caring person, but has a horrible teaching method. He has a habit of not thoroughly explaining the example problems and showing the full steps, just reads off the slides, and when asked a question, he doesn't explain it fully.

You're better off just attending another professor's lectures. My grades improved after doing that.

His teaching was horrible. I don't know if it's because he's new to teaching but he basically reads off slides only; literally shows us what's on there and that's it with almost no explanations. Learned the entire course on Youtube with "Professor V" instead and used old exams as practices, got away with a solid B in the course

Stopped going to lecture because he just read off of the slides that were posted anyways. He sped through class because he would skip things or not explain. He was nice if he understood what you were talking about. Has an accent but it's not impossible to understand.

analysis.name: Dingjing Shi
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Only 2/3 tests count, including the final. Really clear and slow lecturer that goes over how inference tests conceptually work. She uses a random generator for attendance taking, so its a 50/50 that she'll take attendance on any given day. The lab component is also very easy and doesn't require attendance at all.

She is an incredibly thoughtful professor who is aware that most people have to take it because it's required, brings a warm and positive energy to the class that is very refreshing. Tests are very fair and don't try and trick you with questions and are accurate to how you understand the material
Very thorough explanation and makes difficult concepts unbelievably easy to understand! Super sweet professor too.

analysis.name: Stephen Diggle
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: LOVED Diggle! Lectures were super entertaining, but definitely talked a lot about research along with content being presented. Grade was based on 3 tests with the final being 50%, but they were take home! TA's were awesome as well. Highly recommend for BIOS 3380!

He was nice and you can tell he cared about the content but I also think he was kind of immature because he was upset people didn't come to the lecture that he made: non-mandatory, unrelated to the exam content, and was pretty boring.
So then the format and difficulty of the exams changed a lot over the course of the semester I feel like to punish.

Dr. Diggle was okay. Our grade was completely based off of 2 exams and the final, but they were all take home. This was his first time teaching the class. The exams got exponentially more difficult (the final was 4 essays in the span of 2 weeks- horrible). Lectures were interesting but not helpful. Okayish class but I didn't learn much.

very kind and funny professor, but the grading was a bit wonky for the course. he didn't really have a rubric and graded based on how much others included in there answer - most information = highest grade. you have to read journal articles and give a review on them in class and he definitely likes to add his opinions.

I could not recommend Dr. Diggle enough! This course was very engaging and unlike any other course I've taken at Tech. He brought in guest lecturers to give great exposure into fields and split his class time between lectures and journal club presentations. Amazing professor, amazing course, if you're interested in infectious diseases, TAKE THIS !!

analysis.name: Benjamin Diden
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I really like BJ :) He's very caring and accepting of instrumentalists of all levels. If you did band in high school and are interested in continuing, this class was a good way for me to relieve some stress during difficult weeks. Would highly recommend

Love this man he's just so nice and accommodating. He knows my name somehow even though I sit in the back row and don't march. He treats everyone with respect. Music can be easy at times but as an engineering major I don't have much time to practice anyway so it doesn't really bother me. Take for an easy humanities if you play an instrument!
Great guy and great class. Would 100% recommend taking band at Georgia Tech too

If you're thinking about taking band, definitely do! I was on the fence about joining since I'm more used to playing in an orchestra, but I'm so glad I did. He's an incredibly fun and chill guy who makes rehearsals an awesome break from school. The repertoire we play is super cool and just challenging enough to be fun for every instrument.
Wonderful band director! Will definitely be doing band as much as I can!

analysis.name: Dimitri Mavris
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Fun, good times. Lots of material and an intense workload, so be wary if you don't have an AE background.

His class was not very helpful to say the least. Classes were awful. 3+ hours of lecturing and most of the time it wasn't even about content. Took class time to explain how he knows so many famous people yet he has been at the same place for 40+ years teaching.

Dr. Mavris spent lots of time into preparing this course. He structured it so students from many different backgrounds get up to speed with aeronautical engineering topics. It's very challenging as multiple courses are condensed into a single class (that's what makes aircraft design challenging). Nonetheless, it's an amazing learning opportunity.

The set of classes ASDL students take with Doc (Dr. Mavris' nickname) are insanely difficult, but they will make you a better engineer and a better thinker for sure. We call it the bootcamp for a reason. It will be grueling, but if you can brave through the challenge, you will be quite literally "build different" from other engineers

Course material is relevant to the subject. Volume of material is absurd and needs to be parsed into 2 courses. Tests do not effectively measure student's grasp of concepts, ie deductions for not using certain terms regardless if answer correctly addresses question. If you don't need the course, don't bother.

analysis.name: Dina Khapaeva
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Took ML 2500 in Spring 2025 and it was a phenomenal class. She is extremely well knowledged in the topic and a fantastic lecturer. No exams but instead your grade is determined by two presentations and two essays. While the essays are long, she is a generous grader and you have freedom in your writing. Great professor and would strongly recommend!

Dina is very passionate, caring, and warm. I truly appreciated her as a professor, and I hope that I will be able to have her again. Though sometimes the courses focused more on discussion than on the grammar I wanted, she always made herself available for extra help, demonstrated that she truly cared about her students, and taught me how to write!

Slightly disorganized and confused. However, she is very very intelligent and her knowledge of culture and language is immense. Her class is unconventional, but if you show her that you care about the material, the grades come easy. She's not the usual disgusting narcissist that many of the other professors are here, but will take some flexibility.

Professor Khapaeva is incredibly knowledgeable when it comes to Russian culture, film, and literature. Her lectures can seem a bit long and repetitive, but the participation portion of the class keeps it engaging. Be prepared for paper writing- these will determine your grade. She gives good feedback and grades on the nicer side.

I'm a physics major, but I took the class because I thought a "history of fiction" class would be interesting, however it wasn't what I expected. It seemed that she didn't have any sort of direction when teaching. None of the material was connected in anyway. Other than two simple tests we had a 10 page final paper.

analysis.name: Sean Dolan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Spring 2025. Nice guy and you can tell he is intelligent and well-learned. One time he grilled each of us individually in front of the entire class about our podcast projects and maybe I'm too sensitive but I almost started crying it was so bad. I'm sure he didn't mean to be harsh and he did let up when he could tell I was panicking.

He was definitely well informed on the topics of the in class discussions, and he is also very helpful when you ask him for ideas on structuring your assignments. There is almost no way to get a bad grade as long as you complete your assignment on time.

You can tell this professor really knew what he was teaching and he really seemed to care about what was taught. Though he tends to go on a ramble once in a while, he makes it clear what to complete and how to complete it. He's super flexible with deadlines (and gave us a rewrite) and as long as you try you will get an A on every single assignment.

Wonderful guy. He deeply cares about what he teaches and it is so evident. The topic was Ethnography, so it was a little hard to grasp at first, but interesting.  There is sometimes a lot of work but you will get an A if you put in effort. I loved taking Dr.Dolan's class. Only complaint is that he doesnt grade in a timely manner.

Was not a terrible class, grading was easy, but he left pretty much all of the assignments to be graded in the last 2 weeks of the semester. There's a lot of writing in the course, but it comes in bursts - half the time you have no HW, and the other half you have a lot of work to do in order to complete before any of the large projects are due.

analysis.name: Donggang Yao
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof Yao is very kind and funny. He was easy to meet with and explained things well in a 1-1 setting. He has a little bit of an accent so his lectures were difficult for me to follow along with but his notes and slides outweighed this! I should have gotten an A in this class but honestly I was just being a slacker, would totally recommend!

Very funny, caring and respectful of students, was accessible outside of class and would extend deadlines if needed all to accommodate needs he saw. Dr. Yao is passionate about statics and made it interesting, he's also good at teaching the concepts. Not an easy class and exams could be tough but well taught and expectations outlined well.

(MSE6600) Honestly he is a very enjoyable teacher and is very easy to talk to. I went in knowing absolutely nothing and feel like he's very accomodating and helpful. Homework is difficult but he makes sure you understand all you need during class. Would recommend

Lectures may seem slow, but he gets through class material on pace, so it's probably just the nature of statics. Makes jokes during lecture that make him seem like a dad/uncle. Clearly values students time, and he extended all of our homeworks if we asked. Pretty much tells you what will be on exams and how to prepare

he definitely can be hard to follow and understand and you will be teaching yourself a lot BUT he really cares about the students (often extends the homework), he is super passionate about the class, and is so open to helping however he can. The tests are harder than the practice tests though so do study.

analysis.name: Simone Douglas-Green
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Douglas-Green gave extremely detailed feedback for all assignments. Her feedback is helpful for getting better grades in the future if you take into account what feedback she gave and revised accordingly. The BMED 1000 course layout is not fun and can be confusing, so determine your due dates at the beginning of the semester.

It was clear that Dr. Douglas-Green was inexperienced as a guide and professor. While she was interested in your success, her guidance was uninformed. BMED 2250 is an easy A, but you're better off with another facilitator. I don't feel like I am a better scientist for having taken this class, and that was evident in the group presentations.
Dr. Douglas-Green is a very kind and enthusiastic professor. She gives very constructive feedback on assignments and she seems like she really wants you to do well.
BMED 1000 is a pretty annoying class so not Professor Douglas-Green's fault. Make sure to pay attention to due dates and citations in this class.
Thank you Simone Douglas-Green for helping me understand the material. I wish you the best in life. Students, you will enjoy her class.

analysis.name: Donald White
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Flipped classroom, and the online lectures are boring. Tbh I watched the goat Jeff Hanson's lecs on youtube, way shorter and still learned everything needed for class problems. Super lenient grader, just wants you to succeed so as long as you can make yourself watch the vids you'll be good. Only downside is paying for the course but so worth it.

Could genuinely tell he cared about us students. Broke the material down well but class was designated practice time. Lectures were videos we had to watch on our own time so if that's not your thing beware.

Dr. White's class is tough, but doing the homework, watching the videos, and going to class makes all the difference. His class is flipped, which really helped me to understand the types of questions that would be asked an how to do them. His office hours are amazing. He will sit down with you and walk you through the homework until you understand.

Dr white is insanely intelligent but sometimes it makes it hard to understand what he is teaching or saying because he is so smart. His assignments are super long and he's a tough grader. His exams are also super hard and impossible to finish but he curves. He expects a lot but is super nice. Just be mentally prepared lol

Professor White really wants you to succeed in his class. The whole course is curved so that an 85 is an A, 75 is a B and so on. He also has one test drop so a lot of students did not have to take the final. All of his lectures were posted online and then in class he would work through practice problems.

analysis.name: Dianne Leader
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 113 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Tests are worth 75% of our grade, and there are 3 tests that count, so be mindful of that. I found that lectures were so boring that I couldn't even fall asleep if I tried. She genuinely cares about the subject matter that she's teaching, and is knowledgeable, but she fails to pass this passion on to her students.

Lectures consisted of slideshows. Each test is 25% of your grade, but you have 4 (including the final) so the lowest doesn't count. The tests seemed harder than the material we learned in class. Dr. Leader is a very sweet lady, but I struggled a lot with this class despite it being an introductory course.

I got a 95% in this class, and I received a B for my final grade, if that tells you anything. Dr. Leader is incompetent with technology. If you can't use technology, just use Canvas and PowerPoint, and have TAs calculate final grades. But Dr. Leader does not do that, and it caused repeated issues this semester that significantly penalized students.

If you have the option, I strongly recommend NOT taking her class. She rarely responds to emails. Her exams are extremely detailed, covering material that was not addressed in lectures. I was excited to take this course because of my interest in psychological disorders, but that enthusiasm was quickly diminished by the way the class was taught.

Super chill professor, but she definitely expected way to much out of us for an "Introduction to Psychology" (and made me HATE psychology if anything). Spent 20+ hours studying for each exam (which is crazy) despite being attentive; also exam questions had lots of ambiguity, and she shot down any exam contesting. Lectures were boring asf too.

analysis.name: Donald Webster
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Great guy. Honestly, pretty straightforward class. You get a crib sheet for every test, which you honestly don't even need. The tests are very similar to the problems we go over in class and to the practice tests he gives you. Just go to class and spend a fair amount of time studying, and you should have no problem getting an A in his class.

Flipped class. In class we would go over an example and work on worksheets in small groups. Practice a lot. Weekly hw, 3 midterms, final. Takes attendance. Prof is great at explaining the material and genuinely cares about students succeeding.

Dr. Webster has to be one of the kindest professors at Tech. His class was set up well where you would watch the notes online before class when there were notes, and you would spend the entire class doing practice problems. Dr. Webster did an excellent job doing a problem on the board every class, and he was very helpful if you had any questions.

Extremely helpful in office hours (attend them!) and insanely knowledgable. He made the class very straightforward. Don't underestimate exams though- the partial credit was not generous. Do the in class problems, and if you don't get to them in class make sure you go over them on your own time the same week. Allot plenty of time to study for tests

Dr Webster is an amazing professor. He is always available for answers despite the fact that he is a chair and is fairly busy all the time. Class format also helps you study and understand the material better. Lectures, homework, solution, past exams.. etc are on t-square.  Tests are straightforward. He grades fairly with plenty of partial credits.

analysis.name: Doug Yoder
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: 2 Hr 8AM is hard enough already, but he speaks softly and gets too into the math that doesnt help understanding. Textbook is best. exam prep was a practice exam that didnt match actual; no key provided. Recitations are only good option for review. Exams are hard, with recently improved grading. Not a bad person, but his teaching didn't work for me.

Yoder absolutely cares about his students and goes out of his way to help them, either through (relatively free) bonus points on exams or granting homework extensions. Very receptive to feedback from students. Super talent lecturer and I recommend going to class even if its at 8am, you'd benefit a lot. Exams were super doable if you put in effort.

He is the absolute worst prof I've taken. Crib sheets are allowed but don't help much since he only allows formulas, no labels, no notes, no diagrams, and NO UNITS. His lectures are fairly good I guess, but they cover material beyond the textbook, and he does not cover all the textbook material you need to know, which balloons the material so much.

Dr Yoder purposely makes any class he teaches more difficult than it needs to be. He asks for feedback and then ignores genuine advice when you give it, only responding when you give him compliments. There are many students who take his class 3 or 4 times, and they under stand the material, but Yoder's exams always get them.

Genuinely cares about students. Replies fast to email and piazza.  Grades on understanding, so math errors don't count much off.  But then exam problems sometimes have a nuance or twist.  So you have to learn for a good grade.  Lectures helped me with the textbooks.

analysis.name: Lynn Dombrowski
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Ah, Professor Dombrowski, what a delight. First-time teaching and it shows—vague instructions, harsh grading, unrelated readings, and stellar irony (she reads slides while telling us not to). Communication skills? Top-notch, if making students cry counts. Would love to avoid this class, but it's required for MS-HCI. Lucky us, right?
She tries to teach a liberal arts class at a tech school. It's not working. Wouldn't recommend!
I dislike her teaching for pedagogical reasons. Iykyk

analysis.name: Andrew Scherbakov
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Super funny and always made me want to learn more. Convinced some of my non-physics major friends to take this class because I truly believe it's better than regular physics and you'll have a much better time. Only bad thing is how long the labs and lab reports were but still deserves a 5/5 nonetheless!

Dr. Sherbakov is an amazing teacher who does a great job of making the content simple and easy to understand. The tests are similar to the reviews that he gives before the exam, but the homework is quite difficult at times, so beware of that. That being said, fantastic class!

The best lecturer I've had, made me much more interested in physics after taking his class as a non-physics major. Difficult course, but grading is pretty lenient with open book exams and lots of extra credit.

My absolute physics GOAT. Fantastic lectures, tedious but interesting labs, and just great overall. You don't have to read the textbook, but it definitely helps on homeworks and exams. If he is an option for any physics class, TAKE HIM. You won't regret it one bit. Truly the best.

Clearly passionate about teaching the class; even though I took algebra based physics 2 in high school, I still went to every lecture for him. Assigns some pretty difficult homework every week, but the answer key can be found online. Exams are exactly like the practice problems he does in class, so you should be well prepared for each of them.

analysis.name: Andrew Hummel
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Pretty good lecturer in a class that could use some better structure. Most lectures were easy to follow with helpful examples. Homeworks were fair and graded very leniently. Some exam questions were hard to understand and work with, but were graded fairly. Would reccomend!

Dr. Hummel is a fantastic professor who really seems to care and be passionate about teaching ME heat transfer. He connects a lot of the course to his NRE experience which I liked because it makes the class less abstract and more applicable. Fair grader, but it's heat transfer so its just a tough course by nature, wouldn't take it with anyone else

Had Dr. Hummel for NRE 4214, and he did a decent job teaching the content. He is a bit disorganized, and seemingly randomly hand-waived a lot of theory sometimes while diving deep at others. He may not understand theory as well as he should, but he is funny and cares about his students, and he will respond to emails timely. Very lenient grader.

Dr. Hummel is a newer professor, and is still figuring out the best way to lecture to and test his students. Tests were kinda unpredictable, but he's a very good professor, and he's really funny. Give him another year or two to figure out his teaching style and I think he'll be one of the best heat transfer professors at Tech. I def recommend him.

Dr. Hummel was not the best professor I have had at Tech. I feel like with better lecture organization, test structure, and accessibility outside of class my experience would have been A LOT better. The content was presented in a nonchalant manner that sometimes made it hard to follow. He was a nice guy and even funny, but not the best

analysis.name: Andrew Nance
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Made the most difficult artifact (group podcast) the first one in the semester so you're kind of thrown into everything, but that means the semester gets easier as you continue. Dr. Nance is clearly very interested in the class and is always excited to talk more about topics we research for the course.

This professor is a D1 yapper and he would always overexplain a topic which made some things, like homework unclear. He's also very by the book when it comes to giving people grades. You have to follow the assignment requirements down to a T to get a perfect score. He does give extensions on assignments if you talk to him though.
This professor is amazing. I had him for 1102 over the summer and I learned a lot in his class and had fun with the projects he assigned us. Definitely take him if you have the opportunity.
Total Karen. Not serious. Probably reads on weekends and grades like it

analysis.name: Dragomir Davidovic
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Davidovic has a good sense of humor, and is better at lecturing than many of the other E&M professors. However, he is very disorganized, forgets to assign homework, and goes extremely slowly through the course content. Our final was on 2 chapters, as this was all we sufficiently covered. Good lecturer, bad administrator, fun experience.

Overall, Professor Davidovic is one of the best professors in the physics department. Electrodynamics is a difficult class, but he is more than willing to take his time to explain difficult concepts. He also has a great sense of humor. I would recommend taking.

Davidovic is constantly unprepared for his lectures and makes many mistakes which end up taking time, assuming he doesnt give up and ask you to figure it out on your own. Ive no doubt he has a good handle on the material he teaches but he can not express it to others well. Thankfully, he followed the book exactly, and the book was written well.

I took this class in Fall 2022, and his tests were take home. However, the tests were SUPER long/hard so I would spend 8+ hours on each one. I think he said he is not doing online tests anymore. We were supposed to cover 6 chapters but we only got to 3 because he went really slow. He lectures straight from the textbook, so no need to go to class.

Professor Davidovic is one of the most caring compassionate professors I have ever had. He's extremely careful to make sure students feel comfortable in his class and extremely flexible when extenuating circumstances arise. He also usually responds to emails within minutes or seconds of being sent. Lectures and tests are reasonable, good textbook

analysis.name: Andrew Zangwill
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Zangwill is a boring lecturer and enjoys criticizing the GT-issued textbook and teaching things "the textbook doesn't bother to mention" about physics (even though they probably won't show up on the test). In my opinion he didn't explain anything in lecture in a way that was useful on the tests.

Dr.Z is an excellent professor and lecturer, the problem with his classes and why people don't excel is because his test aren't exams on the knowledge you would learn from the resources given to you. The homework, class notes, and book will not help you on his test even with it being open book. His test are based on intuition on what's in his head.

Dr. Z is the worse professor I have ever taken. He gives no partial credit on test, even for simple adding/subtracting errors. If you like going to class, memorizing what's written on the board, and blindly regurgitating it onto a test then this is the class for you. He is very rude if you go to his office. Also, he doesn't know math notation.

He goes into a lot of theoretical rigor and if you take the time to actually do his derivations/calculations by hand (especially in your own time), you will be beyond prepared for the exams. If you have questions go to his office hours he's pretty chill and will take time to explain. His slides are different, and I think if used well, are better.
I've had professors before who were strict or maybe even a little unfair, but Professor Zangwill is the first professor I have ever had in my life who was genuinely mean.

analysis.name: Andrew Newman
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Some of these old reviews are pretty bad but his class is much easier now! Lectures are fast paced, but Dr. Newman is super nice and good at explaining things. Grading came from weekly quizzes (open note) and labs (my TA was super helpful), so overall, not very difficult. My class was for EAS majors so class structure may be different for others.

I took EAS 3610 - Intro to Geophysics. I really enjoyed this class. The lectures were really interesting and Dr Newman did a great job of explaining difficult concepts. The class only had a few homeworks and in-class labs. I highly recommend it.

Andy is a great guy who enjoys answering questions about anything you have. He is passionate about the material and does research related to the class. There were weekly quizzes (open notes), an optional final (open), and a ton of nice information to learn. As an atmosphere person, I didn't feel bored out of my mind, he is very easy to listen to.

Professor Newman is helpful when you ask for help and his notes make sense, but his tests come from out of nowhere. He asked the TA's to take the tests and my TA didn't turn his in because he was embarrassed. He will treat you like a grad student so if you want a breezy easy class, I don't suggest Professor Newman. There will likely be a curve.

Newman is an engaging lecturer, but this course covers a LOT of material. It is difficult to tell what he finds important, and some of the test questions come out of nowhere. If you like your grade after the first 3 exams, you can skip the final. Go to class! He gives pop quizzes that go toward extra credit, and it is why I could skip the final.

analysis.name: Alex Draper
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: The reason I put that attendance is not mandatory is because he doesn't teach during lecture time. All responsibly to learn coursework falls on the student and Dr. Draper is mostly uninterested, unenthusiastic, and often unprepared to answer questions when in class. Tests are unpredictable. Intro class should not have been this difficult.

Honestly, his class was ok but it could've been a lot better if he only made it possible to gain extra credit and be completely clear on how grades are managed. You have to come to class and you need to stay on top of your work. Also, please ask as many questions that you need to and you should be ok. However, personally I wouldn't take him again.

Dr Alex Drapper is one terrible professor, he needs to be removed from the school. He lacks teaching skills and overall overload the exams with topics other than what we actually study for. He has very little consideration. Don't take him and save yourself and your GPA.

Dr. Draper doesn't teach - plain and simple. He expects you to learn on your own through the online textbook rather than during his class, and I think that throws a lot of people off since it is just an intro class. Study the textbook and TICA's THOROUGHLY - dit's entirely possible to get an A if you do that.

He thinks group work is more important than lectures. Many people failed his class. They worked very hard. I worked very very hard to pass a class because of his exam structure and his lack of teaching. 

He doesn't teach during class. He assigns too much work. His exams are structured poorly. He grades slowly.

analysis.name: Dun Tang

This class is a joke because you don't need to understand why anything works and you can still do amazing. Tests are easy with extra credit as well and studio quizzes are beyond free

Seems genuine guy but wouldn't reccomend

analysis.name: Kelly Duquette
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: If you have to take an 8am English class, please pick this one. Dr. Williams' class is not an easy one (by common definitions of the word), but if you put in the effort you will succeed in this course. Btw she also responds to emails pretty quickly and makes efforts to help students the best she can!

Can't get any better than Dr. Duquette. She was simply amazing for 1102. Even though our lectures were bright and early, I was always excited to go to class. She is extremely caring and accessible outside of class if you have any questions. The projects were mainly group-based and fun to work on. I HIGHLY suggest taking Dr. Duquette, even at 8 am.

Goat. Everything is clearly laid out and she deeply cares about each student's well-being. It's an appropriate level of work (perfect difficulty) and is interesting. Grades easy. Extremely helpful and relevant feedback. Brings treats for students' birthdays. Incorporates input from students. No flaws. Wish I could take her for all my classes.

This class overall was easy, and Dr. Williams is nice and understanding when you ask her about assignments or need help. The assignments were slightly more work than I expected to spend time on, but overall would say this is a fantastic teacher.

I think this English section is a little more difficult that others. She grades somewhat harshly, with averages for the Artifacts being around a 90. She learns everyones name though and always makes a welcoming environment in class.

analysis.name: Michael Dutcher
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: super sweet and funny guy! really caring and personable. only gripe is the attendance policy (u will fail the class is u miss 2+ classes) but that's generalized to the class so. class itself was not very helpful if im being honest, but it's only 50 min/week. hes super accessible outside of class and will give u sm chances to makeup absences tho!
this class actually helped me get my 1st internship. he cares a lot and is willing to help at anytime. super awesome and grades lightly.

Super useful class if you're looking for an internship, a lot less so if you already have one. But Dutcher is still a great professor, and the homework isn't that difficult. Like someone else said, it's heavier at the beginning of the semester and gets easier, but it all feels a bit inconvenient for just one credit hour.

Class had no organization or structure- just a final project at the end with no rubric or grading guidelines given. I learned nothing, and received a b despite contributing to the project and attending most lectures.

I found Mr. Dutcher to be incredibly kind and knowledgeable. His best quality is his honesty when it comes to your career field, career ideations, and yourself as a person. The homework is heavy for the first half of the semester but is really light the second half. It's also all really good homework and actually relevant to your life.

analysis.name: Suchismita Dutta
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Dutta is very sweet. You arent required to participate in discussions often but you are expected to read out loud if she calls on you. If you arent an amazing speaker and have troubles or anxieties when giving presentations, she is very understanding. She is also willing to round up your grade as long as you finish the flash writings on time.

A very participation heavy class. She makes you read out loud during class, and as someone with anxiety it was a horrible class to take. I also felt that reading the texts out loud during class was a waste of time when it was our assigned reading before class. If you have anxiety choose a different teacher. If not, you'll be fine I guess.

Was very flexible with deadlines and patient with students. Wanted you to participate and add to daily class discussions. Did often change her mind about criteria for assignments, which could be confusing but was a pretty easy grader. Had relatively low expectations for students. Seemed to genuinely care about students' well-being.

Dr. Dutta is fantastic and one of the best English teachers I've had. She is very accommodating and genuinely cares for her students. Her class was so interesting and I looked forward to going. Very discussion based, not much work outside of the few major assignments of the course. Take her class if you get the chance!

Very caring and understanding professor. I wasn't super interested in the topic at the beginning of the course but the assignments were interesting and engaging and I ended up enjoying the class. Did not take much time outside of class to complete major assignments.

analysis.name: Lane Duncan
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Lane Duncan is a sweet old man who does not teach the standard way. He gave us free reign and our class was very project based. We did some cool stuff in his class like nude figure drawing and sometimes he takes his class to piedmont park to draw.
Compared to other professors at Tech, he's at least completed a few actual construction projects; maybe a house every few years.
Really excellent. If you have a chance to take his watercoloring class, take it. It's a hard class, but he's a very good professor--excellent.

analysis.name: Eva Dyer
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
