6517 is a ML class for people who already know ML. We were told at the start of class that it was actually good to not have any ML experience and that if we did not know much python, we would pick it up quickly. Neither of those are the case. Currently 5 weeks in and completely lost, Dr. Dyer does a poor job explaining and moves too quickly.

The entire class seemed to be about writing fake journal articles. She does not provide prompt feedback - still waiting on a grade for something completed 10 weeks ago. If you want to be a writer, this may be the class for you but if you want to learn machine learning, avoid the prof if at all possible.

analysis.name: Edward Conrad
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: CHOOSE A DIFFERENT PROFESSOR! Truly one of the more awful physics classes I've ever had. He never actually taught in lecture. He just gave clicker questions on what you're supposed to learn reading the book. And the clicker questions count towards your grade. The only time I really learned in this class was when he left and another teacher taught.

This professor doesn't know how to communicate the lectures very well. He goes too fast with is powerpoints and it is hard to grasp the material in class. I only when to class because there were clicker questions. To succeed you need to know every word in the book. Tests were 5 questions, so if you miss two you fail.

His lectures are not the most helpful as far as the course goes. He often diverges from the textbook, which leads to pretty interesting lectures, but unfortunately not useful for tests. Tests are 5 questions, and they're straight from homework/book. Clickers are large part of grade, and they're often about what he's lecturing, not the book topics.

Too many people give this guy a bad rep. Truth is, I think it's hard to find a professor as fascinated by physics, and if approached after lecture this guy makes very interesting conversation. Yes, the tests are generally 5 questions multiple choice and one free response, but lots of them are quite common sense. Read book, do hw, you'll be fine.

I'd honestly avoid Conrad if at all possible. He doesn't really teach, but rather just gives clicker questions all class over material that you haven't actually learned in lecture, but are supposed to have learned through reading the book. He's not very helpful during office hours either because he doesn't know how to "dumb down" physics enough.

analysis.name: Edward Balog

Stopped going to his lectures half-way though the semester since they were confusing, over-complicated, and overall pretty useless. Survived by reading the textbook multiple times and going to another professor's lectures

The class is not easy?there is a lot of reading and writing. But you will definitely learn. I highly recommend his class if you are interested in the subject matter.

He's a pretty cool guy, gotta love the British accent. It's nothing but essays/papers. When you write the essays, and he says you are arguing a point, ARGUE a point. I got a mediocre grade on my first one because I did more commentary. Once I made that adjustment, I blew the other test essays and papers out of the water. Pretty easy B.

A lot of reading, but it isn't always necessary as long as you understand what he is talking about. Two papers in the class and the tests are all essays but he helps you out on those as well. Overall the class is really not that hard as far as college classes go.

Very interesting class.  Note:  Papers ONLY.  However, a STRICT and CONSERVATIVE word count is required, making the papers very challenging.  Also, there is quite alot to read, although it is not all necessary.  It does, however, help considerably.

Very difficult for an intro class. Chapters and chapters of reading out of the book as well as additional readings posted on WebCT were required. Only allows two absences for a MWF class. Nice guy but he talks a lot and is a tough grader.

analysis.name: Magnus Egerstedt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Egerstedt did an amazing job teaching Linear Controls. If there is anything called an "Ideal Professor", then Magnus is it. Each time he explains a concept, you feel like giving him a standing ovation. He is funny,charismatic & extremely intelligent. Taking ANY course under Magnus will be the best decision of your academic career. Also, his homework & exams are based on the lectures, so no sweat....

Pr. Egerstedt is the closest thing you can get to a perfect professor. His teaching style is unrivaled. The course is very structured and you don't need much prerequisites. The homeworks and tests are fair and can ace them if you study well. Too bad he is now chair of ECE and no longer has time to share his genius with the students.
Wonderful professor, he made me revisit concepts I already knew in an original way.

fun; appropriate homework (difficulty and quantity). Great lecture! Even I already knew almost all the materials before taking this course, I still find it fun. Plus, his insight give me a different view point on this subject.

Dr. Eichel is easily the best professor I've had. Everything about the class is engaging and interesting it's hard for me to give him lower than a 5.0.

He makes sure to assign works that are both educational and interesting, so the readings are very entertaining and the projects are fun to do. His lectures are very fun and he is very caring and respectful. As long as you do all of the assignments given, you'll get an A in the class.

analysis.name: Amit Einav

By Tech's standards, I was BEASTING that class. I was consistently above the average on all tests and quizzes.I got a D.I'm retaking Calc 1. :(
Awesome professor.  If you attend class, the tests are really easy.

Take any other professor if you don't want to risk getting a B or prepare to suck up to her like no other.

very caring professor if you participate. some parts of the class seem a bit out of scope for a freshman english class, but theyre pretty fulfilling to complete. its a lot of work at the start of the year and gets lighter until the end of the year.  
if you go to office hours for major assignments youll get a lot of good feedback
The grades she gives out are lower than most other English 1101 professors. She is also very passive agressive and patronizing

analysis.name: Ellery Ingall
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Three exams and a final. Only 3 of 4 count towards the grade so the final is optional.  The best way to study for exams is practice tests and reviewing the lecture notes and slides. If you do that you will get an A in this class.

Ingall is a good option for EAS2600. Grade is 75% tests (lowest test is dropped) and 25% lab. You don't need the lectures to pass tests because they're given online and open note. Lectures themselves are interesting if you do decide to go to them, but you don't need them. Labs are easy and straightforward, you only need an hour to do them.

Grades entirely based on exams and lab work. Lab work is pretty fun, easy most of the time. Content itself is on the more interesting side imo. Don't have to attend lecture, reading the slides is enough. Exams are online and unproctored. Read the slides and do practice exams and the exams shouldn't be too difficult. Get to drop lowest exam score

Thermo with Ingall is pretty easy. He is SUPER nice and knowledgeable. Sometimes lectures were hard to follow or homework was quirky, but he is very accessible outside of class and the grading is lenient. (He will zoom if you need help!) The material covered is basic, but it touches all the bases. Highly recommend attending class and participating.

Dr. Ingall is a great professor! He makes thermo concepts easy to grasp. Lectures aren't mandatory, but I would recommend going because there are helpful worksheets in every class. Homework can be hard, but office hours are very helpful, Dr. Ingall is always available. Also, he is so kind and rounded me up to an A because of my effort he noticed.

analysis.name: Liz Hutter

She is super nice and helps with whatever you need. Grading seemed to be really tough though. It is an easy B but the people who got an A really had to work for it. Also there are no tests or quizzes just a lot of busy work and some big projects at the end.

analysis.name: Elisa Dainese
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: Will 100% recommend. Took the class over the summer. Lectures are very interesting. There is reading, but it's manageable. She gives amazing feedback and is very approachable.

Made everyone cram and then questions why we hadn't finished earlier. She posts lectures though; makes her class easy but boring and way too much work

Professor Elisa is so kind! She is very good with disability accommodations and is incredibly patient. She gives very interesting lectures and records them in case people are sick. The course work is reading-heavy (reports based on 10-20 page articles) but there's lots of time to get it done. She also gave us grace periods for every assignment.
Very reasonable workload. Most papers graded by TA's who are available to contact prior to paper submission. Group projects and papers are entirety of grade.

analysis.name: Elliot Moore

review_highlights.comment: Most people would say the material for this class is pretty hard, but Dr. Moore makes sure you know exactly what you need to do in order to succeed in the class. Dr. Moore picked up this class from another professor and taught it very well - he clearly has tons of experience in ML. Homeworks could take a long time and were tedious, but lecture slides helped a lot. Exams were take-home/open-note and mostly conceptual.

Really good lecturer, the class is super hard since it is considered a weed out for electrical engineers. Homeworks are super hard but the tests are around the same level so doing good on homeworks means doing good on tests. Test 3 is really hard regardless. Supposedly the fall professors are better. Go to all lectures and recitation.

Worst grading scheme I've ever seen. Only 2 exams, 25% each, and a 30% final. Exams graded in canvas separate from written work. If you get a final answer wrong, the max credit you can get back for your work is 50%. That is what killed my grade in this course. On our 2nd exam, the range of scores was from 0 to 60 out of 60, with an average of 30.

Always an entertaining professor even when the material is a bit dry. The class as a whole is very difficult, but it's made bearable by the professors who teach it. Dr. Moore knows what he is talking about and is more than ready to share it with students who have questions. Enthusiastic, funny, knowledgeable. 10/10 would take again!

analysis.name: Eliza Markley

All writings are graded very lightly.

Lazy professor that does not take any pride in instructing this class. Only picked this class because it was online asynchronous and honestly it is not worth it. Take Psych for your ethics requirement guys

The course itself is the issue: dense textbook, six heavy quizzes worth 60%, no extra credit. Unless you love ethics, do not take. TA's were great though, go to office hours.

Gives you a 0 before due process which is ironic for an ethics class. 6 quizzes and 3 long papers. Few lectures that are pre-recorded years before, badly organized, you pretty much read and teach yourself everything.

Don't take this class if you care about your mental well-being. It will eat up all your time. Lectures are prerecorded and unhelpful. You will be reading the textbook for hours a week. analysis.name: Ellen Zerbe

All of her expectations with assignments are clearly laid out in rubrics and you have opportunities to resubmit work if you really mess it up. Overall great prof!

she's a really good professor but she grades REALLY harshly. when they say you can't miss anything from the rubric your REALLY cannot miss anything from the rubric. make sure your group has the same work all around consistently and always tell your group mates when you change something because it WILL affect their grade.

The professor is chill and passionate about what she teaches. The class is fine, but be careful of due dates since they don't post those on Canvas. You're responsible for submitting the assignments on time, but figuring out when is confusing.

I had Dr. Zerbe for BMED1000 and really appreciated her engagement and enthusiasm in the class. She genuinely seemed to want us to succeed in the course and beyond and has made me more excited for what my future in BME could hold.

Made it clear how each unit was supposed to contribute to something broader. Some of the assignments felt redundant but none of them were hard. If you get a good group (they're randomly assigned at the beginning) then it's light

analysis.name: Emiliano Gutierrez-Popoca

review_highlights.comment: I would recommend Professor Gutierrez for 1102! This class was focused on Shakespeare, and while I am not a huge Shakespeare fan, the class was interesting and not hard! No exams or essays; rather, you work either independently or in group projects. He is very accessible, and he loves when people participate in class. Overall, a very chill class!!

awk lil guy most times. put in SOME form of effort and you'll end w an A. dont like how useless going to his classes felt w presentations every session about how to do work when we've been in school for quite awhile now... didnt LOVE the topic but also not the worst ever. dont take the 5-6:15 time you will never want to go. would retake!

Class is very easy with a light workload. However, I would take another section of 1102 if available. The topic is Shakespeare which got very boring and the assignments were super repetitive. But if you are just looking to get the credit this course is by no means bad. Its just that there are better/more fun options with other professors.

while his lectures got a little boring from time to time, you can tell he's really passionate about his discipline. he is an extremely nice man, and before breaks would bring little treats for the class and wish us all happy holidays. he's a very easy grader but will also provide useful feedback on projects. he's very approachable as well.

Dr. Emiliano is a great professor, very sweet and enjoys what he teaches. The class isn't difficult, but the lectures were pretty boring. The workload is extremely manageable and there were plenty of group projects throughout his course.

analysis.name: Emma Hu
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: We didn't learn that much in MSE 3025 but I don't think that's really her fault. I think she was a fine lecturer but the content was just pretty simple and I think she was aware of that bc she didn't really care if we paid attention or not and would end lectures early/cancel class more than most to not waste our time

Lectures are extremely dull, covering what feels like 20 mins of content in 75, but tests are open notes and the content is extremely straightforward. Print the notes and take them to exams and you'll do well. Very little programming in this numerical methods class, except for one (very simple) project.

Class is based on participation, 2 tests, and a final. Participation is a bucket point system, and any extra points are extra credit. Tests are very similar to the practice tests she gives to help study. She gave very good lectures that taught what you needed to know. only complaint is that I wish she used piazza, ed discussion, etc.

She had really good lectures often complemented with long textbook sections (optional). Her study guides did not do a great job of covering exam material, though. I also wish she was more accessible outside of lecture; it's tough reaching her, and there was no forum where students could ask questions. Not a bad professor all in all.

Dr. Hu is a great teacher! She is very kind and she truly cares about each student getting a good grade. She always has office hours and reviews exam questions during them. The class is based off of homework memorization.

analysis.name: Emily Sanders
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She is the best ME 2016 professor by far. While homeworks may take a little bit, office hours help a ton, and her homeworks are much more doable than other professors. Her lectures really help with the homework as well. Her tests are extremely fair and straight forward. Probably one of my easier classes this semester.

Dr. Sanders is very knowledgeable and super accessible for help. Homework can be hard, but she's ready to help if you're willing to work earnestly. Homework every week (Matlab coding) and written exams ( straight from lectures). I would take her again!

Sanders is the best option for 2016. Her lecture notes are very clear and you can probably get away with just that and the textbook, but I'd recommend going to class. Her lectures were directly related to the hw and exams (which had no matlab btw), which other 2016 profs had a problem with.

Lecture material is all there but the HW was sometimes very confusing and took minimum 6 hours weekly. Exams were fair and the practice exams helped a lot. Course itself is boring so can't blame the prof on that. 2 midterms 1 final and 10 HWs.

analysis.name: Stanislav Emelianov
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Stas is a very entertaining and enthusiastic lecturer. He has a harsh style of lecturing and even harsher tests. However, he truly does care about the class and does want to see everyone succeed in their own ways.

I can't recommend him enough. He's explains complicated concepts very well holds engaging lectures. He's VERY flexible with due dates and is very down-to-earth with what he expects from students. Exams are very reasonable and can easily be studied for by reviewing HWs and previous exams.

Awesome professor, he knows the concepts and cares about students. One time when I didn't submit a homework assignment, he emailed me to check that everything was alright. He has a great brand of humor and makes concepts interesting and intuitive. Tests are average difficulty, as it homework. He has great availability for office hours.

Best professor I've had at Tech so far. Extremely effective lectures and is very accessible outside of class. Class is set up so that you don't have to stress about grades. Assignments and exams are very reasonable. Provides A LOT of resources.

analysis.name: Alex Endert
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Endert is a great lecturer and very caring professor. Topics were relevant and I learned a lot, even though I usually don't pay attention in "memorization-based" classes. That being said, the beginning is a little boring but it gets more interesting later, and the final project can be fun if you have a good group. Exams and HWs are easy.

Good choice for an easy elective. Endert is a good lecturer and is engaging to listen to. He is also in general a friendly guy and makes himself pretty accessible. Homework assignments were very straightforward, and so were the exams if you just attended/watched the lectures. The bulk of the class is the group project, so just pick good teammates.

Professor Endert doesn't really teach in this class, instead every class is led by a difficult student group who lead a presentation on an assigned paper and the class discusses. Class ended early every time but the discussions and topics were interesting. The assignments were graded easily and not very time consuming.

Lectures are recorded so attendance isn't required. Unfortunately the lecture content is very boring, but not difficult. There are also coding labs that progressively get harder in Javascript D3, and you need to learn it yourself since lectures don't cover it.

This course is structured with one paper each class, all culminating in a group project. The assignments were moderately time consuming but interesting and ultimately easier than other classes.

He is a great lecturer and has great command over the topics, and the class interactions were quite interesting.

analysis.name: Emily Weigel
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 46 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Out of the 3 biology professors that taught BIOL1510 for fall 2016 (Choi, Kerr & Weigel), her test was the most straight forward. Like her test was my first A, my first decent test score. Her lectures are pretty cool too. I feel like they probably planned this on purpose to give us hope that we might have a chance in the class or something.

Dr. Weigel taught the latter half of general ecology which honestly saved my grade from the first professor. Her lectures and expectations are incredibly clear and comprehensible. She is an overall friendly and approachable, as well as knowledgeable, professor who cares a lot about student progress and feedback. 10/10 would recommend.

Dr. Weigel is a very caring and nice professor...but her style of teaching is somewhat vague and you need to know how to code (use R) for the final project even though she rarely teaches it and provides the prompts for assignments. Her test questions are also vague and the TAs are harsh graders. However, the grading scheme is fair.

She was very kind even though the content was a little boring. The grading criteria was very helpful - there's two schemes that maximize your grade! Each test had 2 parts with one being multiple choice and the other part being a "take-home" test that you can work on with a group. The final project was a lot of work so be sure to have a good group.

I took this course in the Fall of 2021. Professor Weigel is passionate about what she teaches. The coursework is not demanding, but does include a lab, which is where most of the work for this class will be done. If you find Biology boring, this will not be a fun class, but it will be easy. If you like it, you will love this class with Weigel

analysis.name: Enlu Zhou
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: By far the most frustrating professor I've had. Doesn't respond to piazza posts or emails (only when convenient), 2 quizzes worth 40% of your grade with extremely minimal prep, homeworks sometimes skipping lectures ahead. When I asked what I could do to improve my grade, I was told that she was not God from her directly. Do not take her class.

The structure of this class has it to where two quizzes taken during the beginning of the course have a LARGE impact on your grade but really they are both tests. She is also not receptive if you don't form a quick understanding of topics in the course and is very hard on regrades even if there are actual mistakes in the grading.

2 quizzes each worth 20%, 1 is a review of 2027. 2 projects each worth 20% with 2 hours to complete them. She's rude when you ask questions and moves to fast when going over simio. Half of her HWs have nothing to do with what we learned in class. Always finding myself using previous notes to do her HW. Not a "hard" class but she's unbearable.

Probably the worst professor at Tech. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS. She will spring surprise assignments on you due dead week, if you ask her for help she'll tell you about her straight A college career, and she reads off of he other professor's slides. She has no idea what she's doing. 10/10 would not take her class again.

The previous ratings don't apply anymore, she completely changed the course syllabus. She has two "quizzes" which are 20% each and covers maybe half the material in the class. The midterm and final project are really difficult and are not a good representation of the material taught. Teaching is ok but it is hard to follow the presentations.

analysis.name: Mimi Ensley
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Ensley is by far the best English professor I've ever had. Initially, the course topic ("What is English?") seemed boring, but the readings and projects she assigned made it a lot more interesting. While her grading is strict to the rubric, she gives great feedback and is flexible (especially during COVID). Great choice for ENGL overall!

Very fun class. Most of the readings were interesting. Lots of class discussion. The grade is primarily in a few projects, which are graded generously. I asked for time extensions on nearly all of the projects, and Dr. Ensley was always happy to give them, even though I didn't give much of a reason (basically I had quizzes in other classes).

Dr. Ensley was a blast of a professor. One of the single nicest professors I've ever met. The class involved a lot of reading different books and passages as well as discussions about them, but Dr. Ensley made sure that engagement was interesting and worthwhile. Fully recommend for any class you have to take with her!

Dr. Ensley is super sweet and caring, especially during COVID. She cares a lot about the class material, although I did not find it to be that interesting. She grades fairly and gives a lot of feedback, although some of the homeworks and assignments feel unnecessary and like a waste of time. Decent choice as a prof

Take her! She's a wonderful prof and was extremely considerate that I took her class from a totally different timezone (12 hrs ahead). Gave extensions as needed. Very clear with feedback and helped me with non-class writing for a personal project. Great person, wish I could have taken the class in-person with her.

analysis.name: Martin Engman
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I found him really difficult to understand so lectures weren't helpful, and I relied on the book.  He has very few things he grades on (6 hws and 3 test + final) and there is absolutely no curve on anything.  He gives a recommended hw list  and you should absolutely do it.  Tests are pretty straight forward but some discontinuity in grading.

Test are reasonable but if you make a few small mistakes, it can easily drop your grade. He is against curving the class and has a set grading scale. If you make  below an 80 on 1 test, it is very difficult to bring it up to an A. It is easy to learn from the book and in recitation. He has really bad handwriting and is difficult to understand.

A cool guy, helpful during office hours and obviously very smart, but the grading is harsh. He expects you to memorize everything but only tests a few things, so I always felt like I was wasting my study time. A lot of the homework is optional, but if you don't do at least most of it your grade will suffer.

Mumbles a lot and talks into the board during lecture as he writes on the chalkboard. Tests seemed fair enough, but he does not curve and calculates your grade by just adding everything so its out of 500 or something. Homework was 3 mymathlab assignments and 3 written ones from textbook (not sure why we even had to use mymathlab with 3 homeworks).

Marty is so boring and hard to understand (he mumbles a lot and sounds like he smokes a pack a day). His handwriting is terrible, and if you are confused and try to ask questions, he is not helpful. By the end of the semester his lectures were almost empty. The only way I learned was by teaching myself or at recitation. DO NOT take him.

analysis.name: Randy Engle
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: While he was pretty nice as a person, his class was unnecessarily hard (fill in the blank TESTS & quizzes). You should attend class b.c he drops your lowest test grade, but I missed out on that. Do the extra credit, or you're SOL. I got an A, & he went over things you really should know in gen psych, but don't take this if you don't have to.

While he is not a bad teacher, I would say his class just isn't worth the difficulty level. His tests do not test critical thinking but instead require you to remember random vocabulary words that could have appeared only once before. I do not feel that his assessment style is fair to students, and he doesn't grade on a curve.

awesome lectures. very good instructor. supposed to be the hardest section of psych 1101, but the class is very interesting and by the end of the semester he knows everyone's name which is really awesome (you dont see this a lot at tech). great teacher overall. i would reccommend to any psych major.

Supposedly the hardest section for Psych 1101 but he did a great job in not making the lectures dull as hell, which they shouldn't be but somehow other teachers can make them that way. The quizzes are sometimes very detailed and tricky though.
Great teacher, interesting lectures, but weekly quizzes mean you must keep up with the reading or you are screwed.

analysis.name: Enid Steinbart
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Worst Professor I've had at Tech.

Ok so she is a really nice person, but her class is tough. I lost a lot of points because she had weekly quizzes which were worth 25% of the grade in the end. I would say make sure to give you all from the beginning because she doesn't curve or give any extra credit. Other proffs had huge curves with similar grades, so I wish I had someone else.

She teaches well. We had tech issues for a bit but its good now. She is by far the best multi option. PROFESSORS MATTER FOR MULTI (things arent standardized). Her tests were pretty straightforward and quizzes exactly like homework (but no partial credit on quizzes due to MML). *note this was a COVID class so tests/quizzes may be different format

Lectures are long but worth going to, just be ready for lots of proofs that you won't be expected to know. She works lots of examples that are similar to what you'll see on a test. She's very approachable and wants to help her students. Tests are manageable. Only get 3 tries on MyMathLab homework questions.

She flew through the material. Explained concepts clearly but did very few example problem. Seemed bothered when students asked questions in class. If you can learn from a book this prof. is for you. You better have a good TA thats all I have to say.

analysis.name: Jacob Erickson
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I've truly tried to give this professor the benefit of the doubt. I've gone to tutoring, used all my resources, but he teaches as if we're already at his level and tests us on things he barely covers or explains in class. The midterm averages have been failing, yet he refuses to curve despite this. I'm sorry, but not curving a 46 average is INSANE

He doesn't know how to teach. Lectures only made things more confusing, so everyone resorted to watching Lehmann's lectures online and teaching themselves multi. Still, he wrote stupid exams where every average was failing (3rd was a 46), and refused to curve the exams or the class. Even with full HW and Quiz credit, I barely scraped by with a B.

Useless lectures, everyone stopped showing up after the first 2 weeks when they realized its impossible to keep up with him and his lack of structure when you could watch Lehmann's lectures. Lowest averages and hardest exams, had to grind out of getting a C after being 10-20 points above the mean on exams and having full HW/quiz credit. DONT TAKE

Do not take this class. Lectures are incredibly confusing, and going to class did not help at all. The midterms are very difficult and test on things that were barely taught. The averages on the midterms are very low, but when asked to curve, he says no. Worst professor I've had by far.

Exams were hard, and the content was challenging, but realistically, if you paid attention in class and followed his examples, you would be prepared for the exams. Finals were an easy way to improve your grade in class. The professor got much better at explaining the content by the end of the semester.
